**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 1:**

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ (Ar-Rum). We have previously spoken at length about the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) at the beginnings of the surahs, and I do not wish to repeat what I have said. But I want the scholars to turn their attention to this matter with an illuminating glance that shows us all and reveals to us the wisdom and secrets in these letters.

We said: these letters (Alif Lam Mim) are constructed on pausing (al-waqf), each letter on its own, although the Qur'an as a whole is constructed on continuity (al-wasl) in its verses and in its surahs. The last letter of a surah is joined to the first letter of the one that follows it. Here we say: (...and indeed Allah is with the doers of good. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful...).

Even more striking than this, we find that the end of Surah An-Nas is joined to the beginning of Al-Fatihah, so we say: (...from the jinn and mankind. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds).

The Qur'an, then, is continuous, with no break in it. So why were the disjointed letters at the beginnings of the surahs constructed on pausing? Why do we not say: "Alif Lam Mim"? They said: because Allah, exalted is He, did not wish to make them a single word, so they came separated. And the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) comforts us: "I do not say Alif Lam Mim is one letter, but Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter." (1) So we want, and we await, one whom Allah causes to attain it, to be among the doers of good, and to guide us to the secret in these letters at which one should pause and which should not be joined to anything else.

1 Narrated by at-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2910) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith from this route." It was also narrated by at-Tabarani in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/76) from the hadith of Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/163): "In its chain is Musa ibn Ubayd al-Rabadhi, who is weak."

Al-Sha'rawi said, may Allah have mercy on him: The Most High said:

The word ﴿Ghulibat...﴾ (ar-Rum: 2) indicates the existence of a battle in which one party was defeated and another party was defeated, so the one defeated here was the Romans. They were People of the Book, and their dwelling was in al-Sham and the Iraq of the Arabs. Of Iraq, one part lies on the side of the Arabs and one part on the side of Persia. The Romans are attributed to Rum, son of Esau, son of Isaac (Is'haq), son of Abraham.

1 The occasion of revelation of the verses: Kisra sent an army against the Romans and appointed over them a man called Shahrayran. He marched against the Romans with the people of Persia and prevailed over them. He killed them, destroyed their cities and cut down their olive trees. Qaysar had sent a man called Yahnas, and he met Shahrayran at Adhri'at and Busra, which are the nearest parts of al-Sham to the land of the Arabs. Persia defeated the Romans. The news reached the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions in Makkah, and it grieved them. The Prophet (ﷺ) disliked that the unlettered people of the Magians should prevail over the People of the Book, the Romans. The disbelievers of Makkah rejoiced and taunted, and they met the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "You are People of the Book and the Christians are People of the Book, and we are unlettered. Our brothers of the people of Persia have prevailed over your brothers the Romans, and if you fight us, we will surely prevail over you." So Allah, the Most High, revealed: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years...﴾ (ar-Rum: 1-4), to the end of the verses.

2 Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/424): "The Romans are from the lineage of al-Ays ibn Is'haq ibn Ibrahim, and they are cousins of the Children of Israel. They are called the Banu al-Asfar. They were upon the religion of the Greeks, and the Greeks are from the lineage of Yafith ibn Nuh, cousins of the Turks. They used to worship the seven wandering planets, which are called al-Mutahayyirah, and they would pray toward the North Pole. They are the ones who founded Damascus and built its temple, in which there are mihrabs facing the north. The Romans remained upon their religion until about three hundred years after the mission of the Messiah."

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 3:**

His saying, ﴿in the nearest land﴾ (Ar-Rum), means: nearest to the land of the Arabs, as in ﴿when you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side﴾ (Al-Anfal). So "al-'Udwa al-Dunya" means the near one, close to Madinah, and "al-Quswa" means the far one, distant from it. Thus the meaning of ﴿in the nearest land﴾ (Ar-Rum) is: the land closest to the Arabian Peninsula.

In His saying, glorified is He, ﴿and after their defeat, they will overcome﴾ (Ar-Rum), there is good news for the Muslims. The Persians were a people who worshipped fire, whereas the Romans were People of the Book. So the disagreement between us and the Persians is at the summit of divinity (al-qimma al-ilahiyya), while the disagreement between us and the Romans is at the summit of prophethood (al-qimma al-risaliyya). Thus they are closer to us, because they believe in our God, even though they do not believe in our Messenger.

This is one of the greatness of Islam: the one who believes in God is closer to our souls than the one who does not believe in God, because he is at least connected to the heavens. Therefore, when the Romans were defeated, the disbelievers of Quraysh rejoiced and the believers grieved. The disbelievers of Quraysh rejoiced because the defeat of the Romans was evidence that Muhammad and his companions would be defeated just as their companions had been.

The word ﴿their defeat﴾ (Ar-Rum) is a verbal noun (masdar) which is sometimes added to the agent and sometimes added to the object. You say: "I was pleased by the striking of the prince the wrongdoer," where you added the verbal noun to the agent. And you say: "I was pleased by the striking of the wrongdoer," where you added the verbal noun to the object. Likewise here, ﴿their defeat﴾ (Ar-Rum) is a verbal noun added to the object.

But why did He, glorified is He, say ﴿they will overcome﴾ (Ar-Rum) with the sin, which indicates the future, and then say after it ﴿within a few years﴾ (Ar-Rum), which also indicates the future? They said: because victory does not come suddenly; rather, it requires long preparation, taking the causes of victory, and equipping the strength necessary for it. So it is as if during the period of a few years they are preparing for victory, and whenever they prepare a provision, they take a portion of victory. Victory, then, does not come within a few years; rather, it comes from continuous work over the span of a few years.

For example, Hitler, when he was defeated in the World War, and all the countries united against him, came in the year 1939 and threatened the whole world with war. Did the strength with which he threatened fall upon him suddenly? No, rather he continued for several years preparing the provisions, equipping the army, the weapons and the routes, until the strength with which he threatened became available to him.

The excitement of the disbelievers stirred the indignation of the believers, until there was revealed: ﴿They, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after.﴾ (Ar-Rum) The believers rejoiced, until Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, Allah will not gladden these people, and the Romans will defeat Persia within three years."

For the word "bid'" (a few; a small number) means from three to ten, so as-Siddiq took it in its lowest meaning. Why? Because as-Siddiq, and the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, would not burden the believers with the hardship of patience for a period of nine years. This is among the sincerity (siddiqiyyah) that distinguished Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

Therefore Abu Bakr said to Ubayy ibn Khalaf: "By Allah, Allah will not cool your eyes," meaning: by what you rejoiced in of the victory of the disbelievers, "and Allah has informed us of it within a period of a few years." Ubayy said: "Will you bet with me?" He said: "I will bet you on such-and-such number of qalus (camels) — the qalus is the she-camel that is ridden — that in three years, if the Romans win, you give me ten qalus, and I will give you the same if Persia wins."

When Abu Bakr went to the Messenger of Allah and told him what had happened, he said: "O Abu Bakr, increase the stake and extend the term" — meaning, increase the number of camels from ten to a hundred, and extend the period from three years to nine. Indeed, as-Siddiq went to Ubayy and presented the matter to him, and he agreed to the wager of a hundred camels.(1)

When the harm from the polytheists intensified, and as-Siddiq went out as an emigrant (2), Ubayy ibn Khalaf saw him and said: "Where to, O Abu Faysal?" They used to mock as-Siddiq with this expression, instead of saying "O Abu Bakr." The bakr is the strong camel, and they would say "O Abu Faysal," and the fayszal is the young camel. As-Siddiq said: "An emigrant." He said: "And what of the wager between us?" He said: "If he (my son) guarantees it for me, my son Abd al-Rahman." Then, when the Battle of Badr came, Abd al-Rahman saw Ubayy and said to him: "Where to?" He said: "To Badr." He said: "And what of the wager if you are killed?" He said: "My son will give it to you."

At Badr (3), Ubayy was struck by a wound from the Messenger of Allah, of which he died, and his son brought the wager (al-Ju'l) to Abd al-Rahman. They took it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: "Give it in charity." (4)

Here is a pause of miraculous faith and creed: We have previously spoken about the unseen (al-ghayb) and the witnessed (al-mashhad). We said: the unseen has kinds: an unseen to which there are preliminaries that lead to it, as when you give a student a geometry exercise, and like the cosmic secrets that scientists arrive at and discover from the data of the universe, like the one who discovered the steam engine, and Archimedes when he discovered the law of floating bodies, etc. These people are not said to have known the unseen; rather, they took existing premises and deduced from them what did not exist.

As for the absolute unseen, it is that which has no preliminaries leading to it; it is unseen to all people, and of it the Exalted says: ﴿Knower of the unseen, He does not reveal His unseen to anyone, except to whom He has approved of the messengers...﴾ (Al-Jinn)

Among the unseen is that which is hidden from you but not hidden from others, like a thing stolen from you: it is unseen to you because you do not know its place, but it is not unseen to the one who stole it from you.

The human's affliction is that he does not use the premises to investigate the secrets of the universe so that he may advance in cosmic knowledge; rather he uses them to know the unseen of others. We say to him: If you want to know the unseen of others, then permit them to know your unseen, and I believe no one would be content with that.

So: concealing the unseen from creation is a great blessing of Allah the Exalted, for He, glorified is He, is the Lord of all people, and He wills that His creatures benefit from one another. Do you not see that if you know of a person one single fault, it makes you lose interest in all his good deeds, and makes you hate him and hate every good deed of his? So Allah conceals from you the unseen of others so that you may benefit from their good deeds.

The unseen has been withheld from us by Allah, either by the veil of past time, or future time, or by the veil of place. You do not know the events of the past before you were born until someone you trust comes and tells you what happened in the past. Likewise, you do not know what will happen in the future. As for the barrier of place, you do not know what exists in a place other than your own, and a thing may be in your place yet be in a hidden spot so you do not perceive it.

Among that is His saying the Exalted: ﴿And they say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"...﴾ (Al-Mujadila)

So who informed the Messenger of Allah of what was in their souls? Allah tore for him the veil of place and informed him of what was going on in the people's souls, and the Messenger of Allah informed them of it. Was this not sufficient for them to believe in Allah who brings out what is hidden in their breasts? So: the matter for them is one of stubbornness and denial.

Likewise what happened to the Messenger of Allah at the Battle of Mu'tah (5), which took place in the land of Jordan while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in Medina. We know that the people of the biography (ahl al-sirah) only apply the term "ghazwa" (expedition the Prophet personally attended) to those the Messenger of Allah attended, and every military engagement he did not attend we call a "sariyyah" (detachment), except Mu'tah, which alone bears this designation. Why, although the Messenger of Allah did not witness it?

They said: Rather, the Messenger of Allah witnessed it while he was in Medina, by means of what Allah revealed to him of the veil of place, and He showed him what was happening there, so that he would inform his companions of what was happening in the battle as if he were seeing it, saying: "The banner was taken by so-and-so and he was killed, then it was taken by so-and-so and he was killed." When the news came to them, they found the matter as our master the Messenger of Allah had reported. (6)

Just as the veil of the past was torn for him, and he informed of events among the earlier nations, as in His saying the Exalted: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed the command to Moses...﴾ (Al-Qasas), ﴿Nor were you a dweller among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses...﴾ (Al-Qasas).

And just as the veil of the future was torn for him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as in this verse we are discussing: ﴿They, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years...﴾ (Ar-Rum). Show me what power (a computer) in the world can inform us of the outcome of a battle that will happen after three to nine years!

So Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the unlettered Prophet residing in the Arabian Peninsula, who knows nothing of the strength of the Romans or the strength of the Persians, informs us of this outcome. For the one who knows things as they will be is the One who informed him. And that Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, declares it and challenges with it in a Qur'an recited until the Day of Resurrection, is evidence of his confirmation by Allah's speech to him, and that he is certain of the occurrence of what he reported.

And for this certainty as-Siddiq was named "al-Siddiq." When they told him the saying of the Messenger of Allah about the Isra', he said only: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." (7)

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, reports this outcome, lays the wager on it with the polytheists, and holds fast to it; and that is only because of his confidence in the truth of this message, and that it can never fail.

As for the Exalted's saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the command, before and after...﴾ (Ar-Rum), it means: beware lest you understand that the victory of Persia over Rome, or the victory of Rome over Persia, is outside the intentions of Allah. To Allah belongs the command before the defeat, and to Allah belongs the command after the defeat.

So when Rome was defeated, to Allah belongs the command; and when Persia was victorious, to Allah belongs the command; because the Truth, glorified is He, stirs the people of good by allowing the people of evil to prevail, awakens their zeal, rouses their feelings through their enemies, and alerts them that the enemies should not be better than they are.

So: the victory of what is disliked over what is loved, by Allah, comes at a time determined by Allah. Therefore beware of grieving when you find an enemy, for the fool is the one who grieves over that, while the wise is the one who sees his enemy's favor upon him: the enemy reminds me always to be strong and prepared, reminds me to be upright so that my enemy finds no opportunity or flaw in me. The enemy makes you devote all your capacities to goodness so that you become better than him. Therefore the poet says:

My enemies have a favor upon me, and a grace,
so I owe them thanks for their benefit to me.
They are to me like medicine, and healing is in its bitterness.
May the Most Merciful never remove my enemies from me:
they searched for my slip and I avoided it,
they competed with me and I acquired excellence.

So: to Allah belongs the command before and after, and He has wisdom in letting falsehood prevail. Do you not see the Battle of Uhud, and how the Muslims were defeated when they disobeyed the command of the Messenger of Allah and left their positions out of greed for booty; they were routed at the outset, though the Messenger of Allah was with them. For the Sunnah of Allah in His creation requires defeat when we oppose the command of the Messenger of Allah. And how would it be if the Muslims had won despite their disobedience to the command of their Messenger? If they had won, the authority of the Messenger's command would have lost its credibility, and they would never obey him in any command thereafter.

And on the day of Hunayn: ﴿And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you...﴾ (At-Tawbah), to the point that Abu Bakr himself said: "We will not be defeated today for lack of numbers." (8) When they looked to their strength and forgot the support of Allah, they were defeated at the outset; then Allah showed compassion to them, His mercy reached them, and He gave them victory in the end.

So: to Allah belongs the command before and after. Beware of thinking that the victory of falsehood came against the will of Allah or outside His intention; rather, Allah willed it and intended it for a wisdom.

(1) Narrated by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi from Qatadah, and its wording: that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions, headed by Abu Bakr: "Were you not worthy to set a term less than ten? For the bid' is what is between three and ten." So they increased the stakes and extended the term for them, and Allah caused the Romans to prevail over Persia at the end of seven years from their first wager. (Cited by al-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur 6/482).
(2) Abu Bakr al-Siddiq often asked the Messenger of Allah for permission to emigrate, and the Messenger of Allah would say to him: "Do not hasten; perhaps Allah will provide you a companion," so Abu Bakr hoped to be that companion. Related by Ibn Hisham in as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah (2/480). This was regarding emigration to Medina, but it is established in as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah (1/372) that when Mecca became constricted for Abu Bakr and he suffered harm there, he asked the Messenger of Allah for permission to emigrate and was granted it, so Abu Bakr set out as an emigrant, until when he had traveled a day or two from Mecca, Ibn ad-Dughunnah met him, who was then the chief of the Ahabish, and Ibn ad-Dughunnah said: "Where to, O Abu Bakr?" He said: "My people have expelled me, harmed me, and constricted me." Then he took him into his protection, and Abu Bakr returned to Mecca.
(3) Ubayy ibn Khalaf was killed at the Battle of Uhud, not at the Battle of Badr; he was struck by the hand of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace (related by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il an-Nubuwwah (3/212)). As for the one killed at the Battle of Badr, it was Umayyah ibn Khalaf, slain by Bilal (as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham 2/632).
(4) The giving of the wager in charity after the Messenger of Allah came, mentioned by al-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur (6/480), attributed to Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh from al-Bara' ibn Azib, that Abu Bakr was the one who brought it to the Messenger of Allah, and he said: "This is forbidden gain; give it in charity." There is no mention in it of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr. And Allah knows best.
(5) It took place in Jumada al-Ula of the year eight. Its cause was that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent al-Harith ibn Umayr al-Azdi, of the Banu Lahb, with his letter to Syria, to the king of the Romans or the governor of Busra. Shurahbil ibn Amr al-Ghassani intercepted him, bound him, brought him forward and struck off his neck. No messenger of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had been killed besides him, so this was severe for him when the news reached him; he dispatched a force and appointed over it Zayd ibn Harithah. (Zad al-Ma'ad of Ibn al-Qayyim 2/155).
(6) From Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, announced the deaths of Zayd, Ja'far and Ibn Rawahah to the people before their news came to them, saying: "Zayd took the banner and was struck; then Ja'far took it and was struck; then Ibn Rawahah took it and was struck" — and his eyes were shedding tears — "until the banner was taken by a sword from the swords of Allah, and Allah granted them victory." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4262).
(7) Related by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il an-Nubuwwah (2/361), and likewise al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (3/62-63) from the hadith of A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and he said: "Sound in its chain, though they did not record it."
(8) Related by al-Bayhaqi in ad-Dala'il (5/123) from al-Rabi' ibn Anas that a man said on the day of Hunayn: "We will not be defeated for lack of numbers," and they were twelve thousand, so that grieved the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Allah revealed: ﴿And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you...﴾ (At-Tawbah). Also cited by al-Suyuti in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 138).

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God...﴾ (Al-Rum). That is, the victory in which the believers will rejoice: would they rejoice at the Romans' triumph over the Persians? They said: Rather, the joy here consists of interlocking and rising circles. First, they rejoice at the victory of a people of religion and of scripture over disbelievers and atheists; they rejoice that the glad tidings of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) have been fulfilled; and they rejoice because they believed in the Messenger of God and affirmed him before he uttered these glad tidings.

They rejoice because they have attained the truth. Whenever a verse came, each of them rejoiced for himself, because he had been right when he believed in the One God, who knows matters in accordance with what will be, and followed His Messenger (ﷺ). Thus this joy is not limited to one thing; rather, it extends to many overlapping matters.

Moreover, the day on which the Romans were victorious coincided with the day on which the Muslims were victorious at Badr (1).

As for His, the Exalted's, saying ﴿He gives victory to whom He wills...﴾ (Al-Rum): it is the Persians or the Romans, since the command belongs to Him before and after. ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ (Al-Rum). The Real, glorified is He, described Himself with these two attributes: the Mighty and the Merciful. Although the Mighty is the one who overcomes and is not overcome, so His dominance, glorified is He, is exalted in this attribute, He nevertheless followed it with the attribute of mercy, so that there arises in the heart of the believer this balance between the attributes of subjugation and dominance and the attribute of mercy.

Likewise, we understand from the attribute of might here that nothing happens except by His, the Exalted's, will. So when one party is victorious and another party is defeated, even if falsehood is victorious, that happens only by His will; for God, the Exalted, does not leave falsehood standing nor exalt disbelief except to make the truth manifest. So when people are oppressed by falsehood and suffer through thought, they turn to faith and hold fast to it.

And read His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of God is the highest...﴾ (Al-Tawbah). He did not say "and He made the word of God the highest," because it is not a making, since making (ja'l) is the transformation of one thing into another; rather, the word of God is highest from the beginning and always, even if the word of falsehood rises for a time.

1 On the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: When the Day of Badr came, the Romans prevailed over Persia, which pleased the believers, so there was revealed ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated...﴾ (Al-Rum) up to His saying ﴿On that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God...﴾ (Al-Rum). He said: So the believers rejoiced at the Romans' victory over Persia. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (3192), and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 6:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) Exalted One says:

﴿The promise of Allah. Allah does not fail His promise, but most of the people do not know.﴾

Al-wa'd (promise) is the announcement of something pleasing before it happens. ﴿Allah does not fail His promise...﴾ (al-Rum). There is a difference between the promise of Allah and the promise of people, because you may promise a person some good, and then circumstances come between you and carrying out what you promised: your opinion may change, your capabilities may weaken, or the reason for which you were going to act may change.

So: you do not possess the elements of fulfilment and its causes. As for the promise of the Truthful, Exalted is He, it is a certain promise, since no power exists that can take it away from what He has promised. He, glory be to Him, is not incapacitated by anything in the earth or in the heavens. So, as long as the promise is the promise of Allah, be certain that it will be realized.

For this reason the Truthful, Exalted is He, teaches us: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," [23] Except [when adding], "If Allah wills."﴾ (al-Kahf). The meaning: make for yourself a way out of lying if circumstances come between you and what you promised, by placing your matter under the will of your Lord, not your own will, because you possess none of the elements for completing the act.

So: recognize yourself, and say, "If Allah wills." Then, if circumstances come between you and what you had intended, you can say: "I willed it, but Allah did not will it."

And Allah, Exalted is He, does not fail His promise, because He, glory be to Him, knows things in accordance with how they will be. No power can divert Him from His purpose, and He has no partner who could review Him or take Him out of His purpose.

And if you wish, recite: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! [1] His wealth and what he gained will not avail him. [2] He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame [3] And his wife, carrier of firewood, [4] Around her neck is a rope of fiber.﴾ (al-Masad)

Was it not possible at that time for Abu Lahab to accept Islam, as Hamza, Umar, Khalid and Ikrimah and others accepted it? Did he not have the freedom of choice as they did? Indeed, did he not hear this surah? And despite all this he disbelieved and insisted upon his disbelief, and did not utter the word of faith, not even as a scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by saying in the assembly of Quraysh, even hypocritically: "Muhammad said such-and-such, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Is this not evidence of his stupidity?

So: since the Qur'an has given the news, the matter must necessarily come to pass in accordance with what it announced.

And we note here that the word wa'd (promise) means the glad tidings of good that is coming in the future, and the discussion here concerns two groups: a victorious group that rejoices in victory, and a defeated group that grieves over defeat. How then can the promise be rightly applied? The joy of the believer is a grief to the non-believer.

To clarify this matter, we mention that the orientalists paused at the words of the Exalted in the surah al-Rahman: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery [14] And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire [15] So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?[16]﴾ (al-Rahman)

And they said: this speech is intelligible as creation being a blessing from Allah, but what about His saying: ﴿There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and [molten] brass, and you will not be able to defend yourselves [35] So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?[36]﴾ (al-Rahman). So what blessing is there in fire and in the shuwaz(1)?

And these people overlooked that it is a blessing that We alert you to the danger before you fall into it, and warn you of the consequence of disbelief so that you desist from it, like the father who says to his son: "If you neglect your lessons you will fail, and then I will do such-and-such to you."

So: the mention of the Fire and the punishment is a blessing for everyone who opposes the path of truth, for perhaps when he hears the warning he will return and take heed.

And His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ (al-Rum) negates knowledge from them, i.e., of the inner realities of matters and their truth.

1 Al-shuwaz: a piece of flame having no smoke. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/361).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 7:

Then He informs about them:

﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.﴾ (30:7)

When you see a verb negated at one time and affirmed at another, know that the aspect is separate. They do not know the inner realities of matters; they know only their outward appearances. And would that they knew the outward appearances of everything. Rather, [they know] only the outward appearances of this world, and they do not know its inner realities, so what of the Hereafter?

When you reflect on worldly affairs and on the man-made laws that people enacted and then reversed after a time, you find that we know of the world only its outward appearance. For example, the Agrarian Reform Law, which we have applied since 1952, and which we were enthusiastic about, extolling it and not allowing it to be touched, is being debated today; they ask for it to be reconsidered, indeed cancelled, because it is no longer fit for application in this age. Russia, which nurtured the communist system and defended it with all its strength, is the one that repudiated this system and brought it down.

America did not bring it down, for example. Had America brought it down, the power and arrogance of communism would have passed to it. Therefore they say: communism was not defeated, it committed suicide at the hands of its own adherents. It is possible that these people will also commit suicide, just as their systems did, so it is more fitting for them to be upright before God and to be sincere toward people.

So: we know of the world only the outward appearances of things, and we do not know their reality, just as we now suffer because of the insecticides that we thought would relieve us and save us effort and time compared with manual pest control.

How much the world suffers today from the use of cars, for example, from pollution of the environment and the killing of lives every day. You may compare the means of transport in the past with the means of transport today. If modern means have immediate benefit, they have delayed harm. It is enough that the exhaust of what God created repairs the earth, while the exhaust of what people created corrupts it. Why? Because we know the outward appearances of things. Had the one who discovered diesel, for example, known its reality, he would not have used it for what we now use it for.

This is our knowledge of worldly affairs. As for the Hereafter, we are heedless of it. Therefore our master al-Hasan said: I marvel at the man who holds a dinar between his fingers and knows its weight, and who rings it and knows its counterfeit from its genuine, yet does not perform the prayer well.(1)

Among this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was God who threw...﴾ (8:17) Here He negates the throwing and affirms it in one verse, because the aspect is separate: affirmation is for one thing, negation for another. We had earlier illustrated this with the student whom you force to study: he opens the book, turns its pages and nods his head as if he were reading; but when you test him on what he has read, you find he has understood nothing. So you say: "You studied and yet did not study," because he performed the act of studying, yet in reality he did not study, since he acquired nothing of what he went over.

Likewise, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) threw when he took a handful of pebbles and threw them toward the side of the army of the disbelievers. But ﴿And you did not throw when you threw...﴾ (8:17) refers to that handful, because your human capacity could not carry that throw to the whole army. This, then, is the power of God.

We also note His saying: ﴿But most people do not know﴾ (30:6), where He excepted a small group from lacking knowledge. Why did He except this group, even though we change worldly systems and laws for everyone? They said: because when these laws were enacted and these systems instituted, there was a group that rejected them and did not endorse them, so not everyone was charged with lacking knowledge.

The apparent things they know of the worldly life contain enjoyments, pleasures and desires. Some grant themselves absolute freedom in them and forget their consequence in the Hereafter. Therefore the people of the countryside say of one who takes no account of consequences: "The wolf swallowed a sickle; the other says: wait until its excrement, and you will hear its howl."

And read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: women and children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, livestock and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, and with God is the best return.﴾ (3:14)

He mentioned the enjoyment of the worldly life to people, and they forgot the enduring good deeds in the Hereafter. The intelligent person is the one who can balance between them. We have earlier said regarding the world, in relation to you: it is the duration of your stay in it, your own lifespan and not the lifespan of the whole world, just as your lifespan in it is limited, presumed, and must end in death.

As for the Hereafter, it is the enduring abode, lasting, an abode of bliss that does not end, and it will by no means escape you. So why let the perishable occupy you from the enduring? Why are you content for yourself with a losing bargain?

Thus, when Imam Ali was asked: "I want to know whether I am among the people of this world or among the people of the Hereafter?" he said: "God did not leave the answer to me; the answer is with you. If two enter upon you, one bringing a gift and the other asking you for a gift, then if you are delighted with the one who brings the gift, you are of the people of this world, and if you are delighted with the one who asks for the gift, you are of the people of the Hereafter."

Why? Because a person loves whoever cultivates what he loves. If you love the Hereafter, you will consequently love whoever cultivates it for you, and if you love this world, you will love whoever cultivates it for you. Therefore one of the righteous, when a beggar came knocking at his door, would welcome him with a smile and say: "Welcome to one who comes carrying my provision to the Hereafter without a fee."

But why did He repeat the pronoun in ﴿And they are heedless of the Hereafter, they are heedless﴾ (30:7)? Why did He not say: "And they are heedless of the Hereafter"?

Had the Truthful, glorified is He, said "and they are heedless of the Hereafter," it would be understood that heedlessness dominates them and that there are no proofs to awaken them. Rather, ﴿they are heedless﴾ means: heedlessness is established from themselves, for otherwise the proofs are clear. But what use are proofs with a people who are heedless?

(1) Reported by Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh (in their tafsirs) from al-Hasan, who said: "So skilled is one of them in the affairs of his worldly life that he turns the dirham over on his fingernail and tells you its weight, yet he does not know how to pray." (Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/484).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 8:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Have they not reflected within themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.﴾

The meaning: it is for them to not know except the outward appearance of the worldly life, and to be heedless of the Hereafter, and not to reflect within themselves; so the proof comes to them once within themselves and once in the heavens and the earth.

The proof within the self says to you: reflect upon yourself. That is, make it the subject of your thinking, and contemplate the secrets within it that point to the power of the Creator, mighty and majestic. Until now, and despite what science has reached, there remain in the human being secrets that have not yet been discovered.

Contemplate the foundations of your life: eating, drinking and breathing. And how you can endure without food for about a month, feeding on the reserves in your body, and endure without water from three to ten days according to the amount of water in your body; but you cannot endure without air beyond the span of an inhalation and an exhalation.

Therefore, among His wisdom, may He be exalted, when He secured these foundations for mankind, He made the period of your endurance without food longer, because your food may be monopolised by others, so you need to seek it and strive for it. As for water, the period of enduring without it is shorter; therefore the Truth, glorified is He, made the monopolising of water small.

As for air, which you cannot endure without beyond an inhalation and an exhalation, it is by the wisdom of God, may He be exalted, that it is never possessed by anyone at all; for if people monopolised the air, life would not be upright. If the owner of the air were to withhold his air from you, you would die before he became pleased with you.

Reflect upon yourself when you eat food, and within you are two adjacent openings: the windpipe, which is the passage of air to the lungs, and the gullet, which is the passage of food to the stomach. Reflect on what happens to you if a single grain of rice enters the windpipe: without any feeling you choke on it, and you keep struggling against it until it comes out. And reflect on the movement of the epiglottis, which closes the windpipe during swallowing: this involuntary movement over which you have no control and no power by yourself.

Reflect on the state of the stomach, and how God made for it an opening that they call the cardia (fath al-fu'ad), which seals the stomach tightly after eating, so that its smell does not harm you, and so that the stomach's juices do not seep into the mouth and cause you pain. Whoever suffers a defect in closing this opening finds his breath foul, and they call him "abkhar" (one with foul breath).

Likewise, reflect on the process of expelling food: how you are naturally at ease, and then suddenly you need the toilet and to relieve yourself. What has happened? The matter is similar with a sip of water, because your body has a capacity that bears the load in the intestines and in the bladder; in a moment the load exceeds the capacity, so you feel a need to expel.

This is a field without limit, however far the sciences advance, and however much we investigate ourselves. It suffices that we recite: ﴿And within yourselves; will you not see?﴾ (adh-Dhariyat, 21). So our Lord called us to investigate ourselves before investigating what is around us of the signs of the heavens and the earth, because our gaze may fall short of seeing what is in the heavens and the earth of signs; as for my own self, it is the nearest proof to you and the strongest proof against you.

﴿Or have they not reflected within themselves...﴾ (ar-Rum, 8). That is: reflect within yourselves, far from the clamour of people, their disputation and their showing off, for when you argue with people you find in yourself a need and an eagerness for prominence, even through falsehood. But when you are with yourself, questioning and contemplating it, there is no agitator and no obstinate opponent; you are not ashamed that your adversary should prevail over you, nor do you covet a position or rank; therefore, by reflecting within yourself, you reach the truth.

Therefore the Qur'an addresses the Prophet (ﷺ) with His saying: ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing...﴾ (Saba', 46). That is: O you who reflect on the truthfulness of this Messenger, and accuse him of lying, fabrication, sorcery, etc.; I want one thing from you: ﴿that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly...﴾ (Saba', 46). That is, two by two, or alone, each on his own; ﴿then reflect: there is no madness in your companion; he is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾ (Saba', 46).

So: the path to the truth is not by public disputation, but by a person's contemplation with himself, or with his like. In a group, the desire for elevation and victory stirs within the soul; therefore, when you debate with a reasonable person, he says to you: "Your own self is your reckoner; review yourself," meaning: think alone, so that you are not embarrassed before anyone, and so you are nearer to objectivity and to reaching the truth.

After our Lord commanded us to reflect within ourselves, He turns us to contemplate what is around us of the heavens and the earth: ﴿Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term...﴾ (ar-Rum, 8).

There is another verse that puts reflection on the heavens and the earth before reflection on the self: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind...﴾ (Ghafir, 57).

Why? Because a human may die before he is born, or die after several years, or even after hundreds of years; but the heavens and the earth, with what is in them of earth, sky, sun, moon... etc., have not changed since Allah created them. They perform their task without deviation, without maintenance, and without malfunction. So they are truly greater than the creation of mankind and mightier.

Therefore: the signs and proofs are in yourselves and in the heavens and the earth. But which sign is stronger? They said: since the heavens and the earth are greater than the creation of mankind, they are stronger; if you are not convinced by them, then look into yourself. Therefore the scholars say: there is the one who instructs and the one who benefits. The instructor is Allah, mighty and majestic: when He strikes a parable for me, He strikes it with the stronger; if I cannot bear it, He brings me the lesser. The one who benefits is the one who moves from the lesser to the greater.

As for the meaning of ﴿and what is between them...﴾ (ar-Rum, 8): that is, the stars, the spheres and the constellations that we observe in the atmosphere of the sky. In the past, when they wanted to bring matters of religion closer to people's minds, they would say: the seven planets are the seven heavens. Great scholars fell into this, but the reality is that these seven planets are all below the lowest heaven. Read the saying of God, exalted: ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps...﴾ (Fussilat, 12).

So where is the heaven relative to the stars we observe? Do you know how many light-seconds are between you and the sun, or between you and the moon? Between us and the sun are eight light-minutes; between us and the "chained woman" (al-mar'a al-musalsala) is a hundred light-years; between us and the galaxy is a million light-years.

You may multiply a million years by 365 days, multiply the product by 24 hours, multiply the product by sixty minutes, then by sixty seconds, then multiply the product of that by 300 thousand kilometres, then consider the figure you have reached.

What silenced those who said the seven planets are the seven heavens was that scientists afterwards discovered another planet around the sun, and after years they discovered another. Likewise, when space travellers ascended to the surface of the moon, these "fellahin" hastened to say: "The Qur'an has preceded and foretold this in His saying:

﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except with authority﴾ (ar-Rahman, 33).

And they said: the authority is the authority of knowledge, which has enabled us to ascend to the surface of the moon. It is strange that great scholars should say this; for where is the moon in relation to the heaven? The moon is nothing but a suburb of the earth, like New Cairo in relation to Cairo. Then, if the authority here is the authority of knowledge, what do you say of His saying after it: ﴿There will be sent upon you both a flame of fire and molten brass, and you will not be victorious﴾ (ar-Rahman, 35)?

This confusion resulted from mixing the sciences of religion and Sharia with the sciences of cosmology. This is the affliction of religious scholars: that they interfere in matters of which they have no knowledge. From cosmology one takes proof of the greatness and power of the Creator, may He be glorified; but no legal ruling is taken from it.

We have seen some of these people deny that the earth is spherical and that it revolves around the sun; and some have thought that the cosmologists, although they are disbelievers, know the unseen, because they reached, by precise calculations of the earth's movement, the timing of lunar eclipses and solar eclipses, and reality came exactly as they had reported.

This matter, as we have said before, is not of the absolute unseen, but of the unseen for which Allah has given us the premises by which it is reached; scientists have reached it through investigation and study of the data of the universe. We understand this in light of His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth...﴾ (Fussilat, 53).

This too is among the verses which present the proofs of the heavens and the earth before the proofs of the self. So: cosmology is built on sciences and studies, in which religion has no part. Religion came to tell you: do this, and do not do that; then it left cosmology until minds are able to comprehend it.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿except with truth...﴾ (ar-Rum, 8): because the heavens and the earth and what is between them of stars and spheres move according to a fixed system that does not deviate, and the truth is the thing that is fixed and never changes. Reflect on the movement of the stars and spheres and you will find that they move according to a precise system, perfectly regulated.

The sun has never once failed, saying for example: "I will not rise today upon these people, because they are wrongdoers." For it has a law by which it proceeds, and it is created with a fixed truth that does not change. And since this cosmos was created with truth and with something fixed, you may base your calculations upon it and regulate your time by it; and you do not regulate your time by a clock unless it is itself regulated in its essence.

Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿The sun and the moon are by a reckoning﴾ (ar-Rahman, 5). That is: created according to a measure. And because He, glorified is He, created them by reckoning, He made them instruments of reckoning, saying: ﴿And the moon—We have determined for it phases until it returns like the old dried palm stalk. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night precede the day; and each, in an orbit, is swimming﴾ (Ya-Sin, 39-40).

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And He determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the calculation﴾ (Yunus, 5). And would you know the number of years and the calculation by the moon, unless it were created according to a measure?

Nevertheless, though the universe was created by Allah with established truth, beware of supposing that its stability is permanent and everlasting; for Allah created it in the form of stability for a term: ﴿except with truth and for a specified term...﴾ (ar-Rum, 8). So when that term that Allah has appointed comes to an end, the sun will be folded up, the stars will fall, the earth will be changed into other than the earth, and the heavens likewise. The matter is not merely that the stable thing changes; rather it passes away and ends.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾ (ar-Rum, 8). We used to argue with the Communists, saying to them: you have gone too far in torturing your opponents, the feudal lords and capitalists, and you have exceeded in punishing them. They said: because they wronged and spread corruption in society. We said to them: then what of those who wronged before these and died without receiving the punishment they deserved? Is it not just that you should affirm another abode in which they are punished for what they committed?

Does this not draw your attention to the necessity of the Resurrection, and the obligation of believing in it? Whoever escaped your hands in this world, Allah will punish him in the Hereafter. Then you yourselves see the principle of reward and punishment in everything: whoever let loose the reins of his soul in this world, and walked in it according to his desire, and spread corruption in the land, and was not reached by the hand of justice, is the winner if there is no other abode in which he will be called to account.

Therefore: belief in the Hereafter and in meeting Allah is a necessity required by sound reasoning; yet many people disbelieve in it: ﴿And indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾ (ar-Rum, 8).

So the believer must be certain of this meeting; for the laws of the earth only protect against outward wrongdoing, while the inward wrongdoing is known only to Allah. Therefore there must be a period in which those who commit inward wrongdoing are punished.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 9:

The meaning: "Do they not travel through the earth and see how was the end of those before them?" Take only the affairs of this world; they are sufficient for whoever takes a lesson from them. These people did not travel through the world, nor did they look upon it with the eye of reflection at the nations before them that denied (their messengers), nor were they admonished by what happened in the world, let alone by what will happen in the Hereafter.

If we have believed what befell the deniers in this world and witnessed it with our own eyes, then we ought to believe what Allah has told us about the Hereafter, for if you wish to know what you do not know, take for it a means from what you do know. So: travel through the earth, and look with the eye of reflection at the fate of those who denied, and at what Allah did to them.

Travel (al-sayr): crossing distances from one place to another. [Qur'an 29:20 / 30:9] "Have they not traveled in the earth...?" (30:9). But do we travel in the earth or on the earth? This is from the precision of Qur'anic expression and one of the manifestations of its inimitability. Apparently we walk on the earth, but the truth is that we travel in the earth, because the One who created us and created the earth said: "Travel therein by night and by day in security" (34:18).

This is because the earth is not merely the dry land that bears water and on which we live; rather, the earth includes everything that surrounds it of the atmospheric envelope, for without it the earth is not fit for living upon. Thus the envelope of the earth is part of the earth, and when we travel, we do not travel on the earth but in it.

Religion has enjoined travel through the earth from two angles: travel that is a journey for reflection (i'tibar), and travel that is a journey for development (istithmar). Travel for reflection means that you contemplate the signs in the land you pass through. The Arabian Peninsula, for example, is desert and mountains where crops are scarce; but if you go to Spain, for instance, you find green lands where one can hardly see the surface of the earth for the abundance of vegetation.

In each of them there are blessings, because the Creator, glorified is He, distributed the causes of bounty across the whole universe. And you see that this barren, parched land, which was hard for people to live in, when its inhabitants endured it, Allah gave them its bounty from beneath the earth, so that it now supplies the greatest and most advanced nations with fuel, which they cannot do without for a single day. And when we cut it off from them in the year 1973, they cried out, and the cold nearly killed them.

When you travel through the earth and look with the eye of reflection, you find that it is like a watermelon: if you take a lengthwise slice from it, it is equal to the rest of the slices. Likewise, the earth, Allah distributed bounties across its varied regions, so the total of good in each section of the earth equals the total of goods in the other sections.

The mountains that we abandoned in the past, saying they were barren and desolate with no life in them, are now storehouses of wealth and resources, toward which eyes have turned to develop them and benefit from them. Look, for example, at the renaissance of construction taking place in Sinai.

Thus the Creator, glorified is He, distributed the goods over the earth, just as He distributed talents among creatures, so that all remain linked to one another by the bond of need: people do not dispense with one another, nor do lands dispense with one another. Here is a faith-based insight: all creatures are servants of Allah and His handiwork, all lands are the earth of Allah and His dominion, and Allah has no offspring, and there is no kinship between Him and any of His servants; all are equal before Him. Therefore we have said before: you should not resent the possessor of good or envy him, for his good will certainly return to you.

The meaning of "those before them" (9): that is, the nations that denied the messengers. In another verse He clarifies the end of these deniers: "So each We seized for his sin; among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles, and among them were those seized by the Shout, and among them those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them those whom We drowned. And Allah was not one to wrong them, but they were wronging themselves" (29:40).

He, glorified is He, addresses the disbelievers of Quraysh: "And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then reason?" (37:137-138).

That is: in your journeys and trading trips you see the cities of Salih and other villages that were struck by punishment, still standing for everyone with eyes to see.

He, glorified is He, says: "Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the lands?" (89:6-8). They were in the sand dunes of al-Ahqaf. "And Thamud, who hewed out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh of the stakes" (89:9-10), and these are the pyramids. "Who transgressed in the lands and multiplied corruption therein, so your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment" (89:11-13).

All of these had civilizations that still, until now, dazzle the most advanced civilizations of today, so people come to them to contemplate the secrets and wonders within them. Yet these civilizations could not protect themselves from destruction and annihilation, nor could they prevent themselves from Allah's punishment when it descended upon them. So: there is a lesson for you in these people.

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, in His saying "Have they not traveled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them...?" (30:9), is saying to the disbelievers of Quraysh: You, O polytheists of Quraysh, are the least of nations; you have no strength, no wealth, no civilization, no development. It is easy for Us to seize you as We seized those who were stronger than you. You had already taken the covenant in His saying: "But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness" (8:33).

Therefore He says after it: "They were stronger than them in power, and they plowed the earth and populated it more than these have populated it..." (30:9). The denying nations whom Allah seized and made a lesson for you were stronger than you and more fertile in land. Therefore they plowed the earth, that is, they tilled it for cultivation and for development, while you are in a valley without cultivation. Tilling (al-harth) is used for crops, as in His saying: "And He destroys the tilth and the offspring" (2:205).

This is because the earth does not produce good vegetation unless the farmer plows it and turns over its soil so that air penetrates its soil, and then it yields generously and performs its function as it should. But if it is left hard and its soil and particles are compacted, it holds back the plant and gives no opportunity for the tender roots to extend into the soil, especially at the start of germination.

In another place, He, glorified and exalted, says about plants: "Have you considered what you till? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?" (56:63-64).

And in the story of the cow with the Children of Israel, when they dragged their feet in slaughtering it and asked about its attributes, the Truth, glorified is He, said to them: "It is a cow neither trained to plow the earth nor to water the tilth..." (2:71).

That is: a pampered cow, not easily led, so it is not used either for plowing and turning over the earth, nor for watering it after it is plowed. Therefore you find that the wise farmer must plow the land and turn over its soil before planting, and leave it for a period so that air and sun penetrate it; in this there is revival of the soil and renewal of its vitality, just as they also say: before you plant what you need, remove what you do not need.

So these people had crops and fruits, enjoyed them and gathered their bounties.

The meaning of "they populated it" (9): that is, by what Allah facilitated for them of capacities and possibilities, and they put to work the talent that Allah placed in them, so they extracted the earth's bounties from it, as He, glorified is He, said: "He brought you into being from the earth and made you its inhabitants (ista'marakum fiha)..." (11:61).

The populating of the earth occurs through every manifestation of progress and life: by planting or by orchards, by building, by digging rivers and drainage, establishing roads, and other things that benefit people. Here we distinguish between sowing (al-zar') and planting (al-ghars):

Sowing is what you sow and then harvest once, like wheat for example; planting is what you plant and it continues to yield for a long period, its produce renewing, like fruit gardens. Sowing is done with seed grain; planting is a seedling prepared in advance and then set in the ground.

Then He, glorified is He, says: "Their messengers came to them with clear proofs..." (30:9). After He gave them the foundations of life and the means of livelihood and capacities of substance, and after they had gathered its fruits, He did not leave them to matter alone, but gave them the capacities of values and religion, and sent messengers to them "with clear proofs" (30:9), that is, the manifest signs indicating the messenger's truthfulness in conveying from his Lord, and these are what we call miracles.

We have previously mentioned that the word "ayat" (signs) is applied to three meanings: cosmic signs indicating the power of the Creator, glorified is He, such as the sun and the moon; signs that support the messengers and establish their truthfulness in conveying from Allah, which are the miracles; and the verses of the Qur'an that carry the rulings and the method. All of these are clear and evident matters.

As for His saying, exalted is He: "But Allah was not one to wrong them, but they were wronging themselves" (30:9). Indeed, Allah did not wrong them, because He, glorified is He, provided them with the foundations of life and the capacities of substance, then provided them with the foundations of spirit and values; so if they then deviated from His method, glorified is He, they wronged only themselves.

Then we say: how can wronging be attributed to Allah, Exalted? Wronging does indeed occur from a human being against his fellow human, because he resents him and wants to enjoy what is in his hand; the wrongdoer takes the right of the wronged who has no power to protect his right. So how then can we conceive of wronging from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He, glorified is He, is the Owner of everything and free of need of everything? Therefore: Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves when they deviated from the path of Allah and His method.

The evil deed's opposite is good conduct (al-ihsan). It has already been said: al-ihsan is that you leave the righteous thing in its righteousness, or that you increase it in righteousness. We gave as an example a well of water from which people drink. One man comes to it and fills it in or pollutes its water, while another builds a wall around it to protect it, or makes for it a device that draws out the water and relieves the people. The second has done good and the first has done evil. So if you are not a doer of good, then at the very least restrain your evil and leave the situation as it is.

God, glory be to Him and exalted, created the universe in the form of righteousness. If we left it as its Lord created it, it would remain in its righteousness, since corruption only comes from human interference. Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers." Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they perceive not.﴾ (Al-Baqarah)

A person should take from the phenomena of the universe what benefits him. I recall that when we travelled to Makkah in the year 1950, we used to await the water-carrier who would bring us a waterskin (qirbah) of water and take a fee for carrying it. We would pour it into the (bazan), which is like our (zir) here. When one of us wanted to perform ablution, he would take one ladle (kawz) of water and say: "I intend the intention of taking handfuls," and he would not exceed this ladle in his washing, because we were buying the water. Now, however, one of us is not satisfied with a whole (safihah, a tin container) to perform ablution from the tap (hanafiyyah) of water. In rationalising the use of water there is also rationalising of sanitation and of groundwater, which harms buildings and farmland.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) warned us against extravagance in the use of water, even if we were on a flowing river.(1)

So the meaning of "those who did evil" (alladhina asaa'u) is: the one who came to the righteous and corrupted it, or initiated a new corruption. It is natural that its outcome be of the same kind as its deed: ﴿Then the outcome of those who did evil was the worst (al-suw'a)...﴾ (Al-Rum). Al-su'a is the feminine of sayyi' (evil), just as husna is the feminine of hasan (good) and sughra of asghar (smaller); it is the elative form (af'al al-tafdil) of al-su'.

Then the Real, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Because they denied the signs of God and used to mock them.﴾ (Al-Rum) The matter did not stop at denial of the signs; it went beyond denial to mockery. What is the philosophy of those who mock when they ridicule others? We often observe that the failing student mocks the diligent one, and the deviant mocks the upright. Why?

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are the astray."﴾ (Al-Mutaffifin)

But do not be hasty; wait for the outcome of that when these believers take their places in Paradise, sitting on its couches and its thrones: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon the couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ (Al-Mutaffifin)

The address here is to the believers who bore mockery and ridicule in this world: "Are we able to repay them for what they did to you?"

So the philosophy of mockery is that a person has not been able to master himself to drive it toward virtues; so every person of virtue enrages him, and it pains him to see an upright person enjoying the honour of obedience while he is in the mire of disobedience. Therefore he mocks him, perhaps he will turn away from the obedience and uprightness he is in.

1. On the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed by Sa'd while he was performing ablution. He said: "What is this extravagance?" He said: "Is there extravagance in ablution?" He said: "Yes, even if you were on a flowing river." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/221), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (425).

God Almighty then says:

﴿Allah originates creation, then brings it back; then to Him you will be returned.﴾

Did God originate creation in the past, or does He still continue to originate creation? The style here is that of a Lord speaking. He, glory be to Him, originated the roots of creation first, and He is still the Creator, glory be to Him. Since He is the One who created at the beginning, He is the One who brings it back. ﴿Allah originates creation, then brings it back...﴾ (al-Rum: 11)

In the customs of people, restoring a thing is easier than originating it, because origination is from non-existence, whereas restoration is from something existing. Therefore God, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then brings it back, and that is easier for Him...﴾ (al-Rum: 27). That is, by your measures and according to your understanding. In reality, there is no "easy" and "easier" with regard to Him, exalted be He, for He does not act by labouring at things and treating them; rather, He says "Be," and it is. But He addresses us according to the measure of our minds.

So God originated creation, and He still creates, glory be to Him. Consider, for example, the crop: you harvest it and take from it seed for the coming year, and so it goes in a continuous cycle between beginning and return. ﴿Allah originates creation, then brings it back...﴾ (al-Rum: 11)

We have previously given an example of the tender, fresh rose, with its beauty in appearance and fragrance. When it is plucked, it dries, because the water in it has evaporated; likewise its scent and colour have spread into the air. Then what remains crumbles and becomes dust. When a new rose is planted, it draws from the water that evaporated, and from the colour and the scent that are in the air.

Thus one cycle begins and another ends, because the constituents of life that God created are the same in the universe, neither increasing nor decreasing. The water in the universe is as it has been since God created it. Suppose you have drunk twenty tons of water throughout your life: do you carry that water with you now? No. It has been expelled in the form of sweat, urine, mucus, earwax, and so on, and all of it has evaporated to begin a new cycle.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned.﴾ (al-Rum: 11) We observe that the discourse here is about creation: ﴿Allah originates creation, then brings it back...﴾ (al-Rum: 11). Yet the context shifts from the singular to the plural: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾ (al-Rum: 11), and it does not say "it will be returned," i.e., creation. Why?

They have said: because all people do not differ concerning the origination of creation or its restoration, but they differ concerning the return to God. This one is a believer, that one is a disbeliever; this one is obedient, that one is disobedient; and this one is somewhere in between. At the time of return to God, this unity will divide into two paths: a path for the happy and a path for the wretched. Therefore the singular form is required for origination and restoration, and the discourse shifts to the plural for the return to God, because they differ regarding the return.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 12:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will be dumbfounded.﴾

The meaning of ﴿yublis al-mujrimun﴾ (Ar-Rum) is: they will fall silent with the silence of one in despair who finds no argument, so he is cut off, not knowing what to say and finding no one to defend him, even their leaders and their great ones having preceded them into punishment, so that they have no hope of salvation. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection...﴾ (Hud, 98). And from this root Iblis (Iblis) was so named, because he despaired of the mercy of God.

In another place the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair.﴾ (Al-An'am, 44)

That is: when they forgot the methodology of God, He, glorified is He, wished to punish them in this world. When God punishes them in this world, He does not seize them in their current state; rather He loosens the reins for them, increases them in good things, and widens for them the enjoyments and adornments of the world, until, when He seizes them in this condition, His seizing is painful, and their fall is from a height.

It is like when you do not throw your enemy down from the mat; rather we raise him up so that the revenge is more severe. As for if He seized them in a state of constriction and poverty, the matter would then be easy, and how close poverty is to punishment!

We have an observation on His saying ﴿We opened for them...﴾ (Al-An'am, 44). The root f-t-ḥ: if the Truthful, glorified is He, intends opening for the benefit of the one opened for, He says ﴿Indeed, We have opened for you a clear opening﴾ (Al-Fath, 1); and if He intends opening to the detriment of its recipient, He says ﴿We opened for them...﴾ (Al-An'am, 44). The difference between the two meanings is clear, because the preposition here is for ownership in ﴿We opened for you﴾ (Al-Fath, 1), whereas with ﴿We opened for them﴾ (Al-An'am, 44) it is ʿalā, meaning against them and to their detriment, just as we say in accounting: "له وعليه" (for him and against him), for him in gain and against him in loss.

Yes, they will find none among their partners to intercede for them, because the partners will have disowned them, as Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and all ties between them are cut off﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 166).

And likewise the followers will say: ﴿Our Lord, show us those who led us astray of the jinn and mankind; we will place them beneath our feet so that they may be among the lowest﴾ (Fussilat, 29).

Similar to these two is the case of the follower and the one followed: two failing students who grew accustomed to play and wasting time, each distracting the other from his lessons and enticing him to loiter in the streets, until the examination swooped down on them and the bitter truth caught them by surprise. Each of them began to curse and revile the other and to place the blame upon him.

So, in the hour of seriousness, all these frail connections collapse and all the ropes that bound the people of falsehood in this world are severed. ﴿And they used to deny their partners﴾ (Ar-Rum, 13). And why not, since the realities have been unveiled, their falseness has appeared, and their misguidance has become manifest?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 14:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) (subhanahu) says:

﴿And on the day the Hour is established, on that day they will be divided.﴾

That is: those who gathered in the world upon evil and misguidance will be scattered on the Day of Resurrection, and they will become enemies and adversaries after having been close companions. The believers will be distinguished on one side and the disbelievers on another. Even the sinful among the believers who have some trace of obedience will not be abandoned by the believers; rather, they will intercede for them and take them into their rows.

The tanwin in ﴿yawma'idhin﴾ (on that day) is a substitute (badal) for the clause ﴿wa-yawma taqumu al-sa'ah﴾ (and on the day the Hour is established), meaning: on the day the Hour is established, they will be divided.

Since on the Day of Resurrection creation will be separated and divided, there must be this division: those who believed and those who disbelieved. And here the verses show us this detail: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds...﴾ (Surah al-Rum, 30:15). So what is their reward? ﴿They will be in a meadow, made joyful.﴾ (Surah al-Rum, 30:15)

Ar-rawda (meadow): it is a place filled with greenery, rivers, trees and freshness. This was a rare thing among the Arabs, because they were a people of the desert, where gardens and meadows were scarce in their lands.

Therefore, meadows and orchards were a great thing among them and a great blessing. The meaning of ﴿yuhbarun﴾ (Surah al-Rum, 30:15) comes from al-hubur (1), which is joy, the happiness that shows on a person when the trace of blessing appears upon him. This is concerning the believers. So what about the disbelievers?

(1) al-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas said: "they will be honoured." It was also said: "they will be blessed." Mujahid and Qatada said so. Al-hibra among the Arabs means delight and joy. Mentioned by al-Mawardi. Al-Awza'i said: "When the people of Paradise begin to listen to singing, no tree in Paradise remains except that it responds with glorification and sanctification." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5268).

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought forth into the punishment.﴾

Al-muhdar (the one brought forth), with a fatha on the ha', is the one whom another brings in, and the word is used only for evil. It contains an indication of condemnation; otherwise he would have come by himself. We are alarmed upon hearing this word, because one who is brought to you comes only for some harm. Likewise is the condition of the disbelievers and the deniers on the Day of Resurrection: the angels drag them, compel them, and drive them to the place of presentation against their will.

¹ Muhdarun: residing (muqimun). It was also said: gathered (majmu'un). It was also said: punished (mu'adhdhabun). It was also said: descending (nazilun). The meaning is close.(Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5269).

Then Almighty Allah says:

﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.﴾

Here the greatness of faith becomes manifest, and the love of Allah Most High for His creation becomes manifest, in that He calls them to Himself at all times of the day and night: in the morning and in the evening, in the afternoon and at midday.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, asks His servants to believe in Him, it is only out of His love for them and His eagerness for their good, that He may give them and pour upon them of His bounties. Otherwise He, glory be to Him, is Self-sufficient above them by His attributes of perfection and majesty. The faith of believers adds nothing to His dominion, glory be to Him, just as the disbelief of disbelievers subtracts nothing from His dominion, glory be to Him.

So the matter is that He, glory be to Him, wishes to honour His handiwork and to dignify His creation and servants; therefore He summons them into His presence. Let us bring this matter closer by an example, and to Allah belongs the Highest Similitude. We say: if you wish to meet one of the great ones, or one of the people of high positions, then between you and this meeting are hardships which you must endure.

It is necessary that you first be given permission for the meeting; then the time and place are set for you, indeed also the duration of the meeting and its subject, and perhaps the words you are going to say. Then it is he who ends the meeting, not you.

This is if you wish to meet creation, so what of meeting the Creator, Mighty and Majestic? It suffices that He, glory be to Him, summons you Himself into His presence, and makes that an obligation and a certainty upon you, and seeks you before you seek Him, and mentions you before you mention Him, not once but five times in the day and night. So if you answer His call, He pours upon you of His mercy, of His blessings, and of His manifestations. And what of a handiwork that is presented to its Maker five times every day: would it suffer any defect?

Then your Lord leaves you all the details of this meeting, so you choose the time, the place and the subject. If you wish to lengthen the duration of the meeting, your Lord does not tire until you tire. Therefore the people of knowledge, who knew Allah Most High as He deserves, who knew His giving, and who knew the outcome of turning to Him, glory be to Him, say:

"Sufficient for my pride is that I am His servant,
He welcomes me without appointments, my Lord,
In His most mighty holiness, but
I am cast wherever and however I wish."

Servitude is a word disliked by humans, because servitude to humans is humiliation and degradation, where the master takes the best of his servant. But servitude to Allah is the peak of all honour, and in it the servant takes the best of his Master. Therefore Allah Most High bestowed favour upon His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, through this servitude in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night...﴾ (al-Isra).
