The word ﴿So glorify Allah...﴾ (al-Rum) is in itself worship and glorification of Allah, meaning: I declare Allah free from having anything like Him. Therefore the people of knowledge say: whatever occurs to your mind, Allah is other than that, because He, glory be to Him: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ (al-Shura).

We have said: if you survey the root s-b-h and its derivatives in the Book of Allah, you will find at the beginning of al-Isra: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night...﴾ (al-Isra), and at the beginning of surah al-Hadid: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah...﴾ (al-Hadid), then ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah...﴾ (al-Jumu'ah).

It is as if Allah, glory be to Him, was glorified from eternity before He created those who would glorify Him. So glorification belongs to Allah first, and after that the heavens and the earth glorified Him, and their glorification has not ceased; rather they continue glorifying Allah.

So if glorification belonged to Allah Most High before He created those who would glorify Him, and when He created the heavens and the earth they glorified Him and continue to do so, then it is incumbent upon you, O human, not to deviate from this rule, not to fall behind this cosmic system, and that you too be a glorifier. Therefore it came in the Qur'an: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ (al-A'la).

So be ashamed, O human, for everything in existence glorifies: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts [Allah] with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification...﴾ (al-Isra, 44).

However, some scholars wished to bring the glorification of inanimate things, which produce no audible voice or sensation, closer to understanding, and said: their glorification is glorification as an indication of Allah. We say: if it is glorification as an indication, as you say, then you have understood it; but Allah says: ﴿but you do not understand their glorification...﴾ (al-Isra, 44).

So your understanding of it is not real. And since Allah has informed us that they glorify, they glorify in truth, in a language we do not know. Why not, since Allah has given us examples of non-speaking things that glorified? Did He not say of the mountains that they glorified with Dawud, peace be upon him: ﴿O mountains, repeat with him [the praise], and the birds...﴾ (Saba, 10)? Did He not attribute speech and discourse to the ant and the hoopoe? And He said of all creatures in general: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification...﴾ (al-Nur, 41).

So glorification of Allah Most High comes from all creatures. The Truth, glory be to Him, gives us the example in ourselves: if you do not know English, for example, do you understand those who speak it? It is a language with sounds and letters that are pronounced, and you hear them in the same way that you speak.

Therefore the phrase (Glory be to Allah) comes in matters in which you must declare Allah free of defect. Read, if you wish, His saying in al-Isra: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night...﴾ (al-Isra). It is as if He, glory be to Him, says to us: declare Allah free from resemblance to humans, and from the laws of humans in this matter. Beware lest you say: how did Muhammad go from Makkah to Bayt al-Maqdis, then ascend to the heaven, and return in a single night?

Human reasoning finds this matter difficult to grasp, and this is what the disbelievers of Makkah did, when they said: how, when we travel to it on the backs of camels for a month, and you claim that you went to it in a night? They measured the matter and the distances by their own capacity, so they deemed it improbable and denied it.

Had they reflected on the verse ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night...﴾ (al-Isra), and they were people of the language, they would have known that the night journey did not happen through the power of Muhammad. He did not say "I traveled," but said "He caused me to travel by night," so it has no bearing on this matter and its laws are void in it; rather it happened by the law of the One who made him travel.

So you must declare Allah free from your laws of time and distance. If you wish to bring this matter closer to the intellect: the matter requires a time commensurate with the means by which the distance is covered. The one who walks is not the one who rides an animal, nor the one who rides a car, an airplane or a rocket, and so on.

If, in the laws of humans, when power increases the time decreases, how much more so if power is ascribed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Then we say: there is no time. If you say: if we remove time in view of the power and might of Allah Most High, why then was time mentioned here and measured as a single night?

They said: because the journey was not confined to going and returning; rather the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, encountered many signs during it, met some of the prophets there and spoke with them. These events of the Messenger of Allah are what occupied the time; as for the journey itself, it took no time.

Likewise the word (Glory be) came in His saying: ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ (Ya Sin, 36). Why? Because the matter of pairing is one of the matters at which reason halts, and we must declare Allah free of anyone sharing in it.

When this verse was revealed, people knew pairing in plants, because they pollinated the palm trees; they knew it in humans, because they marry and beget children; and they knew it in animals. These are the limits of reason in the matter of pairing.

But the verse is not confined to that; rather He, glory be to Him, said ﴿and of what they do not know﴾ (Ya Sin, 36), because the future would reveal to them other things founded upon the theory of pairing. We have known this theory in electricity, for example, where there is the negative and the positive, and in atoms, where there are electrons and protons, and so on.

So, whenever you hear the word glorification, know that you are about to encounter a unique event, unlike the events of humans, and not subject to their laws.

1 Awwibi: repeat the remembrance and glorification with Dawud. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/42).
2 Ibn Hisham cited in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (1/398) that most of the people of Quraysh said: "This, by Allah, is a clear matter. By Allah, the caravan takes a month to travel from Makkah to Syria going, and a month coming back; will Muhammad go there in one night and return to Makkah?"

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the late afternoon and when you enter the time of midday.﴾ [30:18]

We notice that His saying ﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth...﴾ (al-Rum) separates the times mentioned. He placed ﴿when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ (al-Rum 30:17) in one place, and ﴿and in the late afternoon and when you enter the time of midday﴾ (al-Rum 30:18) in another place, even though they are all times and periods within the day and night. Why?

They said: Because He, glorified is He, wants to make us feel that praise belongs to Him, and you must praise Him for His being exalted above any likeness. This is for your own benefit, and you are the one who gathers the fruits of this exaltation. If He wills good for you, there is no likeness to Him, glorified is He, that could prevent it from you. Greatness belongs to Him alone, and it protects you from anyone's arrogance toward you. To Him alone you bow and prostrate, and you do not prostrate to other than Him. Your prostration to the face of your Lord suffices you from all other faces, as the poet said: "The prostration that you find distasteful within it / Among thousands of prostrations is salvation."(1)

So it is in your interest that Allah, exalted is He, be the One who has no likeness, the Mighty who has no one mightier than Him, and the Truly Proud, for His greatness protects the weak from being overpowered by the strong. You must praise Allah, who has made us worship Him through prostration to Him alone and submission to Him alone, for by prostrating to Him He has saved you from prostrating to every powerful person other than Him. This is from His exaltedness and His mercy toward His creation, and therefore He deserves praise.

So in colloquial speech we say: "Whoever has no great one, let him buy himself a great one." Why? Because one does not live honored and dignified unless he has a great one who protects him and defends him. Likewise, you will not be honored except in your servitude to Allah.

All creation is equal in relation to Allah, exalted is He. He has no son or relative among His servants, so no influences affect Him, and He does not favor one over another. We are all partners in Allah; therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿He has not taken a consort or a son﴾ (al-Jinn 72:3), meaning nothing influences Him, glorified is He.

He said, after the glorification, ﴿And to Him belongs all praise...﴾ (al-Rum 30:18), because glorification should be followed by praise. You say: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Allah," meaning: praise be to Allah that I have glorified the One who is glorified.

When we reflect on these times in which Allah has commanded us to glorify Him, namely the evening, the morning, and the late afternoon, which is from the afternoon until sunset, and then midday, we find that these are general times that flow continuously throughout the creation of Allah and never cease. Which morning and which evening? My morning, or the morning of others? My evening, or the evening of someone else at the farthest edges of the inhabited earth?

Whoever reflects on the cycle of time finds that every moment of it is never free of morning and evening, afternoon and midday. This means that Allah, exalted is He, is glorified and worshipped at every moment of time.

In light of this we understand the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah extends His hand at night to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by day, and extends His hand by day to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by night." (2) So the universe is never free, in any single moment, of night or day, and this means that the hand of Allah, glorified is He, is always outstretched and never withheld: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outspread...﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:64).

(1) al-ijtiwa' (اجتواء): the thing's not agreeing with a person so that aversion arises toward it; from it comes "ijtawaytu al-balad" when one dislikes staying in a place, even if one is in blessing. (Lisan al-Arab, root j-w-y).
(2) Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (2759) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿He brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living, and He gives life to the earth after its death; and thus you will be brought forth﴾ [30:19]

First: What is the connection between the discussion of resurrection, the bringing forth of the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and the preceding discussion of glorifying and praising God? They said: it is because the verse before it spoke of evening and morning, and in these two there is a resemblance to life and death. In the evening the darkness descends, creatures settle down and sleep; it is a time of calm and rest, and sleep, which is a form of death, is why we call it the "minor death." In the morning is the time of movement, work and striving for livelihood, and in it, then, is life, as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We made the night a covering, and We made the day a time for livelihood﴾ [78:10-11].

Death and resurrection are likened to sleep and waking from it, as came in some admonitions: "You will surely die as you sleep, and you will surely be raised as you wake."

Since we have witnessed both states, and experienced sleep and waking, let us take from them a proof of resurrection after death. Although the Qur'an has informed us of this, it is incumbent upon us to believe, and to take from what is witnessed a proof of the unseen. This is what the verse brings:

﴿He brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living...﴾ [30:19]

And His saying here, "the living" and "the dead," means: in our view, and according to the limit of our knowledge and our understanding of matters. Otherwise, everything in existence has a life appropriate to it, and true death exists only in the Hereafter, of which God said: ﴿Everything is perishing except His Face...﴾ [28:88].

So the opposite of life is perishing, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿that whoever perishes might perish upon clear proof, and whoever lives might live upon clear proof...﴾ [8:42].

Since everything is perishing except His Face, the Exalted, then everything, consequently, is living, but it lives with a life appropriate to it. I recall that they used to teach us how to make a magnet, and the transfer of magnetism from one magnetized piece to another by rubbing in one direction; and indeed we saw that a piece of iron acquires magnetism.

And you can attract another piece toward it. Is this not a manifestation of the manifestations of life? Is this not movement in what we see as inanimate matter that has no life in it, which affects and is affected by other things, and within which atoms move in a fixed order and have a law?

Thus we say: for everything that exists there is its own particular life, even if we do not perceive it; for we understand that life is only in living beings, whereas it is in everything. That you do not comprehend the life of these things is another matter.

Therefore, our master Solomon, peace be upon him, when he heard the speech of the ant, and how it understood and stood as a sentinel for its tribe, and understood the movement of the army and the consequence of standing in its path, warned its community: ﴿Enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you, while they do not perceive﴾ [27:18]. It knew that if the army crushed the ants, it would be without intent on their part; and then Solomon felt God's blessing upon him in that he knew what others did not know, and he said: ﴿My Lord, enable me (1) to give thanks for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents...﴾ [27:19].

So the meaning of ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead...﴾ [30:19] is: in our terms, and according to the measure of our understanding of life and death. Some say it means that He brings the chick out of the egg and the egg out of the chicken. But this speech does not accord with the logic of reason: is every egg necessarily going to produce a chicken? No, rather it must be a fertilized egg. Therefore, do not say "the egg and the chicken," but say: He brings forth the living from the dead, from every existing thing.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿and brings forth the dead from the living...﴾ [30:19]. In another place He, exalted is He, says: ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead and the one who brings forth the dead from the living...﴾ [6:95]. Here He used the active participle (mukhrij) instead of the imperfect verb.

Therefore those who doubt the style of the Qur'an stopped at this, saying: if one of them is eloquent, the other is not eloquent. This approach is a natural result of their failure to understand the language of the Qur'an, and they do not possess the Arabic faculty that receives the speech of God.

Here we say: the One who speaks is the Lord, who gives every word its weight and places every word in its place, which no other word could fulfill.

So His saying, ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead...﴾ [30:19]: in whose interest is this? In our interest; for man by nature loves life, and may become arrogant with it and be deceived by this arrogance, as our Lord said: ﴿No! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [96:6-7].

Therefore his Lord reminds him in return: just as I bring forth the living from the dead, I bring forth the dead from the living, so be mindful, beware of exalting yourself or being arrogant, and understand that life is a gift to you from your Lord, which He can take from you at any moment.

He expressed this meaning once with the imperfect verb (yukhriju), which indicates continuity and renewal, and once with the active participle (mukhrij), which indicates the permanence of the attribute and its inseparability from the one described, not a mere passing event.

Therefore reflect on the saying of God: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent, who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [67:1-2]. In our view, life precedes death; but the Truth, glorified is He, wants to kill in man the attribute of being deceived by life, so He made him receive life with what contradicts it. He said: ﴿who created death and life﴾ [67:2], placing death before life. So before you think of life, remember death, lest you be deceived by it and transgress.

This meaning is also manifest in Surat al-Waqi'ah: ﴿Have you considered what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators? We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone, to replace your likeness and bring you into being in what you do not know. And you have certainly known the first creation, so will you not remember?﴾ [56:58-62]

That is: take heed, and understand that I am the Giver of life, and I can take it away, so do not be deceived by it nor become a pharaoh; and it is as if the Truth, glorified is He, wants to crush in man the attribute of pride and haughtiness, so He makes this juxtaposition always between the mention of death and the mention of life in the verses of the Qur'an.

Then do you not see that the Creator, glorified is He, has not made for death any cause of lifespan and years? One dies before being born, another dies after a day or a month, another after several years, and another after a hundred years.

Therefore: it is a matter with no rule except the decrees of God and the term He has appointed, and in this there is a sign for man: beware, for life from which your conceit arises may be taken from you at any moment, without your knowing, without prior warning or preliminaries. So remain upright upon the path of your Lord, and do not dare to disobey, for you may die before you can repent.

Therefore they say: when the Truth, glorified is He, left the time of death undetermined, He made that clear in the utmost clarity. How? They said: because if He had specified the time of your death for you, you would prepare for it only at its appointed time; but when He left it unspecified, He made you prepare for it every moment of your life.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and He gives life to the earth after its death...﴾ [30:19]. And in another place: ﴿And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and grows every lovely kind [of plant]﴾ [22:5].

The earth was dead, lifeless, barren, desolate, with no trace of life in it; then when water descended upon it and rain watered it, it stirred and grew every lovely kind [of plant]. It is therefore a living, visible model of creation and of life.

And in another verse: ﴿Do you not see that God sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ [22:63]. Did the earth turn green at the very moment the rain fell upon it? No, but after a period. It is as if He, glorified is He, says to you: observe the event at the moment it occurs, and keep its image in mind; for after the water descends, you see the earth turning green gradually, even if you have sown nothing in it, for there are various seeds carried by the winds which settled in the soil, and even for years they remain fit to sprout, awaiting water to carry out their task.

Whoever has lived in the desert witnesses this phenomenon. We have seen it in 'Arafah after the rain fell upon it; we returned after several days, and the earth was clothed in green. Therefore beware of thinking that every crop was planted by man, for otherwise, from where came the first seed that man planted? Thus there are plantings in which man has no part.

Let us read the story of Mary, peace be upon her: ﴿O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾ [3:42]. The first choosing did not say "above whom"; the meaning is that He chose you above all creation, by purifying you and making you righteous, pious, devoted to worship, and so on.

As for the second choosing, it is not above all creation, but above women; for she was distinguished from the women of the worlds in that she bore a child without a male.

The evidence we want here is that Joseph the carpenter, when he noticed in Mary signs of pregnancy, and he knew who Mary was and that she had never left the sanctuary throughout her life, the second meaning did not come to his mind, and he wanted to ask about what he saw, so he asked her politely: "O Mary, is there a tree without a seed?" She said, having been taught by the Truth, glorified is He: "Yes, the tree that brought forth the first seed."

Therefore: the Truth, glorified is He, bestows a favor upon us with a thing, then reminds us of His power to take it away and to reverse it, so that we are not deceived by it; not only in the matter of life and death, but in planting, in water, and in fire. Read His saying:

﴿Have you considered what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators? We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone, to replace your likeness and bring you into being in what you do not know. And you have certainly known the first creation, so will you not remember? Have you considered what you cultivate? Is it you who grow it, or are We the growers? If We willed, We would make it debris, and you would remain astonished, [saying], "Indeed, we are burdened with debt, rather we are deprived." Have you considered the water which you drink? Is it you who brought it down from the cloud, or are We the producers? If We willed, We would make it bitter, so why do you not give thanks? Have you considered the fire which you kindle? Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producers?﴾ [56:58-72]

And we notice in the Qur'anic expression in these verses the precision in the use of the emphatic lam in ﴿If We willed, We would make it debris...﴾ [56:65] regarding the crop, because man has a role in it: he plows, plants and irrigates, and may think he has power over it.

But when He spoke of water, in its reversal He mentioned ﴿If We willed, We would make it bitter...﴾ [56:70] without emphasis. Why? Because water is something no one has a hand in, and no one claims it; neither you evaporated the water, nor did you send down the rain. Therefore He said ﴿We would make it...﴾ [56:70] without emphasis.

As for the mention of fire as a blessing from the blessings of God, He did not mention what would reverse it, but said: ﴿Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producers?﴾ [56:72], and did not say, for example, "If We willed, We would extinguish it." Why? They said: so that the fire remains before us in its state of burning, never extinguished, and as if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is signaling with it to every disobedient one, perhaps he will return to the right path.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and thus you will be brought forth﴾ [30:19]. "Thus" refers to what was previously mentioned of the revival of the earth after its death: just as the earth is revived, so you will be brought forth and resurrected. Whoever denies resurrection, let him look at the process of reviving the lifeless earth with vegetation after rain has fallen upon it.

1 The meaning of "awzi'ni": inspire me and make me fond of it. Its linguistic interpretation: restrain me from things so that I may give thanks for Your blessing, and restrain me from what would distance me from You. (Lisan al-Arab, root: w-z-')

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 20:

The discussion here concerns the beginning of creation. God the Exalted says: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you...﴾ (20) (Ar-Rum). The address is in the plural, and what is meant is Adam, then Hawwa' (Eve), and then God spread from the two of them many men and women. So the world today, which is counted in the billions, when you trace it back into the past, you must return to two, namely Adam and Eve. When the two came together, offspring arose from them. But did the offspring arise from dead parts that came out of Adam, or from living parts, which are the sperm cells?

Had the sperm been dead, procreation would not have taken place. Therefore, the children of Adam came from the microbe of their father Adam, spread across the earth and had offspring, and each of them carries a particle of their first father, Adam, peace be upon him. Accordingly, each of us contains a living particle from the time of Adam, and up to now it has never undergone extinction. This is the world of dhar (the realm of atoms/seeds of souls) which witnessed God's creation of Adam. These are our parts that witnessed this first covenant between creation and the Creator, glory be to Him:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."﴾ (172) (Al-A'raf)

Therefore, in each of us now, and until the Hour arises, there is a living particle from our father Adam. This living particle is what witnessed this covenant, and it represents the innate faith (fitrah imaniyyah) in every human soul. But this innate nature may be obscured or covered over by heedlessness and sins... etc.

God the Exalted has informed us that He creates things and brings them into existence by "Be" (kun): ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (82) (Ya-Sin). Except for man: He has honored him to the extent that his Lord fashioned him with His own hand, made him His vicegerent on earth, manifested upon him with some of His attributes, so He gave him some of His power, some of His knowledge, some of His wisdom, and some of His self-sufficiency.

When our Lord creates us in this form, He wants us to use these attributes He has bestowed upon us, just as He Himself uses them. God the Exalted by His power created for us what benefits us, so upon you, with the power God has given you, is to do what is beneficial; and God by His wisdom arranged things, so upon you, with the wisdom you possess, is to arrange things... and so on.

We note that power differs: there is a power that acts for you, and a higher power that makes you act by yourself. Suppose you met a weak man who cannot carry his belongings, for example, and you carry them for him; then you have transferred to him the effect of your strength, but he remained weak.

As for the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, He does not merely transfer the effect of His strength to His servant; rather He transfers to him the power itself, so the weak becomes strong and carries his belongings by himself.

Therefore, the greatest honor for man is that the Creator, glory be to Him, says: "I created him with My own hand," in His saying to Iblis:

﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands?"﴾ (75) (Sad)

Then, O man, after this honor, it is for you to be honorable to yourself as God has honored you, and it is open to you to bring yourself down to the depths; your self is wherever you make it.

He the Exalted says: ﴿Certainly did We create man in the best of stature. Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds...﴾ (4-6) (At-Tin). So look to your own self to see which of the two positions it occupies.

As for the phrase ﴿from dust...﴾ (20) (Ar-Rum), it means the origin from which Adam was created. Dust mixed with water becomes clay (tin). If it stagnates and its smell changes, it is hama' masnun (black, altered mud). If it dries, it is salsal (dry clay) like pottery. So these are the stages mentioned of the creation of man, and all of them are names for dust and states that befell it.

If anyone comes and speaks on the matter of creation other than this, we do not believe him, because the One who created man has told us how He created him; as for those, they did not witness anything of the creation of man, and in the view of religion they are misguided, and one must beware of their ideas, for God the Exalted says concerning them:

﴿And I would not take the misguiders as helpers.﴾ (51) (Al-Kahf)

By God, if the scholars had not delved into the question of the creation of man, the creation of the sun, the moon, the earth... etc. If you had not heard of Darwin's theory, would this verse be true? Otherwise they would say: "Where are the misguiders the Qur'an spoke of?" So they spoke and came out upon us with their theories, wanting to deny God's religion and cast doubt on it, and behold, they all stand as proof of its truth without realizing it.

Similar to those we now hear denying the hadiths of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and casting doubt on their authenticity: this is in reality a natural phenomenon that came to confirm the truthfulness of the Messenger of God, for he, peace be upon him, did not neglect this matter; rather he informed of it and alerted us to it, and gave us the necessary immunity — the triad you hear about from health experts.

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Soon a man of my community will recline on his couch, narrating a hadith from me, and say: 'Between us and you is the Book of God. Whatever we find in it of lawful, we make lawful, and whatever we find in it of unlawful, we make unlawful.' Indeed, what the Messenger of God made unlawful is like what God made unlawful."(1)

Why? Because God the Exalted gave him authority to legislate for his community, as He said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it...﴾ (7) (Al-Hashr). So the Messenger has the giving, and the Messenger has commands and prohibitions which must be obeyed by our obedience to God.

As for the one who denies the Sunnah and says, "The Qur'an is enough for us" — when he prays the maghrib for example, ask him: "How many rak'ahs did you pray for maghrib?" He will say, "Three rak'ahs." So from where did he learn that maghrib is three rak'ahs? From the Qur'an to which he is zealous, or from the Sunnah which he denies? So how does he worship according to the words of the Messenger and then deny them?

Thus, God the Exalted, blessed and exalted, explained the stages of man's creation from dust, which became clay, then became black altered mud, then dry clay like pottery; then God breathed into him of His spirit. We did not witness this matter; He informed us of it. And out of His mercy to His creation, and so that their minds do not become bewildered when this process is investigated, He gives us in the observed universe something that clarifies for us the unseen which we did not witness.

In our customs, the demolition of a thing or the tearing down of a building comes in reverse to its construction: what was built first is demolished last, and what was built last is demolished first. You did not witness the process of creation, but you did witness the process of death, and death is the unbuilding of life.

Consider man when he dies: the first dismantling of his structure is that the spirit leaves him, though it was the last thing in his construction. Then the body stiffens and hardens, as it was in the stage of clay-dryness; then it decays and its smell changes, as it was in the stage of altered black mud; then the earth absorbs the moisture in it until it returns to dust, as its Creator began it from dust. Thus God spoke truly: the observed scene, when He showed us death, confirmed for us what He said about life.

Just as dust and clay are the origin of man, they are also the source of fertility and growth, and stores of sustenance, and they are one of the foundations of our life. Therefore, when the Qur'an spoke of the earth, He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds." And He placed within it firmly set mountains above it and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance...﴾ (9-10) (Fussilat). That is, the mountains, because they are the nearest mentioned, or the earth generally, since the firmly set mountains are in the earth.

Sustenance comes to us from the clay of the earth, and from the dust that is broken off from the mountains, forming the silt or alluvium which rainwater carries to us. So the earth is our true mother; from it we were created, and from it are the foundations of our life.

It is remarkable that we see among non-believing scientists someone who confirms the truth of the Qur'an on the creation of man from clay, when they analyzed the elements of the earth and found them to be sixteen elements, the very ones they found in the human body, as if God the Exalted were enlisting those who confirm the truth of His signs, even from among the disbelievers.

God the Mighty has spoken truly when He said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth...﴾ (53) (Fussilat). In the Qur'an there are verses indicating equations which, if the computer were to investigate them now, we would have to believe that this speech is from God and that it is true.

Consider the phenomenon of language, and how we speak and understand one another. If you have not learned English, for example, you do not understand it; likewise He does not understand Arabic. Why? Because language is born of imitation: what the ear hears, the tongue reproduces. It is a social phenomenon, so if a person lived alone, he would have no need for language, because he would do only what occurs to his mind, and only that.

But when he lives in a community, he must communicate with them: he takes from them and they take from him, he hears from them and they hear from him. Even the mute must have a language by which he communicates with those around him, and he indeed uses sign language, and God has enabled him to understand it.

God the Exalted keeps for the speaking human the signifying indications of gesture within the speaking soul. For example, if you are compelled to speak while there is food in your mouth, you gesture to your child or your servant, for example, and he understands you and does what you want.

So within us, we who are normal, are remnants of muteness that we use when speech does not serve us. Mutual understanding is a necessity, and language is born of imitation; therefore we say to a small child: "Do not go out to the street." Why? So that his ear does not hear foul speech and then he repeats it.

So how did you learn language? You learned it from my father and from those around me, and he learned it from his father and from those around him, and so on. You may trace this matter as we traced human reproduction, and we would then return to our father Adam, peace be upon him. At that point we say: "And who taught Adam language?" The Qur'an answers us: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them...﴾ (31) (Al-Baqarah). This is logical, inductive speech that indicates with decisive certainty the truth of the verses of the Qur'an.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then, when you are human beings dispersing (across the earth).﴾ (20) (Ar-Rum). "Then" means: after God created us from dust, the creation multiplied and increased rapidly; because the context here used "idha" (behold/suddenly), the sudden particle indicating suddenness, which they illustrate by saying: "I went out, and behold, a lion at the door," meaning: it surprised me. So the meaning is that you multiply and spread across the earth rapidly.

1 Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/132), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2664), Ibn Majah in his Sunan (12), and al-Daraqutni in his Sunan (4/286), from the hadith of al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 21:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) subhanahu says:

﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.﴾ [30:21]

We have said that an ayah (sign) is the marvellous thing that stops the intellect in astonishment, an astonishment that produces wonder, and wonder that produces certainty in the wisdom of the Creator. Among these marvellous and dazzling signs is ﴿that He created for you from yourselves spouses...﴾ [30:21], meaning: of your own kind and type.

Thus Allah, glorified is He, did not will that reproduction should take place, for example, between a human and a cow; rather it is human with human, who differs from him only in sex: this is male and this is female. And difference in sex is a difference of complementarity, not of conflict and collision. The woman is for tenderness, softness and tenderness of heart; the man is for strength and roughness. She rejoices in his strength and manhood, and he rejoices in her gentleness and femininity, and thus there occurs the complementarity that Allah willed and intended for the propagation of the human race.

It is strange that some see maleness as the opposite of femaleness, and stir up between them a manufactured dispute that has no meaning. Maleness and femaleness are two complementary necessities, like the complementarity of night and day, and they are two signs that all people encounter. Do we make a comparison between night and day... which is better? Male and female. Reflect on this precise meaning:

﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears, and by what created the male and the female, indeed your efforts are diverse.﴾ [92:1–4]

That is: different. Each of you has his own task, just as the night is for rest and calm, and the day is for striving and work; and through the complementarity of your striving there arises a higher complementarity.

So there is no need for me to demand equality with woman, nor for woman to demand equality with man. We have been given headaches by these proclaimers of this alleged equality, which has no meaning after His saying, ﴿indeed your efforts are diverse﴾ [92:4].

It is strange that we hear someone say, from among the men, that woman should take the place of man and perform what he performs. We say: a woman cannot bear the task of a man unless a man bears the task of a woman: he would carry as she carries, give birth as she gives birth, and nurse as she nurses. So let us set aside the slogans of the "thugs" (al-balTagiyya) who speak of what they do not know.

Similar to this is His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves...﴾ [9:128], meaning: of your own kind and humanity. He is a soul that possesses all the capacities of humanity, so that he may be an exemplar for you; had the Messenger come as an angel, the exemplarity would not have been realized in him, and you would have said, "This is an angel, and we cannot do what he is able to do." Or ﴿from among yourselves...﴾ [9:128] means: from among the Arabs and from Quraysh.

Some (1) hold that ﴿from among yourselves...﴾ [9:128] means the creation of Eve from a rib of Adam, so she is from ourselves, meaning a piece of us. But the address here in ﴿from among yourselves...﴾ [9:128] is addressed to male and female together, just as "spouses" (azwaj) is applied to both of them, to the man and to the woman. Some understand that "zawj" means two; but "zawj" is a singular, with its like alongside it; therefore Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And of all fruits He made in it two spouses, two...﴾ [13:3].

In the past we used to believe that the sex of the fetus is determined by the water of the man and the water of the woman; but the Qur'an says otherwise: ﴿Was he not a drop of ejaculated semen?﴾ [75:37]. The water of the woman has no part in the sex of the fetus, male or female; maleness and femaleness are determined by the water of the man.

This is what modern science has established. On this basis we say ﴿He created for you from yourselves spouses...﴾ [30:21], meaning: from the males of the spouses (2), He created from you a microbe, which is the XY (X and Y chromosomes) as modern science has termed it, and it signifies maleness and femaleness.

We have previously mentioned in this matter the story of Abu Hamza, the Arab man who married another wife over his wife because she did not bear sons, and he abandoned her for this reason; so she said, with what she possessed of Arab natural eloquence, and her saying is evidence of the knowledge of the Arabs in ancient times of this truth which science has established recently. She said:

"Why does Abu Hamza not come to us angry?
Is it that we do not bear sons?
By God, that is not in our hands;
we are like the land to those who sow it:
we give them the like of what we have been given."

By this, the Truthful (al-Haqq) subhanahu wants to say: I want a khalifa (vicegerent) that multiplies, to populate this vast earth. If you see a place that has become crowded with its people, know that there is another place empty; the matter is a bad distribution of God's creation on God's earth.

Therefore they say: the cause of crises is that there are men without land, and land without men. We have given as an example the fertile land of Sudan, which finds no one to cultivate it; had it been cultivated, it would have sufficed the entire Arab world, while we live in the valley and the delta until they became too narrow for us. If you think of migrating to these empty places, you face the problems of borders with which they have restricted people, and God has sent down no authority for them.

Therefore, when we were given the opportunity to speak at the United Nations, I said to them: one verse in the Book of God, if you acted upon it, would solve for you the economic problems of the whole world. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the earth He laid down for the creatures﴾ [55:10]. The earth, all of it, is for the creatures, all creatures without exception.

And read His saying on this matter: ﴿Was not the earth of God spacious, so that you might migrate therein...?﴾ [4:97]. So: do not oppose the method of God and His decree in His rulings, then complain of corruption, constriction and crises. If you were to survey the phenomena of the cosmos, you would find no corruption at all except in what the hand of man touches contrary to the law and method which the Creator of this cosmos, glorified is He, has laid down; as for what the hand of man does not touch, you see it orderly, not disordered and not deviating.

So: problems and crises arise only when we walk in God's cosmos without God's guidance and without His method. Therefore you hear someone say, "Life is narrow" (dank); at the hearing of this word there leaps to your mind only the problem of poverty. But narrowness (dank) is far wider than that: wealth and luxury and abundance of living may exist, and yet you see people in severe narrowness.

Look, for example, at Sweden, which is among the richest countries of the world, yet madness, deviance and psychological complexes are common there, and suicide is common there as a result of the constriction they suffer, although they are the richest and highest in per capita income.

So the matter, then, is not an economic condition; it is a matter of a method of God, exalted is He, that is not applied and not practised. And God has spoken truly: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a narrow living, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ [20:124].

Therefore, if we lived by the method of God, we would find the pleasure of life even with poverty.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that you may find tranquility in them...﴾ [30:21] — this is the fundamental reason for marriage: that the spouses find tranquility, one in the other. Tranquility arises only from movement. Likewise, the man throughout his day is in the movement of work and seeking a livelihood; he toils and is tired, so at the end of the day he wants to find tranquility in one who relieves and consoles him, and he finds none but his wife, in whom there is tranquility, affection, compassion and tenderness; and in this tranquility he rests and regains his energy for work on the morrow.

But imagine that the man returns tired and does not find this tranquility; rather he finds his wife and the place of his residence and rest increasing his fatigue and troubling his peace. Therefore it is incumbent on the woman to know the meaning of tranquility here, and to fulfil her task so that the affairs of life may be set right.

Then the matter is not limited to tranquility; rather ﴿and He placed between you affection and mercy...﴾ [30:21]. Affection is mutual love in the "journey" (mishwar) of life and its partnership: he toils and provides the necessities of living, and she toils to manage the affairs of the house and raise the children; for God says, ﴿indeed your efforts are diverse﴾ [92:4]. This is within aframework of mutual love and tenderness.

As for mercy, it comes last among these qualities: tranquility, affection and mercy. That is because people in general are children of changing circumstances, and their conditions often change: the strong may become weak, the wealthy may become poor, and a beautiful woman may be altered by the passing days or felled by illness... etc.

Therefore the Qur'an draws our attention to the fact that in this stage, in which you may have lost tranquility and lost affection, mercy will encompass you both. Let the husband show mercy to his wife if her capacities fall short of performing her duty, and let the wife show mercy to her husband if illness has laid him low or poverty has struck him... etc.

Many of the elders who fear God and observe these teachings live their married lives on this principle, the principle of mercy; therefore, when they hint to a woman whose husband has been laid low by illness, she says: "Shall I eat the meat and throw him the bone?"

This is the religious woman, which brings us back to the hadith of the Messenger of God concerning the choice of a wife: "A woman is married for four things: for her wealth, for her lineage, for her beauty, and for her religion, and these are all changing; so win the one with religion, may your hands be rubbed with dust (taribat yadaak)." Thus you and she are children of changing circumstances; neither of you remains in his state, so you must be returned to something stable and a neutral method that has no desire inclining it toward either of you, a method in which you are equal, and you will find that only in the religion of God.

Therefore the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, warns us: "If someone whose religion and character you approve comes to you, marry him; if you do not, there will be turmoil in the earth and great corruption."

Beware, when your wife grows older, of saying, "She no longer fills my eye," or such and such, for the wife was not made by God except as a tranquility for him, a female, and a vessel; if his desires are stirred by their nature, he will find an outlet, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If one of you sees a woman and she pleases him—that is, she pleases him and stirs in his soul impulses—let him go to his wife, for the womb is one."

Whenever the spouses apply the religious standards and adorn themselves with the manners of religion, each finds in the other what pleases him. If outward beauty departs with time, the beauty of the spirit and its dignity will remain; the beauty of disposition and conduct will remain in the woman. Whenever you remember her sincerity toward you, her devotion in serving you, her eagerness for your livelihood, and her care for the sanctity of your house, the more you will hold fast to her and the more love for her will increase.

The same applies to the wife with respect to the husband: every stage of life has its own attractiveness and beauty, which compensates us for what has passed.

Since it is the nature of women that signs of age appear on them more than on men, it is incumbent on the husband to take this into account. When someone asked al-Hasan: "A man has proposed to my daughter, and his description is such and such," he said: "Do not marry her except to a believing man: if he loves her, he honours her; and if he dislikes her, he does not wrong her."

Then He, subhanahu, says: ﴿Indeed in the signs are a people who give thought﴾ [30:21]: they give thought to these matters and to these stages through which married life passes, and how God, exalted is He, made for us spouses from among ourselves and not of another kind; and how He built this relationship upon tranquility, love and affection, and then, in the stage of old age, upon mercy by which the spouses must live together throughout their lives.

(1) Qatada said: the intended one is Eve, whom God created from a rib of Adam's ribs. Mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5272), and al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/490) to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir from Qatada. Ibn Kathir also adopted it in his tafsir (3/429).
(2) This opinion was adopted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5273), who said: ﴿from among yourselves...﴾ [30:21] means: from the sperm of men and from your kind. He mentioned Qatada's view in the passive form (with the letter mim) "it is said" (qila). Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, in his book "al-Ba'ith al-Hathith" (a commentary on Ibn Kathir's abridgement of the sciences of hadith), p. 34, Subayh press, says: the form of certainty is "he said", "he narrated", "came", "from"; and the form of hedging (with mim) is "it is said", "it is narrated from", "it is reported", "it is mentioned", and the like.
(3) Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/428), Abu Dawud in his Sunan (2047), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (1858), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.
(4) Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1084), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (1967), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "The hadith has been recorded by al-Tirmidhi, who preferred its being mursal (broken chain). Then it was recorded from the hadith of Abu Hatim al-Muzani, and he said of it that it is hasan."
(5) Recorded by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (3/330, 341, 348, 395), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1403), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw a woman, then went to his wife Zaynab, fulfilled his need, then went out to his companions and said: "Indeed the woman approaches in the form of a devil and withdraws in the form of a devil; so if one of you sees a woman, let him go to his wife, for that will repel what is in his soul."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and your colours. Indeed in that are signs for those who know.﴾

In the creation of the heavens and the earth there are signs, the most evident of which are visible to us, as He said elsewhere that they stand without pillars: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you can see.﴾ (Luqman)

So the sky that you see stretched across the horizon stands without pillars (1). You may travel through the earth and seek these pillars, but you will not see anything. Or, ﴿without pillars that you can see﴾ (Luqman) means: they exist, but you do not see them (2).

Reason requires that a high thing must have either pillars to bear it from below or a force to hold it from above. Therefore we should join the verses together so that this picture is complete for us. The Truth, glory be to Him, says elsewhere: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him.﴾ (Fatir)

So: the sky has no pillars; rather its Creator, mighty and majestic, holds it from above, so it does not fall upon the earth except by His permission. Do not be astonished at this matter, for Allah, exalted is He, has given us a visible example in His saying: ﴿Have they not considered the birds, subjected in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them up except Allah.﴾ (An-Nahl)

If you say: what holds the bird in the atmosphere of the sky is the movement of its wings and their fluttering, which creates resistance against the air, so it rises by it and keeps itself aloft; we say: it is also held in the atmosphere of the sky without any movement of the wings. If you wish, read His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings?﴾ (Al-Mulk)

You see the bird in the sky with its wings outstretched, motionless, and yet it does not fall to the earth, and nothing holds it up in the atmosphere of the sky except the power of Allah.

So: take from what you witness a proof of the truth of what you do not witness. Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ (Ghafir), even though they were created to serve man.

Although you, O human, are a manifestation of the power of Allah, and within you the greater world is folded up, your lifespan is nevertheless limited and counts for nothing when measured against the lifespan of the earth, the sky, the sun, the moon... etc.

Then the context returns here to one of the signs of Allah in man: ﴿and the difference of your languages and your colours...﴾ (Ar-Rum). "Lisan" (tongue) is applied to language, as He said: ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara' 195), and He said: ﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic tongue﴾ (An-Nahl 103).

It is also applied to this well-known organ, and "lisan" was applied to language because most of it depends on the tongue and on speech, although the tongue represents a small part in the process of speech, since the mouth, teeth, lips, vocal cords... etc. also participate in speech, yet the tongue is the mainstay of this process. So: the difference of tongues means the difference of languages.

We have previously said that language is a social phenomenon which a person acquires from the environment surrounding him, and when we trace it back, we must reach our father Adam, peace be upon him. We said that Allah, exalted is He, is the One who taught him language when He taught him all the names, and then Adam and his descendants after him adopted these names so that they might understand one another, and add new names to them.

Therefore, when we want to teach our children and raise them, we see that we teach them first the names of things before they learn verbs, because the noun is more evident. Do you not see that the verb and the action are indicated by a noun? The word (fi'l, verb) is itself a noun.

But how do languages differ? If we reflect, for example, on the Arabic language, we find it one language, but its environments are many: this is Egyptian, this is Sudanese, this is Syrian, Moroccan, Iraqi... etc. We all share one language, but each environment has a particular dialect which may not be understood in another environment; but if we all speak Arabic, the language of the Qur'an, everyone understands one another through it.

As for the difference of languages, it arises from the isolation of environments from one another. This isolation leads to the emergence of a new language. For example, English, French, German and... etc. all go back to one origin, the Latin language. When the environments became isolated, each of them wanted to have its own independent identity with a language of its own, independent in its vocabulary and its grammar.

Or, ﴿and the difference of your languages...﴾ (Ar-Rum) means: the difference of what arises from the tongue and other instruments of speech of various sounds. As we see now, at the latest frontier of phonetics, they have found that the voice has a fingerprint that differs from person to person, like the fingerprint of the fingers; indeed the voiceprint is a clearer indication than the handprint.

For this reason we have seen safes that are set to the voiceprint of their owner: whenever he produces a sound for them, they open for him.

Among the marvellous and astonishing things in the field of sound: sounds are many. Some are from inanimate things, such as the rustling of trees and the murmur of water; some are from animals, such as the croaking of frogs, the neighing of horses, the braying of donkeys, the bleating of sheep, the lowing of camels... etc. But by Allah, I ask you: if you heard the braying of a donkey, could you say, this is so-and-so's donkey? No, because the sounds of all kinds of creatures other than man are one sound, not distinguished by anything.

As for man, each one here has his own voice, distinguished by its tone, its sharpness, its heaviness, its high or low pitch, its softness or its heaviness... etc. Why then is the human voice distinguished by this quality from the rest of the sounds?

They said: because inanimate things and animals do not have responsibilities that need to be controlled and determined as man does. Otherwise, how would we identify the criminal when he commits his crime, when we do not know his name and know nothing of his attributes? And even if we know his attributes, they do not point to him with a decisive indication that fixes responsibility and upon which the penalty is based.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and your colours...﴾ (Ar-Rum). So the difference of tongues and colours is for this distinction to occur among people; and because man is the one held responsible, Allah created in him the difference of tongues and colours, so that we may infer him by his form: his height or shortness, his clothing... etc.

In this there is something that controls man's conduct and straightens him, when he knows that he will not escape with his deed, and that something of these distinguishing features must indicate him.

For this reason we see investigators of criminal research organize a plan to search for the criminal, which may be long. Why? Because they want to narrow the circle of search, excluding those whose characteristics do not match theirs, and they keep narrowing the circle until they reach the perpetrator.

And the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another...﴾ (Al-Hujurat 13).

Distinction and mutual recognition are thus necessary for the proper functioning of life. Do you not see that a man gives each of his sons a name that distinguishes him? If he loves the name Muhammad, for example, and wishes to name all his sons Muhammad, he must still distinguish them: this is Muhammad the elder, this is Muhammad the younger, this is the middle one... etc.

So: creatures must be distinguished so that we can determine responsibilities.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed in that...﴾ (Ar-Rum), i.e., in creation in this wise and firmly ordered form, ﴿are signs...﴾ (Ar-Rum) for us to take lessons from. The Creator, glory be to Him, if He unifies attributes, is a proof of wisdom, and if they differ, it is a proof of the absoluteness of power. Consider, for example, the craftsman who makes glass cups: you see him take the glass paste and pour it into a mould, and they all come out in one shape; whereas the baker, for example, takes the dough and makes it into a loaf, and you never see one loaf exactly like another.

As for the Creator, mighty and majestic, He creates with wisdom and with absolute power, and He creates what He wills, not bound by any particular mould.

And His saying: ﴿for those who know...﴾ (Ar-Rum) means: those who investigate things and do not stop at their surfaces, but penetrate their depths and probe their depths to reach their reality.

For this reason our Lord, mighty and majestic, reproaches us: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it.﴾ (Yusuf 105). It does not befit people of intellect to neglect these signs; rather they reflect on them in order to derive from them what benefits them in the future of their lives, as we see in modern inventions and discoveries that have served humanity, such as the one who invented the steam age, the one who invented the wheel, the one who discovered electricity, gravity and penicillin... etc. So: we pass by the signs of Allah in the universe with alertness, and all the experimental sciences are the fruit of this alertness.

"Al-'alimun" (those who know) is the plural of "al-'alim", which in the past was applied to one who knows the lawful and the unlawful, but it is broader than that: the 'alim is everyone who knows a cosmic or legal matter. This is called "the scholar of cosmic matters," and that is a scholar of the Shari'ah. If you wish, read:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth with it fruits of diverse colours; and among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of diverse colours, and deep black; and among men and beasts and cattle are those of diverse colours likewise... ﴾ (Fatir 27-28)

Here He mentioned plants, then inanimate things, then men, then animals.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿It is only those among His servants who have knowledge that fear Allah...﴾ (Fatir 28), without restriction, and He did not specify which scholars: scholars of plants, animals, inanimate things, or scholars of the Shari'ah. So: the 'alim is everyone who knows a truth in the universe, whether existential or legislated by Allah.

But why did they apply "'alim" particularly to the scholar of the Shari'ah? They said: because it is the first of the beneficial sciences they knew. Therefore we have seen, among the etiquettes of knowledge in Islam, that scholars of the Shari'ah should not enter into cosmic matters themselves, and scholars of cosmic matters should not enter into the sciences of the Shari'ah.

What has caused confusion between these specialisations is that, for example, scholars of cosmic matters say that the earth revolves around the sun, and then some religious scholars stand up and say: this contradicts religion—just like that, without study. Glory be to Allah! Why do you thrust yourself into what you do not know? And what harms you, as a scholar of the Shari'ah, if the earth is a sphere that revolves or does not revolve? What prohibited thing has increased by the earth's rotation, and what permitted thing has been diminished? Likewise, when man went up to the moon, some religious men objected to this.

Likewise we hear someone without knowledge of the Shari'ah objecting to some matters of the Shari'ah, saying: this is not accepted by reason. So: the affliction of knowledge is that a scholar thrusts himself into what he does not know; and if each one kept to what he knows, everyone would be at ease, and each field would be left to its people.

It is strange that religious men cite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the earth—We have spread it out...﴾ (Al-Hijr 19) as evidence that the earth is not spherical. If they had reflected on the meaning of ﴿spread it out﴾ (Al-Hijr 19), they would not have objected; for the meaning of "spread it out" is that wherever you travel on the earth you find it extended, not ending until you return to the point from which you began, and this means it is a sphere without end; whereas if it were flat or triangular, for example, it would have an end.

So: we say to scholars in general: do not poke your noses into what you have no knowledge of, and leave the field to its people, in obedience to His saying: ﴿Indeed, every people knows its drinking place...﴾ (Al-Baqarah 60).

(1) Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it has no visible pillars nor invisible ones. (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/442). He said (2/499): "Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah said: the sky over the earth is like a dome, meaning without pillars; and similarly it is narrated from Qatadah, and this is what is fitting to the context and the apparent sense of His saying: ﴿And He holds the sky lest it fall upon the earth, except by His permission...﴾ (Al-Hajj 65)."

(2) Said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah and Mujahid: it has pillars that you do not see. (Quoted by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 3/442). He said (2/499): "It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others that they said: it has pillars, but they are not seen..."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Surely in that are signs for a people who hear.﴾ (23)

Likewise, among the wondrous signs that demonstrate the power of God is ﴿your sleep﴾ (Surah al-Rum, 23). Until now, the scholars of physiology and anatomy have not uncovered the secret of sleep, and despite all their experiments they have not known what sleep is.

Yet it is a phenomenon that is present and dominant, which no one can resist, however much strength one has. However much a person tries to stay awake without sleeping, sleep must overcome him and he sleeps, even on pebbles and thorns. He sleeps while standing, and while carrying something; he must sleep in any state.

The philosophy of sleep is not how we sleep, but rather why we sleep. They said: because man is made up of energies and organs, each of which has a function. The eye is for seeing, the ear for hearing, and so on. When the body's organs become exhausted, they bring you to a stage at which they are no longer able to work, so you need – without your awareness and by an instinctive command – to rest, as if they were saying to you: enough, you are no longer fit for work or movement, so sleep.

Among the wonders of sleep is that it does not come by summoning. You may summon sleep by all kinds of means and it will not obey you, and you do not sleep. But if it comes to you, it overcomes you in whatever state you are in, and despite noise and disturbing sounds you sleep. Therefore the Arab says: Sleep is a phantom; if you seek it, it troubles you, and if it seeks you, it gives you rest.

For the people of knowledge there is a beautiful cosmic view and meaning of sleep. Regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise...﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 44), they say: everything in existence glorifies, even the parts and organs of the disbeliever are glorifying; it is only his will that is disbelieving. These parts remain subject to the will of their owner until they are released from this will on the Day of Resurrection, and then they bear witness against him to what he did, and to the disobedience to God to which he compelled them.

We have previously given an example of this: the commander of a battalion, whose soldiers obey him even in error, because their obedience to him is obligatory until they return to the supreme commander and complain before him, informing him of what their commander did.

We also mentioned that one of the commanders of the World War wanted to use a trick by which he would outdo his enemy, although it violated the laws of war among them. When his plan succeeded and he defeated his enemy, they honoured him for his initiative, but they did not fail to punish him for violating military regulations, though it was a nominal punishment so that the law might retain its dignity.

Likewise, the parts of the disbeliever submit to him in this world, and bear witness against him on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿On the day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will bear witness against them for what they used to do.﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 24)

Even though these limbs are the ones that uttered the word of disbelief, and they are the ones that stole... etc.; this is because God subjected them to the will of their owner. But on the Day of Resurrection he has no will over his limbs: ﴿And they will say to their skins: Why did you testify against us? They will say: God made us speak, who makes everything speak...﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 21). Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, reassures us with His words: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (Surah Ghafir, 16)

So when the disbeliever sleeps, his parts and limbs are relieved of him; they are relieved of the evil desires he holds. Therefore our brothers who perform the pilgrimage to the House of God tell us: there sleep has blessing, and the least amount of time suffices me to rest. Why? Because your mind during the Hajj is occupied with obedience to God, and all your time is devoted to worship, so your limbs are at rest and at ease, not burdened by disobedience; therefore the least amount of sleep suffices them to rest.

In light of this understanding we understand the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "My eyes sleep but my heart does not sleep" (1). Because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, devoted his whole life to obedience, so his limbs were at rest, and mere dozing sufficed him from sleep.

In colloquial speech the people of the countryside say: the sleep of the wrongdoer is worship. Why? Because during his sleep he does not command his limbs to evil, nor compel them to disobedience, so his parts rest from him, and people and the world rest from his evil. And what worship is greater than this?

We note this verse: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty...﴾ (Surah al-Rum, 23). Here He made night and day the place of sleep and of seeking provision. In another verse: ﴿And of His mercy He made for you night and day, that you may rest therein﴾ (Surah al-Qasas, 73), He combined them together, then mentioned the detail of that in order: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ (al-Qasas, 73), i.e., at night; ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ (al-Qasas, 73), i.e., by day.

This is a style known in the language as al-laff wa'l-nashr (the wrapping and unfolding), which is to mention several things that are predicated upon, then mention after them the predicates upon them collectively, leaving it to the listener's intelligence to return each predicate to its appropriate subject.

From this is the poet's saying: "My heart, my eyelid, the tongue, and my Creator / A fasting one, a weeping one, a grateful one, and a forgiving one." So the subjects are gathered in one place, then the predicates in another place. Gathering the subjects is called laff, and gathering the predicates is called nashr.

These two verses are among those at which the scholars paused, and we cannot derive a ruling from them except by combining the verses, not by understanding each verse on its own. Here, in the verse before us, ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty...﴾ (Surah al-Rum, 23), we note that God, exalted is He, made each of night and day a place for sleep and a place for striving.

In the other verse: ﴿And of His mercy He made for you night and day that you may rest therein﴾ (al-Qasas, 73), then He said: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ (al-Qasas, 73), and He did not say "therein." We must be attentive here: this is a cosmic sign, that night be for sleep, stillness and rest, and day for work and movement. There is no objection to working at night too, for some work can only be done at night, such as watchmen, security men, night patrolmen, bakers in bakeries and others; and these people's rest is by day. With this understanding the verses complete one another on a single subject.

Therefore: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and your seeking of His bounty...﴾ (Surah al-Rum, 23), means: the seeking of provision and striving for it occurs by day and occurs by night, but most people seek it by day and rest by night, and the minority are the reverse.

If you say: this is in our case, where night and day are equal, but what about the lands where the night, for example, lasts three months and the day likewise; we want to interpret the verse on this basis: do they work three months and sleep three months? Or do they make the nights of the months night and day, and the days of the months also night and day? There is no objection to that, because a person is never without a night for rest and a day for work, or the reverse; so each of night and day is a time for work or for rest.

Therefore, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, bestows His favour upon us through the alternation of night and day, and He says, glory be to Him: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if God made night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God would bring you light? Will you not then hear?﴾ (al-Qasas, 71). He concluded the verse with "Will you not then hear?" ﴿Say: Have you considered, if God made day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God would bring you a night wherein you may rest? Will you not then see?﴾ (al-Qasas, 72). He concluded this one with "Will you not then see?" Why?

They said: because day is the place of sight and vision, while night has no sight in it, so hearing suits it, and the ear is the instrument that performs its task at night when sight is unavailable.

In another place: ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day alternating for whoever wishes to remember or wishes gratitude﴾ (al-Furqan, 62). So night succeeds day, and day succeeds night, this in the ordinary time we live in. As for the beginning of creation, which of them came first, and then the other succeeded it?

If you say: the night came first, and then day succeeded it; but night in this case would not be a succession to anything, while the previous text shows that each of them succeeds the other. So what resolves this riddle?

The key to this matter lies in the sphericity of the earth. Had the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them at the beginning of the mission of this fact, they would not have believed him; how, when we still see those who deny this fact until now?

The Truth, glory be to Him, does not leave a cosmic matter like this untouched, even if lightly and gently, so that when minds advance they take notice of it. If the earth were flat and God, exalted is He, had created the sun facing the earth, we could say: day came first, then when the sun sets night comes. But if the beginning was the creation of the earth not facing the sun, then night in this case is first, followed by day; this on the assumption that the earth is flat.

Since the Creator, mighty and majestic, has informed us that night and day each succeed the other, He must have created the earth in a form such that night and day exist together, so that as the cycle of the cosmos turns, each succeeds the other; and this can only be if the earth is spherical, so that what faces the sun becomes day, and what does not face the sun becomes night.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says in another verse: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each is floating in an orbit.﴾ (Ya Sin, 40)

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, denies that night precedes day. Why?

They said: they believe that night precedes day. Do you not see them seeking the beginning of Ramadan by its night rather than its day? And since they believe that night precedes day, the counterpart in their view is that day does not precede night. This is a matter the Truth, glory be to Him, affirmed; so He did not alter it, but rather negated the first: ﴿nor does the night outstrip the day﴾ (Ya Sin, 40).

Thus: He negated what they believed, ﴿nor does the night outstrip the day﴾ (Ya Sin, 40), and confirmed what they believed, that day does not precede night. From this matter there arises: night does not precede day, nor does day precede night; and this is only possible if both exist at one time, so that what faces the sun is day, and what does not face the sun is night.

(1) A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh), from the hadith of 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3569), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (738), that 'A'isha was asked: How was the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Ramadan? She said: He did not exceed eleven rak'ahs in Ramadan or otherwise: he would pray four rak'ahs, do not ask about their beauty and length, then four, do not ask about their beauty and length, then he would pray three. I said: O Messenger of God, do you sleep before you pray witr? He said: "My eyes sleep, but my heart does not sleep."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 24:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, as a fear and a hope, and sends down water from the sky, and gives life thereby to the earth after its death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use their reason.﴾ (30:24)

We observe in the concluding phrases of these verses that He, glorified is He, says sometimes ﴿for a people who reflect﴾ (30:21), sometimes ﴿for people of knowledge﴾ (30:22), sometimes ﴿for a people who listen﴾ (30:23), or ﴿for a people who use their reason﴾ (30:24). Thus the investigating faculties mentioned in the verses differ.

Some think that reason (ʿaql) is an instrument one operates in everything: reason is what affirms or does not affirm. The truth, however, is that you use reason in the matter of religion once, and that single use suffices you thereafter. You use reason in deciding whether to believe or not to believe. If reason guides you to the conclusion that the cosmos has a God who is capable, wise, and Creator, there is no god but Him, and you trust this proposition, then it will not recur to test your belief again, nor will reason investigate it afterward. Moreover, in subsidiary matters you proceed according to this first matter of faith, and so you do not need reason in them.

For this reason the wise say: reason is like a mount that brings you to the presence of the sultan, but it does not enter with you into his presence. Likewise, reason has brought you to faith, and then its role has ended. So when you hear "God says," you are confident of the truth of the statement without applying reason to it.

When He, glorified is He, says "they use reason," "they reflect," "they know," and calls you to contemplation and admonition, He is in fact alerting within you the faculties of questioning, so that you may be certain. Reason here has the task of examining alternatives, premises, and conclusions.

Consider, for example, if you went to buy cloth and the merchant displayed his goods to you: "This is pure wool, and this is pure cotton." He does not stop at that but shows you the quality of his merchandise. He takes a strand (fatlah) of wool and a strand of cotton and sets fire to each of them so that you see for yourself: the wool does not keep burning as the cotton does.
