Thus it is he who alerts within you the means of criticism, and he does not do this unless he is confident of the quality of his goods. As for the other, who is not confident of his goods' quality, he resorts to tricks and stratagems by which he lures the buyer to deceive him.

Likewise the Creator, mighty and majestic, alerts us to searching and reflection upon His signs, saying: reflect, contemplate, use your reason, be aware scholars of what goes on around you. This is evidence that if we examine these signs we would arrive at what He, glorified is He, desires, which is faith.

The lightning (al-barq) is one of the phenomena of the winter season, where we hear a loud, thundering sound we call thunder (al-raʿd), after we see an intense light flashing in the air that we call lightning (barq). It is one of the factors of the electrification of the atmosphere, which modern science has reached. But before that, all people, when they see lightning, understand from it only one of two things: either it will bring a thunderbolt that burns them, or rain will descend upon them. So they fear the thunderbolt and hope for the rain.

﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, as a fear and a hope, and sends down water from the sky...﴾ (30:24), so that the servant may always remain with his Lord between fear and hope.

But do all people hope for rain? Suppose you are a traveler or a resident in the desert, having no shelter in which to take refuge and no cover to shield you from the rain. Such a person does not hope for rain nor await it. Therefore, by His mercy, exalted is He, the emotion of desire for the water by which the earth lives through vegetation predominates.

﴿And sends down water from the sky, and gives life thereby to the earth after its death...﴾ (30:24)

The word "sky" (samāʾ) has two meanings: a predominant meaning, the seven heavens, and a linguistic meaning, which is everything above you that shades you. This is the meaning intended here, ﴿sends down water from the sky...﴾ (30:24), because rain descends only from the clouds, so "sky" here means everything above you that shades you.

If you reflect on the water that descends from the sky, you will find it comes from accumulated clouds: ﴿Do you not see that God drives the clouds, then joins them together, then makes them a heap, so you see the rain issuing from their midst...﴾ (24:43).

We have previously discussed how clouds form, that they result from the evaporation of water. Therefore, in His wisdom, exalted is He, He made three-quarters of the earth water and a quarter dry land, so that the area of evaporation would be vast, as though the three-quarters were made to serve the quarter, and so that the rainwater would suffice the inhabitants of the dry land.

We have also explained the importance of the expanse of the water surface in the process of evaporation: if you leave a cup of water on a table for a long time, for example, it remains as it is, and if some of it is lost it is only a little. But if you pour the water of the cup onto the floor of the room, for instance, it dries in a few minutes. Why? Because the surface of the water has expanded, so the amount of water evaporating increases.

We may liken the formation of clouds to the process of distillation that we perform in pharmacies to obtain pure, sterilized water. This rests on the principle of collecting water vapor from boiling water, then passing it over a cold surface, where the vapor condenses into clear water. So when you receive rainwater, you are receiving distilled water of the utmost clarity and purity, without your feeling this process at all, and without our burdening you with anything for it.

Consider this wondrous cosmic engineering from which rain arises: the heat of the sun on the earth's surface evaporates the water by heat; in the upper layers of the atmosphere the temperature drops, so the water condenses and clouds form. It is remarkable that every time we ascend thirty meters above the earth the temperature drops a degree, even though we are drawing nearer to the sun. That is because the sun does not heat the atmosphere; it heats the earth's surface, which in turn gives its heat to the atmosphere. Therefore, the further we move from the earth, the lower the temperature.

And among God's wisdom is that He made the water of the earth from which sweet water evaporates salty; because its saltiness preserves it from becoming stagnant, or foul, or changing its smell, and preserves it from being a breeding ground for harmful parasites, and so that it remains in its soundness, since it is a reservoir of sweet water by which the earth is watered with its sweetness.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then, when He calls you with a call from the earth, behold, you will come forth.﴾ (30:25)

The "heaven" here means the seven heavens, which stand without pillars. We have said that a thing that is above you is either supported on pillars, or is fastened upward, like suspension bridges for example. Likewise, the heaven is a raised ceiling whose pillars we do not see. So there remains only the other means: that Allah, exalted is He, ﴿holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth except by His permission﴾ (22:65). Thus it stands by His command.

﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command....﴾ (30:25). Its order never wavers, and you find in it no fissures, because it is firmly constructed. Look at it when the sky is clear and free of clouds, and you will find it smooth, of one colour across its vastness. Can anyone paint for us such an expanse in a single colour that does not vary?

And if we take the heaven to mean everything that is above you and shades you, then look at the sun, the moon, the stars and the planets, and how they stand by the command of Allah their Creator, in a precise order with no disruption. We have not seen, for instance, one planet collide with another, nor any of them leave its course.

Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿Each in an orbit they swim﴾ (21:33). Each of them has a speed, and each has its own particular orbit and an order by calculation. That is because they stand by the command and decree of Allah, exalted is He, so they are regulated, performing their task without defect and without failure.

So the meaning of ﴿stand﴾ (30:25) is: they remain standing in their state without corruption, and it is a present-tense verb indicating continuity. And when you reflect: before man invented magnifying instruments and microscopes, we saw of the solar system nothing but the sun; then when they invented the telescope we saw the other planets that revolve around it.

And the wonder is that they do not revolve in equal circles, but in an elliptical shape, widening on one side and narrowing on another. These planets have a revolution around the sun, and another revolution around themselves. The earth, for example, has an orbit around the sun from which the four seasons arise, and a rotation around itself from which night and day arise. All this compound motion takes place with a precise, firm order, regulated to the utmost degree.

These planets differ in their nearness or distance from the sun: the nearest to the sun is Mercury, then Venus, then the Earth, then Jupiter, then Mars, then Saturn, then Uranus, then Neptune, and the farthest from the sun is Pluto. Each has its own orbit around the sun, called (a year), and a rotation around itself called (a day).

It is remarkable that the day of Venus, the second planet from the sun, is estimated at 244 Earth days, whereas its year is estimated at 225 Earth days; so the year is shorter than the day. How? They say: because this rotation is independent and that one is independent; it is swift in its revolution around the sun and slow in its rotation around itself.

And if you knew that in space and in Allah's vast creation there are a million systems like our solar system in (the Milky Way), and all of this within the galaxy we know, you would see the greatness of this universe, of which we know only a little. Therefore, when you read: ﴿And the heaven We built with might, and indeed, We are expanding it﴾ (51:47), know that it is a matter without end or limit in our knowledge and our minds, but it has an end with Allah.

Nothing shows the precision of these cosmic motions more than the precision of the timing of solar and lunar eclipses, which scholars calculate and which arrive perfectly exact, for they base their calculations on the motion of the planets and their rotation. So we say to whoever still obstinately denies it and says the earth does not rotate: you must then admit that those who predict eclipses know the unseen. The closer conclusion, then, is that it all belongs to Allah, who created them in this form of order and precision; so attribute it to Allah instead of attributing it to the scientists.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then, when He calls you with a call from the earth....﴾ (30:25). The meaning of ﴿a call from the earth....﴾ (30:25) is the second blast. The first, of which Allah says: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be extinguished﴾ (36:29), and the second, of which He says: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us﴾ (36:53).

The first is for total death, and the second for total resurrection. If you look at these two blasts and what Allah has placed in them of secrets that correspond to the secrets of worldly life, you will find something wondrous.

Every moment of time there is a birth and there is a death; we differ in our births and in our terms, but in the Hereafter the matter is in agreement. Those who differed in births will agree in resurrection: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us﴾ (36:53).

And those who differed in death will agree in extinction: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be extinguished﴾ (36:29). Birth corresponds to resurrection, and death corresponds to extinction. So the difference of these is treated by the agreement of those, and the agreement of these is treated by the difference of those; therefore He says: ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering....﴾ (64:9).

The second blast is performed by Israfil by the command of Allah; for the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, carries out some things by His own essence, and we know of them only that He, glorified and exalted is He, created man and shaped him with His hand, as He said: ﴿O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My hands?....﴾ (38:75). As for other than that, He, glorified is He, carries out things through His creation in all matters of the cosmos.

Consider, for example: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death....﴾ (39:42). Here the one who takes is Allah, mighty and majestic. In another place: ﴿Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you....﴾ (32:11), so the taking is ascribed to the angel of death. And in another place: ﴿Our messengers take him....﴾ (6:61), so the taking is ascribed to the messengers of death from among the angels, who are soldiers of the angel of death.

The explanation of that is that He, glorified is He, first ascribed death to Himself, because He is the one with the supreme command over it; He commands the angel of death, and the angel of death in turn commands his soldiers. So the matter returns to Allah.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then, when you come forth﴾ (30:25). That is: when the dead hear this shout, they will all rise up alive. The "idha" here is the sudden-occurrence particle, indicating suddenness, and this is the difference between the birth of this world and the birth of the Hereafter. The birth of this world was not sudden but gradual: before the woman gives birth we see her pregnancy for several months, and she suffers the pains of pregnancy for several months, so there is no suddenness in it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 26:

We know that "man" (من, man) is used for the rational being, and we may ask: why was the rational being singled out, when everything in the universe is subject to God, obedient, glorifying Him, and included in the sphere of qunut (devout obedience) to God? They said: because rebellion comes only from the side of the intellect; therefore God mentioned it specifically. As for the inanimate object that has no intellect, its command proceeds smoothly, for nothing refuses God's command, neither the inanimate, nor the animal, nor the plant.

Consider, for example, the donkey: filth is loaded on it and it bears it; but if you tame it and make it a mount for riding, it does not resist. There is no stick in the first case, and no stick in the second, because it has been made submissive to you by God's subjugation, not by your intellect or your strength: ﴿Have they not seen that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We have subdued them for them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ (Yasin 36:71–72).

And we may give the example of the camel: when God subjected it to you, a small boy can lead it, make it kneel, mount it, and carry loads on it. But the small serpent frightens you despite its smallness, because God has not subjected it to you.

We pause here at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth…﴾ (al-Rum 30:26). As for those in the heavens, yes, they are qanitun (devoutly obedient) to God, meaning they are submissive to Him, glorified, obedient to His will, because they are honoured angels: ﴿They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ (al-Tahrim 66:6); ﴿They glorify Him night and day, and they do not slacken﴾ (al-Anbiya 21:20).

Then what of the people of the earth, among whom are atheists and disbelievers who are not qanitun? How then are we to understand ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ (al-Rum 30:26)?

They said: because when they rebelled against God and disbelieved in Him, or rebelled against His judgment and disobeyed Him, they did not rebel by their own essence, but by the choice God created in them. Had He, glorified be He, willed them to be subdued by compulsion, not one of them would have deviated from the will of his Lord. Almighty and Majestic God does not wish to rule man by the compulsion of power; rather He wishes His servant to come to Him willingly, choosing: he is able to disbelieve and yet believes, and able to disobey and yet obeys.

Had God willed them to be believers, they would not have found a way to disbelief, and He would have protected them as He protected the prophets. Your Lord wills you to be a believer out of love and sincerity, not out of compulsion and dominance. Therefore Iblis said in his dispute: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾ (Sad 38:82–83).

He has no power over the sincere servants of God, whom God has chosen for Himself, and he has no authority over them. Iblis, then, is not in a battle with his Lord; he is in a battle with man. In another place God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, over My servants you have no authority…﴾ (al-Hijr 15:42).

When these rebels against God came to love rebellion and loved it, God increased them in it and helped them to it; for He, glorified be He, is not benefited by the obedience of the obedient, nor harmed by the disobedience of the disobedient. So He sealed their hearts, so that no faith enters them and no disbelief exits them. He, glorified be He, is free of need from His creation. Therefore, when He created Paradise, He created it to be wide enough for all people if they believe, and when He created Hell, He created it to be wide enough for all people if they disbelieve; and He left us free choice: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ (al-Kahf 18:29).

It is as if the Truth, glorified be He, says to us: you are free; I am ready to recompense in whatever state: My Paradise will be wide enough for you if you all believe, and the Fire will not be too narrow for you if you all disbelieve.

We say to whoever has rebelled against God: you ought to be consistent with yourself, and remain a rebel against God in everything, since you have grown accustomed to rebellion. If sickness comes to you, you refuse it; if death comes to you, you reject it. But if you cannot do that, then you are subdued to God and submissive to Him, ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ (al-Rum 30:26): submissive, either by choice or by compulsion in every matter in which you have no choice. So you are devoutly obedient against your will, and your qunut together with your rebellion is more eloquent testimony to God.

Thus, the believer is submissive to God in the realm of choice, which is faith and the obligations, and submissive to God in what he has no choice about, such as decree and matters of necessity; he receives these with contentment. As for the disbeliever, he is submissive to God and cannot escape His decree or His destiny against his will in matters where he has no choice, but he receives them with wrath and discontent; he is a disbeliever in God, hating His decree.

So we say to whoever has rebelled against God and disbelieved in Him, or rebelled against His rulings and disobeyed them: what is wrong with you that you do not rebel against God in what He decrees upon you of matters of necessity? This is proof that you have taken choice out of its proper place; for whoever chooses ought to take choice in everything. But to choose in one thing and not in another is not permissible.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 30, verse 27:

The Noble Qur'an often speaks to us about this matter and reminds us of the beginning and the return. Why? The Qur'an gives this matter great attention and stresses it because it was the foundation of its call; for if they (the disbelievers) believed that they would return to Allah, they would fear His punishment. Therefore, it emphasizes to them in many places the certainty of the return and that it is true.

The words of the Most High: ﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it...﴾ (27) (al-Rum). The verse opens with His words "wa huwa" (and He). In another verse: ﴿Allah originates creation, then repeats it...﴾ (11) (al-Rum). So "huwa" (He) signifies "Allah," and it is, as we know, a pronoun of absence (ghayba), and the Truth, glorified is He, is hidden from sight. Among His greatness, glorified is He, is that He is unseen; for if He were perceptible and sensed, He would not deserve to be a god. And how could we hope to perceive Him, glorified is He, when we cannot perceive some of His creatures?

The meanings that Allah created to govern the movement of life: the word of truth, justice; the truth to which the whole judiciary stands to render and proclaim it, and justice that governs the balances of life, to balance between desires and realities. These meanings are not perceived by the senses. Have you seen justice? Have you heard justice? Have you smelled justice?... etc.

Therefore: lofty meanings cannot be perceived, because they are higher than perception, for it is by them that perception occurs. Could the created be loftier than being perceived, while the Truth, glorified is He, be an object of perception?

So when you hear "huwa" (He), know that it refers only to the One God, who in His greatness cannot be perceived: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision...﴾ (103) (al-An'am).

Therefore, we read in Surah al-Ikhlas: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ (1) (al-Ikhlas). You see that "Allah" is the proper noun of majesty (lafz al-jalala), which is a name for the Necessarily Existent (wajib al-wujud), and it comes after "huwa." So "huwa" is more indicative of the existence of the Truth, glorified is He, than the name "Allah." Thus, it is not valid, when the pronoun of absence "huwa" is used, for it to refer to anything but Allah, because there is nothing in the cosmos but Allah.

And His words here: ﴿And He it is who originates creation...﴾ (27) (al-Rum) use the present tense verb that indicates continuity, although He, glorified is He, began creation with the past tense: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾ (29) (al-A'raf). If you mention the first, then He has originated creation; and if you mention continuity in bringing into existence, then He originates always, and at every moment you see in creation something new from Allah. Creation did not come once and then stop; rather it began and then continued.

We note that the Qur'an mentions this matter sometimes in the past tense ("bada'a," He originated) and sometimes in the present ("yabda'u," He originates); because the Creator, glorified is He, actually began creation by creating Adam, peace be upon him, the first human: ﴿He who perfected everything He created and began the creation of man from clay﴾ (7) (al-Sajda). And He, by His self-subsisting (qayyumiyya), continues to be the Creator, originating every day and every moment a new creation that we witness in humans, in animals, in plants, etc.

And by the renewed creation of humans, in that every moment a new child is born, we refute those who speak of metempsychosis (tanasukh al-arwah) — meaning that the soul leaves one body and settles in another — for this would mean that births equal deaths, and that the world would remain at one fixed number without increase. We now see the extent of the population density of which the world complains today, and this suffices to demolish this theory.

The Truth, glorified is He, warns us not to take the story of the beginning of creation from anyone other than the Creator, glorified is He. Among people are misleaders who will mislead you on this matter, so do not lend them your ears, for Allah says: ﴿I did not make them witnesses to the creation of the heavens and earth, nor to the creation of themselves, nor was I one to take misleaders as helpers﴾ (51) (al-Kahf).

We have seen among these misleaders those who say that man's origin is a monkey that evolved into a human. The refutation of these errors is easy: if the monkey evolved into a human, why did the other monkeys not evolve? And why has the human not evolved since Adam until now into something else? How can we believe these errors, when our Lord, glorified is He, says: ﴿And of everything We created pairs, that you may remember﴾ (49) (al-Dhariyat)?

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ (36) (Ya-Sin). So beware of saying that something evolved from something else; every kind subsists in its own right since Allah created it.

So: beware of such sayings, and take the story of the beginning of creation only from Allah alone.

His words ﴿...then repeats it...﴾ (27) (al-Rum): meaning, back to creation, so it means "yakhluquhu" (He creates it). The meaning is: He originates creation, then causes it to die, then repeats it. Some think that "yu'idu-hu" (repeats it) means He resurrects it in the Hereafter; but Allah, the Most High, says: ﴿Allah originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned﴾ (11) (al-Rum). So "yu'iduhu" is other than "turja'un" (you will be returned); "turja'un" means on the Day of Resurrection.

His words ﴿...and it is easier for Him...﴾ (27) (al-Rum): meaning, according to your own understanding of things. Otherwise, it is not said of Allah, the Most High, that this is easy and this is easier, nor "light" or "lighter," for He does not handle things as we handle them, nor does He treat actions; rather He does by "Be," and it is.

Among this is His saying, the Most High, to Zakariyya, peace be upon him, when he wondered how he could have a son, having reached extreme old age and his wife being barren: ﴿It is easy for Me...﴾ (9) (Maryam). That is because the absoluteness of power does not stop at your causes. Likewise He said to Maryam: ﴿Thus said your Lord: It is easy for Me...﴾ (21) (Maryam).

The matter seemed strange in Maryam's view, that she should bear a child without a husband; but it is not strange in the power of Allah. If it is customary for a child to come through causes, then Allah, glorified is He, is the Creator of causes, and does what He wills without them.

We have previously spoken of the absoluteness of Allah's power in the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when the people wanted to burn him. If the matter were the rescue of Ibrahim from the fire, He would not have empowered them to seize him; or even if they seized him and threw him into the fire, it was possible for Allah to send down rain upon the fire so that it would be extinguished.

But the Truth, glorified is He, wanted to close off to the disbelievers the avenues of argument and nullify their disbelief. So they had gained mastery over him and cast him into the depths of the fire, which was blazing and burning; but they were heedless of something important: that the Lord of this fire, its Creator and the Creator of its power of burning, is exalted, and He alone is able to strip it of this property, so that His prophet Ibrahim was cast into it without being burned. In this lies the greatness and the manifestation of the proof: ﴿We said: O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim﴾ (69) (al-Anbiya').

We note the eloquence of expression in ﴿And He it is who originates creation...﴾ (27) (al-Rum). It is a restrictive construction (uslub qasr), in which the element that should be placed later is placed first, as in ﴿You alone do we worship...﴾ (5) (al-Fatiha), where the object is fronted. The object, by rule, should be placed after the verb and subject, but here it is placed first, so that worship is restricted to Allah alone, apart from others, and so that we do not associate anything with Allah, the Most High. If you said "We worship You," it would be permissible to say "and we worship other than You." Likewise here: ﴿And He it is who originates creation...﴾ (27) (al-Rum) confines the origination of creation to Allah alone, without our associating anyone with Him.

His words, the Most High, ﴿...and it is easier for Him...﴾ (27) (al-Rum): in reality, there is no "easy" or "easier" with respect to Allah, the Most High; rather, these are in our terms, and so that the Truth, glorified is He, may bring the matters closer to our understanding. Otherwise, the Truth, glorified is He, does not treat matters or handle them as we do, but He does by "Be," and it is.

Therefore, when we reflect on the words of Maryam, peace be upon her, when the angels gave her the good news of the Messiah, she said: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me...﴾ (47) (Ali 'Imran). How did Maryam understand this matter, and who informed her that the child would come without a man touching her?

Maryam understood this from the words of the angels: ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Maryam...﴾ (45) (Ali 'Imran). Had he had a father, the angels would have mentioned him; and since they attributed him to his mother, he has no father.

Then the Most High says: ﴿And His is the highest description in the heavens and the earth...﴾ (27) (al-Rum). "Lahu al-mathal al-a'la" (His is the highest likeness): meaning, Allah, the Most High, has no likeness. If something of His creation resembles Him, glorified is He, in some attribute, take it within the framework of bringing the meaning closer, and within the framework of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ (11) (al-Shura). You have existence, and Allah, the Most High, has existence; but your existence is not like the existence of Allah. You are alive and Allah is alive, but your life is not like His life, mighty and majestic is He... and so on.

As for His words ﴿al-mathal al-a'la...﴾ (27) (al-Rum), we say: "'Al" and "a'la" (highest), so it is the elative form (af'al al-tafdil) meaning: that which is not similar to and not matched by anything. Therefore the Most High says: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ (11) (al-Shura), which negates that there is a likeness to the likeness of Allah, not a likeness to Allah; because the kaf here means "like." It is as if you said: "There is nothing like the like of Him."

The Arab way of expression regarding likeness is that they say: "Zayd is like the lion in courage." You want to give me an image of Zayd's courage, so you mention the clearest thing for this quality, which is the lion; so the lion is the thing likened-to (mushabbah bihi).

Thus, the lion is stronger than Zayd in this quality; otherwise you would not make the likened-to an illustration of something you do not know.

So when you say ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ (11) (al-Shura), you mean: if there were a likeness to Allah, there would be no likeness to that likeness; so you have negated likeness all the more, because the weaker, which is the likening thing (al-mithl al-mushabbah), is weaker than the thing likened-to; so if the likeness is weaker than the one likened, and there is no likeness to the weaker, how could there be a likeness to the stronger?

Consider the beauty of the Truth, glorified is He, when He manifests to creation a likeness from their world, and makes His own essence the object of comparison, glorified and exalted is He. He says, to bring closer to our understanding the manner of His light: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp in a glass, the glass as if it were a pearly star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills...﴾ (35) (al-Nur).

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, strikes the likeness of His light with the niche. The superficial think the niche is the lamp, but Allah says: ﴿like a niche in which is a lamp...﴾ (35) (al-Nur). The niche (mishkah) is a recess in the wall, like a non-penetrating opening; if it penetrates, we call it a window. In the past they would place the lamp in this recess to illuminate the room. This recess, or niche, gathers the light and strengthens it; therefore the light in it is stronger than the light of the room, or: the lamp fills the niche more than it fills the whole room.

Reflecting on this meaning, we see that the Truth, glorified is He, does not strike for Himself a likeness of His light but for its illumination. The illumination of Allah, the Most High, is like the niche in which is the lamp, and the lamp indicates advancement in means of lighting; beneath it is, for example, the torch, a wick kindled in the air that produces black smoke; but the lamp has a glass that keeps out the air except what suffices for the wick to burn, so the light comes from it clear.

Then, in addition, it is in a glass that is not ordinary, but ﴿as if it were a pearly star...﴾ (35) (al-Nur), meaning: like a pearl that shines by its own essence. This lamp is lit from a blessed olive tree of moderate temperament, ﴿neither of the east nor of the west...﴾ (35) (al-Nur). Imagine this lamp in a narrow place, not in the whole room, but in the niche: how would its light be?

Likewise is the illumination of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, of the heavens and the earth despite their vastness, for His light encompasses them, leaving no dark place in them, like the window in relation to this lamp we described.

This likeness has a famous story in Arabic literature, for Abu Tammam(1) perceived it in his praise of one of the caliphs, and when he wanted to combine for him the qualities and gifts of the Arabs: generosity, courage, forbearance, and intelligence, he said in praise:

The boldness of 'Amr in the generosity of Hatim,
And the forbearance of al-Ahnaf in the intelligence of Iyas.

'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib was renowned for courage and boldness; Hatim al-Ta'i was renowned for generosity; al-Ahnaf ibn Qays was renowned for forbearance, until it was said: "the most forbearing of the Arabs," nothing ever angering him or moving him from his forbearance, so much so that a group intended to provoke him out of it, following him on the road and mocking him while he laughed, until he approached the tribe. He looked at these youths and said: "O youths, we have come close to the tribe; if in..."

1 He is Habib ibn Aws ibn Ta'i. Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani said in al-Aghani (p. 1738): "A poet of subtle wit and precise meanings, who followed in badi' and tibaq a path no one before him had taken, though they were the ones who opened it for him."

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿He has propounded to you a parable from yourselves: Do you have, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal therein and fear them as you fear one another? Thus do We detail the signs for a people who use reason.﴾ (30:28)

The parable (ḍarb al-mathal) is one of the Qur'an's methods of clarification and of bringing matters closer to understanding. In another place He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example — that of a mosquito or what is above it...﴾ (2:26). And He says: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it...﴾ (22:73). This is frequent in the Book of Allah, and a parable is struck to make a truth manifest. The word ḍarb here does not mean inflicting a harmful effect on the one struck, but producing a beneficial, positive effect, as in His saying: ﴿And others travelling through the land...﴾ (73:20).

Our saying, in the matter of minting coins: ḍarb fī kadhā (striking a coin in such-and-such), implies that the striking leaves a lasting mark on what is struck: in the earth, by stirring up its treasures and extracting its hoards; and in the coin, by leaving a prominent imprint that hands cannot erase in circulation. It is as if the parable strikes a thing that is obscure, clarifying it plainly, as a coin is minted, and makes the idea firmly established in the mind with clear features. The striking has three elements: the striker (al-ḍārib), the struck (al-maḍrūb), and that with which it is struck (al-maḍrūb bihi).

It is related in the domain of proverbs that a man went out hunting with his equipment: the kinānah, which is the quiver of arrows, the arrows, and the bow. When he saw a gazelle, he began to prepare his quiver and bow for shooting, but the gazelle did not give him time and fled. Another man, who had seen what happened, said to him: "Before the shooting, fill the quivers." It became a proverb, and although it was said on a particular occasion, it is struck on every similar occasion, and is said in any situation exactly as it is, with the same words, without changing anything in it.

Thus, when you see a student who neglects his studies and studies just before the exam, or when you see someone who undertakes a matter without preparing its requirements, you may say: "Before the shooting, fill the quivers." So this expression has its clear meaning, and it has taken root in the mind until it became a proverb that is struck.

And you may say to one who dominated you and claimed to be stronger than you: "If you are a wind, then you have met a whirlwind."

Allah, the Exalted, strikes parables for Himself to clarify and to bring meanings closer to understanding. Therefore He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example — that of a mosquito or what is above it...﴾ (2:26). Here some quibblers who love to find fault with the words of Allah stop and say: since Allah is not ashamed to cite the mosquito or what is above it, then by a stronger argument [He should not be ashamed of something bigger], so why does He say "or what is above it"?

This shows their failure to understand the meaning intended by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The meaning is: "or what is above it" in strangeness, and in smallness and insignificance, not what is above it in size.[2]

Among the parables that Allah has struck for us to clarify the matter of tawḥīd is His saying: ﴿Allah presents a parable: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.﴾ (39:29)

The one who takes another god alongside Allah is like the one who serves two masters, whose masters are not in agreement but are quarrelling and opposed to one another. If he pleases one, he angers the other, and he is worn out between them. Is this servant equal to another servant who serves a single master? Likewise in the worship of Allah alone, with no partner. By the parable the matter is made clear and firmly fixed in minds. Therefore He says: "I am not ashamed to strike parables, because I want to make clear to My servants the realities and show them the meanings."

﴿He has propounded to you a parable from yourselves...﴾ (30:28)

In this verse, and by this parable, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, at the peak of the education of the faith in belief, affirms the oneness of Allah and His uniqueness (aḥadiyyah). Oneness (waḥdiyyah) is one thing and uniqueness (aḥadiyyah) is another: oneness means that He, glorified is He, is one, with no other individual alongside Him; but this single individual may in its essence be composed of parts. So He described Himself, glorified is He, as Aḥad, meaning: not composed of parts.

Allah affirmed this truth in His Qur'an with proofs and demonstrations, and struck a parable for it. Here He strikes for us a parable from ourselves to affirm this oneness.

His saying ﴿from yourselves...﴾ (30:28) means: not far from you, and the nearest thing to a human being is himself. So the clearest parable is one that is drawn from yourself. Among this is His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves...﴾ (9:128), meaning: of your kind, whose upbringing you know, whose nature and conduct you know.

But what is the intended parable?

The parable: ﴿Do you have, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal therein and fear them as you fear one another?...﴾ (30:28)

He, glorified is He, says: I want to strike for you a parable to show that the one God must, by reason, not be associated with other things. The parable is that I provide for you, and of My provision to you are wealth and slaves. Have you then given the provision that Allah has given you, and the slaves, and said to them: "You are partners with us in our wealth; you dispose of it as we dispose of it," and then given them absolute freedom and disposal, so that they are free like you, and you fear them lest you dispose of something without them, as you fear one another? Have you done that? Rather, would you accept it for yourselves? Then why would you accept it with regard to Allah, the Exalted, and be content for His servants to share in His dominion?

You have not accepted this for your masters, who are human beings like you, whom you have owned by the law of Allah, so that they obey your command. This is the meaning of ﴿from yourselves...﴾ (30:28), that is: from among humankind; they are like you in humanity, and your ownership of them is not absolute. You own their necks and you own the movement of their lives, but you do not own, for example, their killing, nor can you prevent them from fulfilling their needs; you do not own their hearts or their wills. Moreover, it is an ownership that may lapse from you, as when you sell or free them, or even by death. Yet even so, you have not taken them as partners. So it is shameful that you should ascribe to Allah what you disdain for yourselves.

We notice here that Allah did not argue with them about the matter of partners in the form of a statement from Him, glorified is He, but chose the form of a question, which is more eloquent in establishing the truth: ﴿Do you have, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided for you...﴾ (30:28)

You do not turn from a statement to asking about it unless you know and are confident that the answer will be in your favour. For example, when a person mentions your favour, and you say, informing: "I did such and such for you," the statement may be true or false, and he may deny it, saying: "No, you did nothing for me."

But when you ask, saying: "Did I not do such and such for you?" you force him toward a reality he cannot deny, cannot escape, and can only acknowledge your favour; at the least he must be silent, and silence means that things are as you said.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, who knows best His creation, asks: ﴿Do you have, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in...?﴾ (30:28). They must say: "No, we have no partners in our wealth. Then why have you made partners for Allah?"

As for His saying ﴿in what We have provided for you...﴾ (30:28), we have already spoken on the matter of provision and said: Allah, the Exalted, is the Provider, yet He respects the ownership of His creatures and respects their striving, because He is the bestower of this ownership and He does not take back His gift from His creatures. Therefore, when He wished to move the hearts of His creatures toward one another, He said: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan...?﴾ (2:245), counting your charity to your poor brother as a loan which He returns to you multiplied.

Provision is not limited to wealth, as some suppose; rather, your provision is everything from which you benefit, and it is a provision you must pour out upon those who need it, and extend to those who lack it. The strong man's provision is strength, which he extends to the weak; the scholar's provision is knowledge, which he restores to the ignorant; the forbearing man's provision is forbearance, which he extends to the angry, and so on. Otherwise, wealth is the least of the kinds of provision, for the poor man who owns no wealth and to whom no one has given charity, the most that happens to him is that he goes hungry, and in this state it is permitted for him to ask people. We have never seen anyone die of hunger.

But if need drives the poor man to ask, he should ask gently and softly. If he is hungry, he should not ask people for money, but for a morsel of food, a piece of cheese, or whatever is available to satisfy his hunger. No one doubts the one who asks for food, because he asks only out of hunger, even if he asks you while he is full and you give him what he can eat. But the one who asks for money, we may suspect him of greed or of intent to hoard. Therefore, the most excellent of begging is the begging for sustenance.

So in the story of al-Khiḍr and Mūsā, peace be upon them: ﴿...until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them...﴾ (18:77). When they refused them even a morsel of food, they deserved to be described as the basest of people. The Sharia permits the hungry person to ask the stingy for food, and if he refuses, the hungry person may take it, even by force; and if his matter is brought before the judge, the judge supports him. Therefore they say: "The seeker of sustenance does not transgress."

Allah, the Exalted, has guaranteed your provision, but He has made causes for provision, and all that is required of you is to take these causes, then not preoccupy your mind with anxiety about it. Beware of supposing that effort is the source of provision: effort is a cause, and provision is from Allah, and all you must do is seek out the causes. If your provision is delayed, then ease your soul, for you do not know its address, but He knows your address and will come to you knocking at your door.[3]

What wearies people is that one of them remains anxious and preoccupied with the matter of provision. If he knew that the One who created him and brought him into existence has guaranteed his provision, he would find rest. If the causes of provision fail you in one direction, be reassured, for it will come to you from another direction.

We mention here the story of ʿUrwah ibn Udhaynah,[4] who was a friend of Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik in Medina before Hishām assumed the caliphate. When Hishām became Commander of the Faithful and moved to Damascus in Syria, ʿUrwah was struck by poverty. When his condition became hard, he recalled his old friendship with Hishām and the affection between them, so he went to him in Damascus, hoping he would relieve his distress.

ʿUrwah came to Damascus and asked permission to see the Caliph; he was granted it. He entered, presented his need to his friend, hoping entirely that he would do him justice and console his heart. But Hishām was not successful in replying to his friend, for he said: "You came from Medina asking me for your need, while you are the one who said: 'I know, and extravagance is not my nature, that what is my provision will come to me.'"

ʿUrwah said, after his friend had broken his heart: "May Allah reward you well on my behalf, O Commander of the Faithful. You have alerted me when I was heedless, and reminded me when I had forgotten," then he turned and left.

Then Hishām was troubled within himself, recalled ʿUrwah's affection and friendship, felt that he had wronged him, and his conscience reproached him. So he summoned the treasurer and ordered a great gift for ʿUrwah, and sent someone after him with it.

But every time the messenger reached a station, he found that ʿUrwah had already left it, until he reached Medina. He knocked on ʿUrwah's door. The messenger was tactful, so when ʿUrwah opened the door he said: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Messengers of Hishām. This is Hishām's gift to you; he did not wish you to carry it yourself, fearing for you from highway robbers, or to bear the burden of carrying it, so we have sent it to you."

ʿUrwah said: "May Allah reward the Commander of the Faithful well. Tell him: you reminded me of the first line, and if you had reminded me of the second, you would have eased and been eased. You said:

'I know, and extravagance is not my nature, that what is my provision will come to me.
I strive toward it, and it tires me; I seek it, and if I sit still it will come to me without my trouble.'"[5]

Then, after this parable, He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Thus do We detail the signs for a people who use reason.﴾ (30:28), that is: We make them clear and explain them, such that if they were presented to unadulterated reason free of desire, it would arrive at nothing but them. The meaning of ﴿who use reason﴾ (30:28) derives from reason ('aql), and it is called 'aql because it restrains its possessor and holds him back from what is unseemly.

Some suppose that reason was given only so that you may roam freely in your thoughts; rather, it came to restrain those thoughts and regulate conduct. It says to you: "Restrain your thoughts, examine them; do not let them run free according to your desire, doing what you like, but do what is right and say what is fitting." So We have not fallen short in explanation or in clarification.

The role of pure reason, and its agreement even with revelation, is evident in the conduct of al-Fārūq ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while revelation was descending upon him: ʿUmar would come and advise the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on matters, and then revelation would descend...

[1] Occasion of revelation: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, he said: The people of polytheism used to say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am; here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns." So Allah revealed: ﴿He has propounded to you a parable from yourselves...﴾ (30:28). Cited by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr (6/492), attributed to al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh.

[2] Ibn Kathīr's statement in his tafsīr (1/64): "His saying ﴿or what is above it﴾ (2:26) has two opinions: one, what is below it in smallness and insignificance; this is the view of al-Kisā'ī and Abū ʿUbayd, mentioned by al-Rāzī and most of the verifiers. The other, what is above it, for there is nothing more insignificant or smaller than the mosquito; this is the view of Qatādah ibn Di'āmah and the preference of Ibn Jarīr."

[3] From the poetry of the Sheikh, may Allah be pleased with him:
"Seek out the causes of provision, and do not let yourself be preoccupied with worry after them,
for you do not know its address, while your provision knows your address."

[4] He is ʿUrwah ibn Yaḥyā (known as Udhaynah) ibn Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith al-Laythī: a foremost love poet from Medina, counted among the jurists and transmitters of ḥadīth as well, though poetry predominates in his reputation. He died around 130 AH (al-Aʿlām of al-Ziriklī 4/227). Imam Abū ʿUbayd al-Bakrī said in al-Tanbīh ʿalā awhām Abī ʿAlī fī amālīh (p. 29): "Mālik and other imams narrated from him."

[5] Khayr al-Dīn al-Ziriklī mentioned these verses in al-Aʿlām (4/227), attributing them to ʿUrwah ibn Udhaynah. al-Iṣbahānī recorded his reports in al-Aghānī (p. 1911) and mentioned this account between ʿUrwah and Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, citing these two verses.

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 29:

They followed their desires, because they chose to worship One who has no method (manhaj) and no obligation (taklif). They worshipped a god who has no command and no prohibition, for whom falling short brings no punishment and work brings no reward. All of this is from the inspiration of the desire they followed.

Beware of letting desire (hawa) precede reason ('aql), for when you let desire precede, reason becomes a justifying reason (ʿaql tabriri), which tries to give you what you want regardless of its outcome. Rather, first define your desire by reason, then make the movement of your life follow it.

Some think that desire is blameworthy in every respect, but a single desire is not blameworthy. What is blameworthy is multiple, conflicting desires, because a single desire in the heart mobilizes the whole body to serve it. When my desire is to go to a certain place, the body strives and plans for this goal: it determines the route, prepares provisions, and takes the means of reaching it.

This single desire is what is meant in the noble hadith: "None of you truly believes until his desire is subordinate to what I have brought" (1). The Prophet (ﷺ) did not forbid a person from having a desire that his soul inclines to and loves, because that desire helps him in striving and struggle in the movement of life.

But when desires multiply, you have one beloved and another person has a different beloved, and they undoubtedly conflict and contend with one another. God, exalted is He, wants the community of faith to have all its desires support one another, to cooperate and not conflict, and to unite and not clash, because the clash of desires dissipates the movement of life and wastes its fruit.

As for when my desire is your desire, and it is a desire that is not human but one that the Creator, glorified and exalted, has laid down for us, then we will agree on it, and the movement of our life will bear fruit through it: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ (al-Mulk 14).

We have said before that the craftsman of a thing in this world attaches with it a manual (katalog) explaining how to maintain it. The Truth, glorified and exalted, is the One who created you, and He is the One who defines your desire for you. The first failure in the universe is that people created by God want to set for humans a law for their preservation from their own selves.

We say: this is not valid, because whoever legislates and sets down for people what will preserve them must possess certain conditions. The first of them: he must have comprehensive knowledge that is not subject to correction. You, O human, your knowledge is very limited, and you often find yourself correcting it after a while, and it becomes clear to you that it is unsuitable and unfit.

Indeed, you may even discover the corruption of your own opinion and retract it in favor of another. Likewise, whoever legislates a single desire for people must be equal to them all in relation to it, and must not benefit himself from what he legislates. Otherwise, if he had some benefit, he would incline toward what benefits him, and so he would not be objective, as we have seen in communism, capitalism, and other human doctrines.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, is alone the One who cannot be corrected, because His knowledge encompasses everything, nothing is hidden from Him, and all creation for whom He legislates stands equal before Him. All are His servants; He favors none of them, and He does not distinguish one over another. He, glorified is He, has no consort and no offspring from His creation.

Therefore He reassures us with His saying: ﴿And that He, exalted is the majesty of our Lord, has not taken a consort or a son﴾ (al-Jinn 3).

It is as if God, exalted is He, says: be reassured, for your Lord has no consort who could influence Him, and no son who would favor him. The consort and the son are the point of weakness and the cause of inclination in the matter of legislation.

Likewise, He, glorified is He, does not benefit from what He legislates for us, because He created us by His power, and He is independent of us: the obedience of the obedient does not benefit Him, and the disobedience of the disobedient does not harm Him. Thus He alone fulfills the conditions of legislation, and He alone deserves them, and He is the explanation of the single desire upon which all creation gathers.

We have mentioned before, regarding legislation, that you should not look at what is taken from you, but compare what you took with what you gave. The one who prevented you from transgressing against others, though you are a single individual, has prevented all creation from transgressing against you. So legislation is, in fact, in your own interest.

Thus, if we followed, we would take our one desire from one God, Who is God, exalted is He. But the tragedy is that they neither listened to this speech nor understood it.

﴿But those who did wrong followed their desires without knowledge...﴾ (al-Rum 29). They did wrong because they set aside the single desire and pushed it aside, and took up various desires that conflicted and contended, so they reached no conclusion from them.

They wronged only themselves by associating partners with God, and God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, association [with God] is a great injustice﴾ (Luqman 13). They wronged themselves when they gave their souls fleeting desire and transient pleasure, and neglected the consequence of that. They are either hateful toward their souls, or they love them with a foolish love, and this is the affliction of desire when it precedes reason and controls it.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿without knowledge...﴾ (al-Rum 29). First: what is knowledge? In the universe there are propositions that we affirm with certainty. If what we affirm corresponds to reality and we can demonstrate it, as we teach a small child: God is One, and if he can demonstrate it, then it is knowledge; if he cannot, then it is imitation (taqlid).

Similarly, someone who says, for example: the earth is spherical, and indeed it is so. But whoever stubbornly insists until now that it is not spherical, while the reality is that it is spherical, this is ignorance (jahl).

So we say: ignorance is not merely not knowing; rather, ignorance is knowing a proposition contrary to reality. Therefore we distinguish between the ignorant (jahil) and the unlettered (ummi). The unlettered person has an empty mind, with no proposition at all; if you inform him of a proposition, he takes it from you without obstinacy or stubbornness. The ignorant person, however, holds a false proposition stubbornly, so you must first remove the corrupt proposition before you can convey to him the correct one.

If a proposition does not reach the level where we can affirm it with certainty, then consider: if affirmation and negation in it are equal, it is doubt (shakk). Thus doubt is an unaffirmed proposition in which affirmation and negation are equal. If affirmation prevails and outweighs, it is conjecture (zann); but if negation prevails, it is illusion (wahm). So we have, then, among the types of propositions: knowledge ('ilm), ignorance (jahl), imitation (taqlid), conjecture (zann), and illusion (wahm).

So the Truth, glorified and exalted, wants the desire that our life's movement serves to be a desire grounded in knowledge and in a proposition affirmed with certainty, corresponding to reality, and supported by evidence. But since these people followed their scattered desires and took them without their foundations in knowledge, I will complete for them what they wanted and help them to what they loved: ﴿So who can guide one whom God has sent astray...﴾ (al-Rum 29). They have nullified their minds and disabled them, and they have loved disbelief after We had presented to them the proofs and evidence.

So: nothing remains but that I help you in what you believe and assist you in it, and I seal your hearts so that no faith enters them and disbelief does not leave them, for I am the Lord who helps His servant in what he wants. Thus God misguides these people, meaning He aids them in the error they are upon after they have loved it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿God has sealed their hearts and their hearing, and over their sight is a veil, and for them is a great punishment﴾ (al-Baqarah 7).

Therefore we warn those who are afflicted with a calamity and then do not console themselves, and do not forget, and cling to grief. We warn them and say: do not leave the door of grief open; close it with the nails of contentment, or else sorrows will follow one another upon you, for God, exalted is He, is a Lord who helps His servant in what he loves, even the one who is angry at His decree.

So the meaning of ﴿So who can guide one whom God has sent astray...﴾ (al-Rum 29) is: who can rescue him? And who will set for him a law for his preservation if his Lord has abandoned him and left him to do whatever occurs to him? No one. And if you advise your companion and repeat the advice but he does not obey you, you abandon him. Indeed, one of the wise men said: advise your companion from morning until noon, and from noon until afternoon; if he does not comply, leave him to go astray, or complete for him the rest of the day in deceit.

We have previously discussed the correct method of examining propositions so that you reach the right judgment about them. Do not enter knowledge with a prior desire; rather, bring out everything in your heart that supports this proposition or opposes it, then examine the proposition objectively. What rational scales are persuaded of and weigh in favor of, admit into your heart.

What now wearies people is that they discuss the question of Islam, for example, while their hearts have an inclination toward communism, for example, and so they reach an unsound conclusion.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they have no helpers﴾ (al-Rum 29). That is: would that they had someone who could rescue them if God misguided them, having sealed their hearts so that no faith enters them and no disbelief leaves them. They have no helper from God who would help them, nor any protector who would protect them from God, and He, glorified is He, protects and is not protected against.

(1) Narrated by Ibn Abi 'Asim in "al-Sunnah" (1/12) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, and cited by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali in "Jami' al-'Ulum" (p. 460), who declared it weak.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. The nature of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no alteration to the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.﴾ (30)

The address here is to the Prophet (ﷺ): O Muhammad, since this is the case, and since they have followed their desires and gone astray, and persisted in their error, then leave them alone and do not be affected by their turning away.

Just as his Lord said to him: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers.﴾ (26:3)

And He said to him: ﴿So perhaps you would kill yourself following them, out of grief, if they do not believe in this message.﴾ (18:6)

So there is nothing for you, O Muhammad, but to convey (the message). Leave them to Me, and beware lest their obstinacy affect you, or that their conspiring against you, or their plotting against you, grieve you. For My word has already gone forth that they will not prevail over you, rather you will prevail over them.

This is a Qur'anic principle which I declare, and which is recorded for Me: ﴿And已 Our word has already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would indeed be helped, and that Our soldiers would indeed be the victorious.﴾ (37:171–173)

And: ﴿Allah will surely help those who help Him…﴾ (22:40)

And: ﴿If you help Allah, He will help you…﴾ (47:7)

This is an established Qur'anic principle, settled and beyond dispute, and it is on our tongues and in our hearts. If our reality comes contrary to this principle, then the reality of earlier nations has already confirmed it, and something similar will happen to you. Therefore the Truth reassures His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), then to Us they will return.﴾ (40:77)

So here, ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining…﴾ (30): that is, leave these misguided people, devote yourself to your mission of calling to Allah, and beware lest they distract you from your call.

The meaning of "setting the face toward the religion" is: make your direction toward your Lord alone, and do not turn aside to the right or the left. The face is singled out, though it signifies the whole self, because the face is the mark of facing toward something.

From this is His saying: ﴿Everything is perishing except His face…﴾ (28:88), meaning: His Essence, may He be exalted.

As for the meaning of ﴿ḥanīfan﴾ (30): this word is one of the words that has caused confusion among those who try to find fault with the words of Allah, since the meaning of ḥanīf is one whose legs incline, so that you see in his leg an inward bend; it is said: "in his foot there is ḥanaf," meaning inclination. So the meaning is: "So set your face toward the religion, inclining." Yes, this is the meaning, but inclining away from what?

One must understand the meaning here, so that you do not accuse the style of the Qur'an. The Messenger (ﷺ) came to reform a corrupt, deviant society that professed polytheism and idolatry. So the meaning is: inclining away from this corruption, inclining away from this polytheism and this idolatry which you came to demolish and eliminate. And the meaning of "he inclined away from falsehood" is: he went toward the truth.

And (aqim) here means "establish" in the plural, since the address to the Messenger is an address to his community, as evidenced by His saying in the verse after it: ﴿turning back to Him…﴾ (30:31). Had the command been to him alone, it would have said "turning back to Him" in the singular. A similar example is His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed time…﴾ (65:1).

So the address is to the whole community in the person of the Messenger of Allah, because he (ﷺ) is the conveyer, and the conveyer is the one who receives the command and is convinced of it first, so that he can convey it. Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, said: ﴿There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern…﴾ (33:21).

And He said ﴿ḥanīfan﴾ (30) because messengers come only upon a corruption that has encompassed people in general. Just as the Truthful, glorified is He, placed in the body a physical immunity, He placed in it a moral immunity. A person is moved by his soul toward a desire and overcomes it, so he falls into it, but at the moment he finishes with it he regrets it, his conscience reproaches him, he weeps over what he did, and perhaps he hates whoever helped him in the sin.

This is the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah), and it is a sign of the existence of good in a person, and this is the self-immunity that proceeds from the self.

There is a difference between one upon whom sin descends and confronts his path, and one who arranges for it and strives toward it. This is clear in His saying: ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon…﴾ (4:17).

The difference is like that between one who goes to Paris to seek knowledge, and a young woman crosses his path, and one who goes to Paris because he heard of the allurements there. The first, generally, reproaches himself, and within him the self-reproaching soul and self-immunity stir; but the other, his soul has grown accustomed to sin and has been enticed by it, so there must be an immunity for him that is not from his own self, but from the society around him. Society must prevent him and restrain his hands.

Immunity in society does not mean that it is an ideal society that knows no sin; sins do occur in it, but they are scattered across people's desires: this one inclines to theft, this one inclines to looking at what is forbidden, this one loves such-and-such... and so on.

So, among people there are areas of strength and areas of weakness, and whoever is strong in something must restrain the weak in it, rebuke him and set him right. Therefore He says: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾ (103:1–3)

When corruption becomes widespread and overwhelms, as He said about the Jews: ﴿They did not forbid one another from wrongdoing that they committed…﴾ (5:79), the society also loses its immunity. Then heaven must intervene with a new messenger and a new miracle to rescue these people.

Then He says: ﴿The nature of Allah upon which He created mankind…﴾ (30). We see people taking vaccines and serums to protect against diseases; likewise the Truthful, glorified is He—and to Him belongs the highest likeness—placed this vaccinating serum in every human soul, even in the physical constitution.

Do you not see His saying regarding the formation of man: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed…﴾ (22:5)

The "formed" (mukhallaqah) is that which forms the organs, and the "unformed" (ghayr mukhallaqah) is the stored reserve in the body, by which any defect in the formed organs is compensated; it supplies them with what sets them right. Likewise in values, the religion of Allah came upon the nature of Allah upon which He created mankind. So when desires intrude and heedlessness occurs, immunity comes: either from the self itself, or from society, or through a messenger and a new method.

Allah has honored the community of Muhammad by making its Messenger the Seal of the Messengers. This is good news for us that goodness remains within us and continues until the Day of Resurrection, and the community of Muslims will never be corrupted so completely as to lose all this immunity. If a group within it becomes corrupt, another group arises to set it right. This is clear in the words of the Prophet (ﷺ):

"A group of my community will continue to prevail upon the truth; those who forsake them will not harm them, until the command of Allah comes while they remain so." (1)

And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Goodness is in me and in my community until the Day of Resurrection." (2)

Otherwise, if corruption were to pervade this community, the matter would call for something else.

When we read the verse, we find that the word ﴿fiṭrata⦆ (30) is in the accusative, and there is nothing preceding it that governs it, so why is it in the accusative? The style here wants to draw your attention to the reason for the accusative, and to the omitted verb here, so that you search for it yourself. It is as if He said: "So set your face toward the religion, inclining, and adhere to the nature of Allah upon which He created mankind."

Therefore the grammarians call this style the style of al-ighra' (urging/incitement), which is that I urge you toward a beloved matter and encourage you to do it. Likewise the Truthful, glorified is He, urges His Messenger (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) to set his face toward the pure religion, to adhere to the nature of Allah, and not to turn toward these corrupters or those who obstruct him.

And fiṭrah means creation (khilqah)(3), as He said: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth…﴾ (12:101), meaning: their Creator. The fiṭrah intended here is His saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.﴾ (51:56)

So adhere to this nature, and know that you are created for worship.

Or: the fiṭrat of Allah means: the disposition which Allah deposited in your constitution since Allah created Adam, and from him created his offspring, and made them witness against themselves: ﴿Am I not your Lord? They said, "Yes…"﴾ (7:172)

We have previously explained how in each of us there is a living particle from our father Adam that remains in each one of us; a human being arises only from the living male germ that fertilizes the ovum, and when this process is traced back, it must reach Adam, peace be upon him.

This remaining offspring in each of us is what witnessed the first covenant that Allah took from us. Otherwise, how did the disbelievers in the Jahiliyyah, to whom the Messenger of Allah came to guide, acknowledge to Allah the creation: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah…"﴾ (39:38)

From where did they know this truth? It was transmitted to them from this first covenant. Since that covenant, no one among the creatures of Allah has dared to claim this creation for himself, so this matter has remained sound in minds despite the corruption that has occurred in human beliefs.

This matter remains established by the remnant of this first covenant, even among disbelievers and atheists. When events overwhelm them and their means become constricted, you see them saying, spontaneously and without thought: "O Lord!" They do not call upon an idol or a tree, nor do they go to their gods that they fabricated, for they know that they are falsehood upon falsehood, and fraud upon fraud.

Now they do not deceive themselves nor lie to themselves. Now, in times of hardship and the arrival of distress, there is none to whom they turn but Allah, none but the Truth and the sound fiṭrah upon which Allah created mankind.

Since Allah has created us upon this fiṭrah, there is no alteration of what He willed, ﴿There is no alteration to the creation of Allah…﴾ (30), meaning: no one has been able to say, "I created the heavens and the earth," nor to say, "I created you," or "I created myself."

﴿That is the correct religion…﴾ (30), that is, the true religion. ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ (30), that is, they do not know with the knowledge in its true reality, which we have explained as the certain affirmation of a proposition that corresponds to reality and for which evidence can be established.

1 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1920), Kitab al-Imarah, from the hadith of Thawban (may Allah be pleased with him), and narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7311), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1921) from the hadith of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah with the wording: "A group of my community will continue to prevail upon the truth until the command of Allah comes to them while they are still prevailing."

2 Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani said: I do not know it, but its meaning is sound. Mentioned by al-Qari in "al-Asrar al-Marfu'ah" (457), and likewise al-Suyuti in "al-Durar al-Muntathirah" (220), and al-Ajluni in "Kashf al-Khafa'" (1/476).

3 Ibn 'Atiyyah said: What is relied upon in interpreting this word is that it is the natural constitution and disposition that is in the child's nature, which is prepared so that he may distinguish Allah's creatures by it, derive evidence from them for his Lord, know His laws, and believe in them. (Cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir 7/5284).

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Turning penitently to Him, and fear Him, and establish the prayer, and do not be among the polytheists﴾ [30:31]

Anāba (to turn back in repentance): it means to return and sever one's connection with other than the Truth ﴿to Him...﴾ [30:31] to God. So there is no relationship with creation in matters of belief; he makes his entire relationship with God.

From it they call the fang (nāb) because it cuts things. They say nāba ilā al-rushd and nāba ilā rushdihi, both meaning: he returned. And wherever there is a return, there is an origin to which one returns, and that is the origin of fiṭrah (the innate disposition).

His exalted saying ﴿and fear Him...﴾ [30:31] is because it is not permissible for you to turn penitently to God, and return to Him, and keep Him in mind, and then turn away from His method which He legislated to organize the movement of your life. Turning in repentance alone and faith in God are not sufficient; rather, it is necessary to apply the method through the fear of God. Therefore the Qur'an often combines faith and righteous deeds: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds...﴾ [26:227]

Because the benefit and fruit of faith, after you believe in the true God, and that His method is truthful, and in it is your benefit and safety in the movement of your life, and that it is what brings you to the happiness of both abodes, none of this has meaning except through action and application.

﴿and fear Him...﴾ [30:31] That is: fear His anger, and place between you and the anger of God a shield. This shield is realized by following the method in "do" and "do not do." We have previously discussed the meaning of taqwā (God-consciousness/piety) and said that it carries two meanings that some think contradict each other: we say "fear God" and "fear the Fire." But the meaning is one in the end, because the meaning of "fear God" is: make between you and the punishment and anger of God a shield, and this same meaning is that of "fear the Fire," i.e., keep away from its causes so that you do not touch it.

His exalted saying: ﴿and establish the prayer...﴾ [30:31] Establish the prayer: perform it in its most complete form, and perform it in the way He loves from you in its performance. When I call you, "God is greatest," you must turn toward Me, and you, when you answer the call, do not come to help Me with anything, nor do I benefit from you in anything; rather, you are the one who benefits from this meeting, and you draw from Me help and strength, and you take a charge of faith and certainty from your Lord.

We have said: what is your image of a machine presented to its maker every day five times—would any defect remain in it? Therefore our Prophet ﷺ taught us that when a matter distresses us, we should hasten to prayer, and the Prophet ﷺ himself used to do so when something was hard for him or when the means were constrained. Otherwise, what is the meaning of faith in God if you do not turn to Him?

And since your Lord is unseen, He, glorified is He, also reforms you unseen, and from where you do not know. Therefore our Lord commanded us to establish the prayer and made it the pillar of religion and the foundation that never drops from you in any state. Zakāh and Ḥajj, for example, drop from the poor and from one who is unable, and fasting drops from the sick or the traveler during their illness or journey, then he makes it up after the cause of breaking the fast ends.

As for the prayer, it is the constant pillar: not once in a lifetime, nor once in a year, but five times in the day and night. Thereby the declaration of loyalty to God the Exalted is a constant declaration, and this, if it indicates anything, indicates the greatness of the human being and his station before his Lord and Creator.

We have previously said: if you wish to meet one of the officials or people of rank, how much you suffer until you are admitted, and the appointment and place must be set for you, and even the subject of the meeting and what you will say in it, and then the one being met may end it whenever he wishes.

Thus, you possess none of the elements of this meeting. But in your meeting with your Lord—Mighty and Majestic—the matter is the opposite: your Lord is the One who seeks you and calls you to turn toward Him, not once but five times every day, and He permits you to confide to Him whatever you love, and to ask Him for whatever you want.

And you may end the meeting yourself by saying: "Peace be upon you." If you wish to prolong the meeting, or to seclude yourself in the house of your Lord, He, glorified is He, does not tire until you tire. So this is not servitude, but honor and sovereignty.

How beautiful is what the poet said on this meaning (1):
It suffices my self honor that I am a servant [of Him]—
He welcomes me without appointments, the Lord
He is in His holiness the Most Mighty, yet I meet [Him] whenever and wherever I wish.

And because prayer has this station among the pillars of Islam, it was not entrusted to revelation as the other pillars were; rather, it was enjoined directly by God upon His Prophet ﷺ when his Lord summoned him to meet Him in the heavens during the Night Journey of the Ascension (al-Mi'rāj).

We have previously illustrated this—and to God belongs the highest likeness—by a head of a work who issues his orders by telephone or by a signature on a paper. When a matter of importance arises, he summons the competent employee to his office and gives him the order directly because of its importance. Likewise was the prayer, and likewise was it imposed upon our master, the Messenger of God ﷺ, by direct obligation.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and do not be among the polytheists﴾ [30:31] Here there is a pause: how, after turning penitently to God and taqwā, and after the command to establish the prayer, does He say ﴿and do not be among the polytheists﴾ [30:31]? And where is shirk in one who performs the teachings on this method? They said: the shirk forbidden here is not associating with God another god; rather, they associated with God another intention. So shirk here means riyā' (showing off), and looking to people instead of to God.

Therefore they say: doing deeds for people is riyā', and abandoning deeds for the sake of people is shirk. So one who prays or builds a mosque for God for fame, and that people may praise him, is a show-off, and he is disappointed and a loser, because people benefit from his deed and he gains nothing from his deed.

As for one who abandons action out of fear of falling into riyā', refraining from zakāh, for example, out of fear of being accused of riyā', he is, God forbid, a polytheist, because people benefit from the deed even if it is riyā'; but if you refrain from action, people gain nothing from you.

So the meaning of ﴿and do not be among the polytheists﴾ [30:31] is: hidden shirk, which is riyā'.
