If we look at the positions of scholars on the question of riba, some permit it and some prohibit it, and the latter are the majority. Suppose they were equal, those who prohibit and those who permit: what is Allah's ruling on a matter in which the ijtihad (independent reasoning) is equal?

The Prophet (ﷺ) clarified this matter for us in his saying: "The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters. Whoever avoids doubtful matters has protected his religion and his honour, and whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like the shepherd who grazes around the sanctuary, about to graze within it. Verily every king has a sanctuary; verily the sanctuary of Allah is His prohibitions."(5)

Did the Messenger of Allah say: "whoever does the doubtful matters," or "whoever leaves the doubtful matters"? So whoever falls into doubtful matters has not protected himself, neither his religion nor his honour. Would anyone accept to be described thus? It is strange that we hear someone say: "What is the connection of honour to this matter?" We say: By Allah, even the non-believer who has no religion disdains to be called a usurer; his honour does not accept it, let alone his religion.

Therefore, those cunning people who wish to make it lawful, and who wish to live on people's blood, do not realise that utilitarianism is the law by which Allah governs His creatures, so that He makes the good deed tenfold for them. This is why the Jews say: "How do you forbid riba when Allah deals with you by it?"

Yes, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, deals with us by riba and gives us with increase, because this increase does not diminish what He has. But increase taken from people, from the needy, weighs them down and increases them in poverty and need.

Then leave all this aside and reflect on the environment you live in: in every country there are people who love riba and deal in it. Have you seen a usurer die in good condition? Did a usurer die with his wealth intact? No, because Allah, exalted is He, would not say: ﴿Allah destroys riba...﴾ (2:276), and then leave a usurer whose wealth grows, handing it to him until he dies. If he becomes wealthy for a time, his wealth is only a snare for him and an exaggeration of his harm, as in the report: "When Allah is angry with a person, He provides him with sustenance from the unlawful; and if His anger intensifies against him, He blesses him in it."

And read the saying of

1 Ibn 'Abbas said regarding this verse: "Riba is of two kinds: a riba with no harm in it, and a riba that is not proper. As for the riba that has no harm, it is a man's gift to another man, desiring its excess or multiples of it." (Recorded by Ibn Abi Hatim.) In another statement of his he said: it is what people give one another; a man gives another a gift desiring that he give more than it. (Recorded by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari.) al-Suyuti cited these two reports in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/495.
2 Al-Shawkani said in Nayl al-Awtar (5/232): "What indicates that a loan which draws a benefit to the lender is not lawful is what al-Bayhaqi recorded in al-Ma'rifah from Fudalah ibn 'Ubayd as a mawquf report with the wording: 'every loan that draws a benefit is a form of riba'; and he narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra from Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and Ibn 'Abbas as mawquf reports. al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah narrated it from a hadith of 'Ali (peace be upon him) with the wording: 'The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade a loan that draws a benefit,' and in another narration: 'every loan that draws a benefit is riba'; in its chain is Sawwar ibn Mus'ab, who is abandoned (matruk). 'Umar ibn Zayd said in al-Mughni: nothing authentic has been established in it."
3 Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Tawus and Mujahid said: this verse was revealed concerning the gift given seeking recompense (hibat al-thawab). Ibn 'Atiyyah said: whatever is similar to it, that a person does in order to be repaid, such as greeting and the like, although there is no sin in it, there is no reward in it and no increase in the sight of Allah, the Exalted. Cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5293).
4 Recorded by Ibn Majah in his Musnad (2431) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, who said the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw written at the gate of Paradise: charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan eighteenfold. I said: O Jibril, why is a loan better than charity? He said: Because the one who asks, asks while he has; whereas the borrower borrows only out of need."
5 A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2051), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1599), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 30, verse 40:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿It is Allah who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life. Is there any of your partners who does anything of that? Glory be to Him, and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾

We have already said that the matter of creation is accepted, because it is a matter that no one has claimed for himself, despite the abundance of those who boast of disbelief and atheism. Therefore, when Nimrod, who argued with Abraham about his Lord, claimed it, saying: "I give life and cause death," Abraham, peace be upon him, knew that he wanted contention and sophistry that serve no purpose. Otherwise, how could ordering the killing of one person be causing death, and ordering the release and pardon of another be giving life?

Then, what about those who were created before you, and whose birth was before yours? So you have not created anyone, nor given life to anyone. We have previously explained the difference between killing (qatl) and dying (mawt), though both share in ending life and taking away the soul. However, death occurs by the departure of the soul first, followed by the breakdown of the structure and the collapse of the body.

As for killing, it breaks the structure first, in a way that results in the departure of the soul, for the soul does not remain except in a sound structure. We illustrate this with the electric bulb: when it burns out, its light goes off. Does that mean the current has been cut off from it? No, rather it is still present, but it needs a sound structure, as evidenced by the fact that when we replace the bulb, it lights up.

The Truth, glory be to Him, shows us this distinction in His saying: ﴿Muhammad is nothing but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels...?﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:144). So Nimrod does not give life; rather, he remains alive, and he does not cause death; rather, he kills and takes away the soul.

Abraham, peace be upon him, could have answered this argument and exposed its falsehood, but he wished to take him to another field in which he could not resort to fabrication or evasion. So he said to him: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.﴾ Then the one who disbelieved was confounded... (Al-Baqarah 2:258).

Likewise the matter of provision is accepted as belonging to Allah, and no one has claimed it: ﴿It is Allah who created you, then provided for you...﴾ (Ar-Rum 30:40).

The evidence is that Allah made some regions barren, where the strong and the weak go hungry, and where the wealthy and the non-wealthy go hungry. If there were a provider other than Allah, let him give life to these barren regions.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life...﴾ (Ar-Rum 30:40), and He did not say "will kill you." ﴿Is there any of your partners who does anything of that?...﴾ (Ar-Rum 30:40), meaning: ask them this question, and let them answer it themselves: can the idols you associate with Allah do anything of creation, provision, giving life, or causing death?

Is there in their power any of that, when you are the ones who make them, carve their stones with your hands, and shape them as you wish? Then when a storm blows and overturns them, or perhaps breaks an arm of one of the idols, you gather to erect and repair them. Where are your minds? And what of this disappointment that has befallen you?

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says about them: ﴿Those they call upon besides Allah create nothing, and they are themselves created.﴾ (An-Nahl 16:20)

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gather together for it...﴾ (Al-Hajj 22:73). And more than that: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them something, they could not retrieve it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ (Al-Hajj 22:73)

By Allah, can anyone retrieve what the fly has taken from him?

We note in the verse the repetition of (min), which is for partitive meaning: ﴿Is there any of your partners who does anything of that?...﴾ (Ar-Rum 30:40). The meaning is: none of your partners can do anything, even something trivial, of creation, provision, giving life, or causing death.

Therefore you must respond to these matters concerning Allah with one statement: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾ (Ar-Rum 30:40). There is no response but this.

Thus, when Abraham, our master, spoke about the idols, he said: ﴿For they are an enemy to me... except the Lord of the worlds, who created me and guides me.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 26:77–78). That is: you and what you worship besides Allah, because they associated their gods with Allah, so Allah, glory be to Him, is included in this partnership; therefore his Lord excepted Him.

You notice here in His saying ﴿who created me...﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 26:78) that He did not emphasize it with anything, and did not mention the pronoun (huwa) before "created," because the matter of creation, as we said, has not been claimed by anyone. As for guidance, which is an area of claim, he said "fa-huwa" (then He), meaning that the Truth, glory be to Him, restricts guidance to Allah: ﴿so He guides me.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 26:78)

In this there is an indication that the law which organizes my life and the method which guides me is the law of my Lord, which I take from no one other than Him. We often see one who claims guidance and says: "I have devised a law that will make people's lives happy, and it does such and such." We have heard this tune once from capitalism, once from socialism, and from communism... etc.

So this is a wide field of claim, and Abraham, peace be upon him, restricted it and confined it to Allah, for there is no method but the method of Allah, and no law governs us but the law of our Lord, as we say colloquially: "There is none but Him" (mafish illa huwa).

Likewise in the matter of feeding he said: ﴿And the One who feeds me...﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 26:79), using the restrictive construction by the relative pronoun (alladhi) and then the singular masculine absent pronoun (huwa), to emphasize that the One who feeds him is indeed Allah. For a person may think that his father is the one who feeds him, or that his mother is the one who feeds him, since she prepares his food; these are the two apparent causes in this matter, so the matter required more than one emphasis.

Then peace be upon him said: ﴿And the One who causes me to die, then gives me life.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 26:81) Thus without emphasis, because death and life are two matters accepted as belonging to Allah and settled. Likewise: ﴿The One from whom I hope He will forgive me my error on the Day of Recompense.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 26:82) This too can be only for Allah, exalted is He.

So: whatever has a semblance of action by others, he emphasizes and restricts to Allah, while the other matters in which no one other than Allah has any part, he states in absolute terms without restriction.

Thus the response to this wondrous matter can only be our saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾ (Ar-Rum 30:40), meaning: exalting Him above having partners. And since the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has informed us that Allah, exalted is He, said: "There is no god but Me," and no one has disputed this matter or claimed it for himself.

So it is accepted, for otherwise, if there were another god, where is he? And why did he not defend his right to divinity? If he does not know, then he is heedless; and if he knows and does not oppose, then he is a coward; and in either case he is not fit to be a god.

Therefore our Lord judged the matter with one statement, saying: ﴿Say: If there were with Him gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Possessor of the Throne.﴾ (Al-Isra 17:42)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 30, verse 41:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may make them taste part of what they have done, so that they might return.﴾ [30:41]

"Zahara" (ظهر): became clear and manifest. Zuhur (الظهور) is that something existing in actuality becomes evident, though we do not see it. Since the Truthful, glorified is He, said "Corruption has appeared..." [30:41], it must be that the corruption was already existing, but the people of corruption concealed it and let it spread until it hatched and multiplied within society.

Corruption does not itself appear; rather, its effect appears. Do you recall the earthquake that occurred, which revealed the corruption, fraud and deception between the contractor and the engineer? The buildings were standing and the corruption was hidden, either because of our heedlessness toward it, or our complicity with it, that is, because of our lack of concern for things, until matters were buried. So God exposed the earth through the earthquake, to reveal what we had of corruption.

So when the rot increases, spreads, and exceeds what can be tolerated, God must make it manifest to people, for no one remains able to stand against corruption or prevent it. Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, intervenes, exposes the people of corruption, and makes them taste the consequences of what their hands have done.

"Zahara" also comes in the sense of "domination," as in His saying, ﴿So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾ [61:14], i.e., victorious. And in Surah al-Tahrim: ﴿And if you support one another against him...﴾ [66:4].

And in the sense of "elevation," as in His saying, ﴿So they were not able to scale it, nor could they make a hole in it﴾ [18:97].

So the meaning of ﴿Corruption has appeared...﴾ [30:41] is: righteousness was overcome and rose above it. God created the universe in the form of righteousness and prepared it marvelously to receive man. To verify the truth of this matter, look at the universe, its kinds, its spheres, and its atmospheres; you will not see corruption except in what the hand of man touches.

As for what the hand of man does not touch, you see no defect in it, because God created it harmonious in its kinds and harmonious in its formation: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outpace the day, and each, in an orbit, is swimming﴾ [36:40].

So have the Truthful, glorified is He, and His creation of our choice, made us corrupt in the universe?

No. Rather, it is the trial of choice, when the methodology is revealed to you and made the law of your movement: do and do not. What I have not stated, "do" or "do not," you are free in. No harm arises in the universe from doing it or not doing it. But I have said "do" regarding that whose non-performance causes harm, and I have said "do not" regarding that whose performance causes harm.

So corruption comes when your hand enters into something while you discard God's law of "do and do not." As for righteousness, it exists and has an immunity by which it combats corruption; if the current of corruption rises and prevails over righteousness and overcomes it, it becomes evident to people.

At that point the Truthful, glorified is He, alerts us through events that touch us and says to us: look at what happened to whoever opposed God's methodology. Therefore, in the aftermath of events, we increase in love for God and in desire to obey Him, and you see people (walking on dough, bewildered), but soon they return to their former neglect and heedlessness, in accordance with the saying of the poet:

The funerals startle us as they approach,
and we amuse ourselves when they depart, turning back.
The fright of a flock before a wolf's den;
when he was gone, they returned, grazing.

So the Truthful says: ﴿Corruption has appeared...﴾ [30:41], i.e., it overcame the law of righteousness upon which God established the order of this universe, which, if the hand of man reached it, would itself become corrupt, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ [23:71].

The phenomena of the universe are matters and issues for all the common people, and it is of wisdom that the hand of man does not reach them, because God, exalted is He, wants the universe to endure, and its time of ending has not come. Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, places within us an immunity that makes us accept corruption for a time, until it reaches the degree of saturation, and then conditions burst.

So His saying, ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land...﴾ [30:41], is a result of his call, may God bless him and grant him peace; for the word "zahara" indicates that something has occurred. It is as if He is saying to us: if you repeat corruption and heedlessness, the appearance of corruption will recur. It gives us a summary of what has actually happened of their enmity toward the Messenger of God, their boycott, his isolation, the instigation of the foolish among them to harass him, then the enmity toward his companions and their being forced to emigrate to Abyssinia, so that no settled place would remain for them in Mecca.

Therefore the Messenger of God invoked against them: "O God, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph" (1). So drought and famine struck them, to the extent that it is related they used to go to the sea to fish, but the fish would stay away from them and nothing would work out for them, so they would return as they came.

This is the meaning of ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea...﴾ [30:41].

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, clarifies the cause of this corruption: ﴿by what the hands of people have earned﴾ [30:41]. Note here that when the Truthful, glorified is He, mentions mercy, He does not mention its cause, but He mentions the cause of corruption, because mercy from God, glorified is He, is a bounty first and last; whereas seizure and punishment are by His justice, exalted is He. Therefore He shows you that you did such-and-such and deserve such-and-such, so the cause is clear.

There is another matter I love to make clear to you: that the Truthful, glorified is He, treats His creation in recompense according to His treatment of them. God says: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like...﴾ [6:160].

So one good deed covers ten misdeeds. Likewise in the human body: some physiologists and anatomists say that the kidney contains a million cells, of which a tenth work in rotation; one group works while the rest rest, and so on. Consider how long a cell rests until its turn comes to work.

So it is as if our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, made for it a tenth that stands in place of the million. Therefore they said: if in one office there are ten employees, one of whom is virtuous and covers the faults of the rest, this phenomenon is often observed in government offices. You find most employees occupied: this one reads the newspapers, that one drinks tea, and another has not come at all.

And behind a pile of files you find a lean employee immersed in work, whom everyone turns to, who bears the negligence of the others and performs on their behalf, and by him the affairs of the matter are steered. But if we lose this as well, then ﴿Corruption has appeared...﴾ [30:41] must come. Therefore: if you see corruption, know that it is the result of negligence and heedlessness that have exceeded all bounds.

Since the Truthful, glorified is He, said: ﴿by what the hands of people have earned﴾ [30:41], it must be that corruption came from their side. By God, have we complained of a shortage in the air, for example? Yet we complain of the pollution of the air by what the hands of people have earned. But when we go out into the open where no human is present, we find the air pure as God created it.

The Truthful, glorified is He, has guaranteed us our sustenance, saying: ﴿And He determined in it its sustenance﴾ [41:10]. Yet we complain of a food crisis. Why? Because food requires labor, and we have been lazy and have mismanaged the universe, either through sloth and inertia in extracting the earth's bounties and sustenance, or through selfishness, where the one who has withholds from the one who lacks.

We have read, for example, that America pours milk into the sea and destroys much produce, while in the world there are people dying of hunger. So this is selfishness, whereas laziness occurred on our part in the past.

Now look at our deserts, which were barren and desolate: how they have become green now, and have become a source of bounties since we cared for them and facilitated their ownership for people. If the land in one region is stingy, God has given us breadth in another. The Creator, glorified is He, did not make the earth for one kind or for one homeland; rather He made it common for all God's creatures.

Read His saying: ﴿Was not the earth of God spacious, so that you could emigrate within it?﴾ [4:97].

Therefore I said at the United Nations: there is one verse in the Qur'an which, if the world acted upon it, would guarantee for it prosperity, stability and security. It is His saying: ﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures﴾ [55:10]. The earth, all of it, is for the creatures, all of the creatures. But reality is otherwise: they have set boundaries for the earth and erected barriers and walls upon it. If you wish to move from one country to another, you undergo much hardship in procedures, visas... etc.

The result is that in the universe there are men crowded together without land, and in another place land without men. If integration occurred between this and that, affairs would be set right.

Therefore: those who placed boundaries and barriers in God's earth took it for themselves, so God's spacious earth no longer receives God's creatures from any other place; rather they made it their own land and subjected it to their own laws. And you will be astonished when you look at the borders of states on the map: they are interlocking. You see a part of one state entering the territory of another state in the shape of a triangle, for example, or the land of one state extending into another in the shape of a tongue or winding areas. Since you have placed boundaries between you, why do you not make them straight?

Those who set these boundaries intended them to be sources of dispute between states, and this division is not free of whim, tribal, racial, national and religious partisanship. But if we took up our Lord's saying: ﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures﴾ [55:10], we would not suffer all this suffering.

His saying, ﴿kasabat [has earned]﴾ [30:41]: with us, kasaba and iktasaba. The general rule is that kasaba is used for good deeds, and iktasaba for evil deeds, because a good deed comes from the believer naturally, without strain or contrivance, so it is indicated by the bare verb (kasaba).

As for evil, it is contrary to nature, so it requires from you strain and contrivance, and so it is indicated by the augmented verb indicating contrivance (iktasaba).

Do you not see that in your house you look at your wife and daughters as you wish, but with a stranger woman you steal glances at her and contrive to do so? All your movements are contrived. Why? Because you are doing something forbidden and prohibited. But goodness you do spontaneously and naturally, without strain.

Just as a good deed does not require effort from you, whereas an evil deed requires that you mobilize all your strength and take precautions, like one who steals, for example, who needs effort and needs to fight his own limbs, because in reality they refuse what he does.

Yet we note His saying: ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and is encompassed by his sin—those are the companions of the Fire﴾ [2:81].

Here He made evil a kasb (earning), not an iktisab. They said: because the evil here has become a habit for him, and has been made easy for him until it becomes a natural matter that he does without caring, like one who does good. This type, God forbid, loves evil and is infatuated with it, until he takes pride in it, does not conceal it, and boasts of doing it.

This we call "fāqid" (one who has lost all sense of shame). Wrong and corruption have become his trade, so he is not affected by it and does not feel shame over it, like one who accepts a bribe and rejoices at receiving it. If you ask him, he says: "And what is wrong with it? I am not stealing from people."

His saying: ﴿that He may make them taste part of what they have done﴾ [30:41]: the tasting here is a punishment, but it is the punishment of correction, as you punish and harm your child out of concern for him. We have said before that one should not separate the event from its doer. If a boy assaults your son and wounds him, you take him to the doctor, and the doctor wounds him more severely; but this is the wound of the aggressor, and that is the wound of the healer.

When God makes a person taste some of what his hands have sent forth, He awakens him from his heedlessness and alerts in him the faith-nature, so that he takes precaution in the matter and does not neglect or fall short. This awakening of faith remains in him according to the measure of his faith-awareness: one remains alert for a month and then returns to what he was; another remains alert for a year; another remains his whole life without heedlessness overtaking him.

God made the people of Mecca taste the consequence of their disbelief, until they became hungry and found nothing to eat but the blood of camels mixed with their hair, which is al-'ilhiz.

His saying: ﴿so that they might return﴾ [30:41]: because the discussion here concerns this world, which is not the abode of recompense. So the Truthful makes them taste some of their deeds so that they turn their attention to Him, glorified is He, and repent and return to the fold of faith, for they are His servants, and He, glorified is He, is more merciful to them than a mother to her child.

When the Truthful, glorified is He, says ﴿Corruption has appeared...﴾ [30:41], i.e., in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is to show us that the messengers came only to rescue humanity from this corruption.

1 Related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (2/470, 502, 521), and likewise al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1006), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he raised his head from the last rak'ah would say: "O God, tighten Your grip upon Mudar. O God, make it years like the years of Joseph."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those before you; most of them were polytheists."﴾ (30:42)

Al-sayr (travel): moving from one spatial place to another. We have already said that the superficial view, on the face of the matter, is that travel takes place "on the earth" and not "in it," since we dwell on the earth, not in it. But the Truth, glory be to Him, makes us see, by His saying: ﴿Say: "Travel through the earth..."﴾ (al-Rum), that the earth is not merely the dry land and water on the surface of the terrestrial sphere. Rather, "the earth" includes its atmospheric envelope, which revolves with it, and which is the elixir of life within it; there is no life for it except through it.

Therefore, these (creatures) are from the earth, and it is the most important of the sustenances for the living upon it. So when He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And He determined therein its sustenances...﴾ (Fussilat 41:10), the air is included in it. That is why He said: ﴿Say: "Travel through the earth..."﴾ (al-Rum).

We have also said: if you were to survey the classes of existence, you would find that you are the highest class in the cosmos, and all the other classes are beneath you, serving you. You benefit from animals, from plants, and from minerals. Even the lowest class in the cosmos, which is inanimate matter, has a function it performs.

So you, O human being, whom God has honored above all classes of existence: if you do not seek for yourself a task to perform in life and a role to play, then you are of lower rank than the lowest class, which is inanimate matter. If you do not search with your intellect for something to which you may attach yourself, one that befits your dominion over those beneath you, then you are more worthless than a stone, because the stone has a function it performs, while you have no function.

Yet this lowest class, if He, glory be to Him, wills, He bestows upon it a honor above its master who is served, namely the human being. In the rite of Hajj, it is prescribed for you to kiss this stone, and to strive earnestly to kiss it. Consider the human being, the lord of this existence, as he tries to kiss the stone, and becomes angry if he is unable to do so.

And consider the reply from the kingdom of stones to those who worshipped them besides God:(1)

They worshipped us, while we are more devoted to God than those who stand in prayer at dawn.
They took our silence as a proof against us, so we became fuel for their fire.
They have transgressed in ignorance, as they transgressed in ignorance against the son of Mary and the disciples.
For the extremist is his recompense, and the one who is extreme regarding him is saved by the mercy of the Forgiving.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Observe how was the end of those before... (42)﴾ (al-Rum). Travel on the earth is either for tourism and reflection on the signs of God in His creation, which is why the fa' (then) is used in ﴿fa-unzuru (observe)﴾ (al-Rum); or one travels on the earth in pursuit of livelihood.

In another verse: ﴿Say: "Travel through the earth, then observe..."﴾ (al-An'am 6:11). The meaning: travel through the earth for investment, seeking sustenance, and attending to affairs; but do not let slip from you contemplation and reflection on the signs of God and His creatures, so that you may draw from them lessons and admonition.

The meaning of ﴿how was the end of those before...﴾ (al-Rum) is: those among whom corruption appeared, so God made them taste the pain for what their hands had earned. This is not unique to you; it occurred among the earlier nations, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ (al-Saffat 37:137).

There are the cities of Salih, al-Ahqaf, 'Ad, Thamud, the Pharaohs... etc. Look at what befell them of civilization and splendor, after they had attained knowledge of embalming, whose secrets science has not yet come to know until now, and they placed with the corpses of the dead grains of wheat or barley, which remained in their state so that when sown after thousands of years, they sprout.

This is a supreme scientific capacity, yet this civilization could not protect itself from perishing. If the Qur'an spoke of the Pharaonic civilization: ﴿And Pharaoh of the stakes﴾ (al-Fajr 89:10), it spoke of Iram: ﴿the like of which was not created in the lands﴾ (al-Fajr 89:8).

What civilization is this? And where is it now? The sands of al-Ahqaf buried it(2), and it was interred beneath layers of earth. Do not be surprised at this: in this region, if a single storm blows, it covers an entire caravan, with its camels and its men, beneath the ground. How much more so with storms over long centuries; that is why every antiquity is excavated by digging.

Thus, civilizations, despite their greatness, could not protect themselves from extinction, and this is evidence of the existence of a higher power that removes them and brings them to an end.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿most of them were polytheists﴾ (al-Rum): meaning that a few of them were not polytheists. It has been said: this minority are the children and the insane, and whoever has no free will. Even if this minority is taken together with the polytheistic majority, God wills good for them, because their abode is Paradise without reckoning.

Therefore, when we spoke of Moses and the righteous servant in Surah al-Kahf: when al-Khidr killed the boy, Moses was amazed. In the first instance, he damaged the ship and transgressed against a king; but in this instance he took a soul. Therefore in the first he said: ﴿You have certainly done a thing terrible (imran)﴾ (al-Kahf 18:71), i.e., wondrous; but in the second he said: ﴿You have certainly done a thing unthinkable (nukran)﴾ (al-Kahf 18:74).

Then al-Khidr explained the wisdom in killing the boy, saying: his two parents were righteous, and in God's knowledge he would corrupt their religion for them; for temptation comes to a person usually from a spouse or from a child, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ (al-Taghabun 64:14). Why? Because they may compel you to what you cannot bear, and may force you, perhaps, into theft or bribery to provide for what they need; and because corruption comes from their direction. He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿He has not taken a companion or a son﴾ (al-Jinn 72:3), meaning: be reassured, My servants, for no one influences My will.

Thus al-Khidr did a kindness to the parents, in that he rescued them from this son; and he also did a kindness to the boy, in that he killed him before the age of obligation and made his destiny Paradise. Perhaps, had he left him, he would have been a disbeliever undutiful to his parents. All of this occurred only by the command and judgment of God: ﴿And I did it not of my own accord﴾ (al-Kahf 18:82).

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is saying to His Prophet regarding this matter, beginning with ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾ (al-Rum 30:41), then the infliction of punishment upon them as recompense for what their hands had done, and My answering your supplication against them.

All of that means that I strengthen your position, and I will never abandon you. Since this is so, beware lest their plotting affect you, or that you incline toward any of them, those who said to you: "Worship our gods for a year, and we will worship your God for a year"(3). But the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So set your face toward the upright religion before there comes from God a Day that cannot be turned back; on that Day they will be divided﴾ (al-Rum 30:43).

(1) From the poetry of the Shaykh, may God be pleased with him.
(2) Al-Azhari said: al-Ahqaf are sand dunes on the outskirts of the land of Yemen where 'Ad used to dwell. (Lisan al-'Arab, entry: h-q-f).
(3) Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 261) regarding the revelation of the Surah (al-Kafirun): that a group of Quraysh said: "O Muhammad, come, follow our religion and we will follow yours; you worship our gods for a year, and we worship your God for a year..."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 43:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion...﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:43]. He means: Be reassured, O Muhammad, and devote yourself to the worship of Allah, for I have promised you victory and have answered you when you said: "O Allah, make Your trampling severe upon Mudar, and make it upon them as the years of Joseph."(1)

﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them or cause you to die, to Us they will return﴾ [Ghafir 40:77]. He means: whoever was not struck by the punishment of this world will be struck by the punishment of the Hereafter.

He said: ﴿So set your face...﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:43], because the face is the seat of honor, the lord of the human being, and the place of his dignity. The proof is that prostration and humble supplication to Allah the Most High are performed by placing this face upon the ground. Therefore, when you send a person with a message or assign him a matter to accomplish, whether with his foot, his hand, his tongue, or any other of his limbs, you say to him: "I hope you will whiten my face," because the face is the chief.

Among this is His saying: ﴿Everything will perish except His face﴾ [Al-Qasas 28:88]. For you do not recognize people except by their faces. Whoever wishes to disguise himself or conceal his identity covers only his eyes, so what of one who covers his whole face? You do not recognize a person from his back, nor from his palm, nor from his foot; you recognize him only by his face. They say: "So-and-so is the notable of the people," or "he has his standing among the people," all of which relate to the face.

Since the face is singled out, and it is the most noble thing in you, all the limbs are intended by way of priority, for they follow the face. The meaning is: set your hand to what Allah has commanded you to do, your foot to what Allah has commanded you to strive toward, your heart to what Allah has commanded you to occupy it with, and your eye to what Allah has commanded you to look upon... etc.

That is: seize the opportunity of your life ﴿before there comes a Day...﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:43], which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿that cannot be turned back from Allah...﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:43]. The meaning: when Allah brings it, no one can recall it from Allah, or take it from His hand, or prevent Him from bringing it; or, when He, glory be to Him, has decreed a matter, it does not return or revert.

The phrase ﴿from Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:43] thus gives us both meanings, as in His saying: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before him and behind him, who protect him by the command of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rad 13:11]. How, then, do the successive angels protect him "by the command of Allah"? They said: their being successive guardians is itself a command issued by Allah in origin, based on His command to protect.

As for His saying: ﴿That Day they will be separated﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:43]: he means, on the Day that cannot be turned back from Allah. ﴿They will be separated﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:43]: that is, those who banded together against you in war, enmity and harm, and who united in opposition to you, will split apart, some from others, and scatter. This matter has been mentioned in many verses.

The separation is either between belief and disbelief, that is, between the wretched and the blessed, or it may be the separation of the people who were stubborn and followed their followers in polytheism, so that each of them disowns the other, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:166].

Then the Truth said, to make that separation clear to us in the Hereafter by its cause, and its cause is what happened in this world, for Allah the Most High does not wrong anyone.

(1) On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say, when he raised his head from the last rak'ah: "O Allah, make Your trampling severe upon Mudar; O Allah, make it upon them as the years of Joseph." Reported by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (2/470), and by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1006).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 44:

Then, after that, He said:

﴿Whoever disbelieves, on him is his disbelief; and whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare [the way].﴾

Since the Resurrection is a matter from Allah that cannot be averted, let us be mindful of the consequences and reckon with them. Whoever disbelieves, on him is his disbelief, against him and not for him. And this is a proposition that calls for us to say, in its counterpart: and whoever believes, for him is his belief.

After He had shown the clear proofs of His oneness in the cosmos and His singularity in His essence, and had set forth the cosmic evidences in every form as proof and argument, and had coined parables and details after that, He said: I shall tell you that you have become chooser-beings, that is, I have created in you the faculty of choice within the scope of moral responsibility (taklif), so that I do not compel anyone to believe in Me.

The creation of choice within moral responsibility, after compulsion in what is not subject to responsibility, indicates that Allah, exalted is He, does not want from His servants mere moulds that obey by compulsion, but He wants to draw people by their love for the One, the Unique.

Otherwise, it would have been possible for Him to create them all guided, and to create them in a form unable to disbelieve, moving toward obedience unwillingly, as He, glorified is He, said recounting [the words] of the heaven and the earth: ﴿We came willingly, obedient﴾ (Fussilat 11). And this explains to us the trust (amanah) of the creation of choice in human beings.

And when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, spoke clearly on this matter, He said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it… ﴾ (al-Ahzab 72). The refusal here is not the refusal of arrogance against the will of Allah; rather, they placed themselves in their natural position, and said: No, to bearing the trust, for we do not trust ourselves and we do not guarantee it at the time of its discharge.

The human being, likewise, is a son of changing circumstances. He may bear the trust and guarantee its discharge at the time of undertaking it, but he does not guarantee himself at the time of discharge. We had previously given an example of this: one who accepts the trust and welcomes it at the time of undertaking it, then there befall him, from the events of life, what compels him to reach out to this trust even though his intention was to discharge it; but the time comes and he is unable. And another who assesses this responsibility and refuses to bear the trust, and this is the wise one who considers circumstances and the changing of conditions.

It is well known that a trust is not documented; if it is written and witnessed upon, it is no longer a trust. The trust, then, is returned to the choice of the one entrusted: if he wills, he acknowledges it, and if he wills, he denies it.

So the Truth, glorified is He, said, recounting [the words] of the heavens, the earth and the mountains: ﴿…they declined to bear it and feared it…﴾ (al-Ahzab 72), because they assess its responsibility. As for the human being, he exposed himself to bearing it and said: I have an intellect with which I think, and I choose between alternatives, and I will discharge it. So he guaranteed at the time of undertaking, but he does not guarantee at the time of discharge, and so he wronged himself and was ignorant of the realities of matters.

﴿And the human being bore it; indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ (al-Ahzab 72): he wronged himself, [and was] ignorant of what changing circumstances could befall him.

And since the human being is a son of changing circumstances, he does not remain fixed in one state. Therefore we have said: if a human being climbs a mountain to its summit while he is a son of changing circumstances, there is nothing before him but to descend. The wise fear that blessing will be completed for them, because after completion there is nothing but decline, as the poet said:

When a thing is complete, its deficiency appears; be wary of its vanishing once it is said to be complete.

Now if you say: why did Allah create choice in the human being and not in the kinds that serve him, of inanimate matter, plants and animals? We say: be precise, and understand that they too were given the choice by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it…﴾ (al-Ahzab 72).

So: these kinds too were given choice, but they chose a single choice which suffices them for all choices, and so they said: O Lord, we want to be subdued to all that You wish.

And since we are choosers, Allah, exalted is He, gave us this principle: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, on him is his disbelief…﴾ (al-Rum 44). The word ʿalayhi (on him) indicates harm and burden, and lahu (for him) indicates benefit. So if we bring the counterpart by saying: and whoever believes, for him is his belief, as in: ﴿Indeed the righteous are in bliss, and indeed the wicked are in the Blazing Fire﴾ (al-Infitar 13–14).

But the Qur'an did not bring this counterpart; rather it turned to another matter: ﴿and whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare [the way]﴾ (al-Rum 44). Why? They said: because the benefit of faith is that you believe in the existence of a capable, singular God, who is Allah, so you believe in Him; then, when He commands you, you obey. So the cause of faith is moral responsibility (taklif). Therefore, when you investigate any obligation that is imposed upon you, beware of looking at its cause and saying: He obligated me with this for that. The cause and wisdom of the obligation are with Him, exalted is He.

So if we say, for example: the wisdom of fasting is that the rich person feels and tastes the pain of hunger and so is moved with compassion for the poor, does this mean that the destitute poor person does not fast? Then this is not the wisdom of fasting. The more correct thing is to say: I fast, because Allah wanted me to fast, and its wisdom is with Him.

And for Allah, exalted is He, is the highest likeness, let us illustrate: when you complain of an illness or pain, you seek a skilled and specialised physician until you arrive at him, and then the task of your mind ends there. You place yourself in his hands; he examines you, diagnoses your illness, and writes you a medicine. You do not oppose him in anything, nor do you ask him why he prescribed this medicine.

If a visitor, for instance, asks you: why are you taking this medicine? You do not say: because of its properties, and its interactions are such-and-such; rather you say: because the physician prescribed it for me. Even though the physician is a human being who may err, and may write you a medicine, or give you an injection you do not want, yet you submit to him in what he sees as suitable for you. So if you do not argue with the physician though he may be wrong, how do you argue with Allah concerning what He has enjoined upon you, and seek a cause for everything?

Only an equal disputes about the causes of things; the physician is disputed only by a physician like him. Likewise, we must submit to Allah, exalted is He, regarding the causes of things and their wisdom, until there exists one equal to Him, glorified is He, who could dispute with Him.

The Truth, glorified is He, explains to us the cause of faith, not faith in itself; rather what follows from it: obedience to the commands of this God. And upon obedience to these commands the goodness of the cosmos is contingent, as evidenced by the fact that Allah requires the believers to spread the call, to convey it, and to fight whoever opposes it and prevents them from spreading it.

The sword was not drawn in Islam except to protect the conveyance of the call. If they leave you to yourself, then leave them, as evidenced by the fact that the lands conquered by Islam retained people of other religions upon their religions, and this is proof that Islam did not compel anyone to adopt it.

But since Islam has conquered the lands, it must be that it holds dominance, and that everyone walks with it under the shade of the method of Allah, so that the disbeliever and the one without religion have what the person of religion has.

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, wants His laws to govern, whether you believe in Him or do not; for the goodness of the cosmos can only be by these laws.

So: you are free, you may believe or not believe; but what is required of the one who believes is to protect the call in its conveyance, and then to leave people free: whoever believes therein, excellent; and whoever refuses, we say to him: for you is what is for us, and upon you is what is upon us.

So: the root of faith is for the goodness of the caliphate (khilafah), and Allah, glorified is He, is not concerned whether you believe or do not believe, as long as the method of the caliphate stands; and this method's benefit returns to both the believer and the disbeliever. If faith trains the human being to do only good and righteousness, the disbeliever must benefit from this righteousness. Did the Law say to the believer: do not steal from a believer? No; rather, also: do not steal from a disbeliever… and so on. All stand equal before the method of Allah.

In the Qur'an there is a verse that we should be mindful of, and make known to non-believers, so that they may know that faith protects the interest of all people. It is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And seek forgiveness of Allah…﴾ (al-Nisa' 105–106). That is: if it occurs to you to be on the side of the treacherous one, seek Allah's forgiveness from this. ﴿Indeed Allah does not love one who is a habitual betrayer, sinful﴾ (al-Nisa' 107), even if he is a believer in Him.

There is a well-known story behind this verse: the story of the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samin. Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq, who was a believer, came to him and said: O Zayd, take this coat of mail as a trust with you. Zayd accepted it, and behold, the coat of mail was stolen; Ibn Ubayriq had stolen it from Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man(1) and placed it in a sack of flour, so the coat of mail had traces of flour upon it. When Ibn al-Nu'man searched for his coat of mail, the trace of flour led him to the house of the Jew Ibn al-Samin, and he accused him of stealing it.

They then brought him to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to judge in his matter. He related to him what had happened with Ibn Ubayriq, and that he had placed it with him as a trust.

At that point it was grievous to the Muslims that one of them should steal, and that the Jews should take it as a humiliation to them. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began to deliberate the matter in his mind: if he judged against the Muslim, the Jews would take it as proof, and if he judged for the Muslim, it would be a shame and a blemish upon the religion. So his Lord aided him with this verse: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾ (al-Nisa' 105). He said: between people, not between believers only.

As for ﴿and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾ (al-Nisa' 105), some say: do not dispute with the treacherous lest he persecute you; but the intended meaning is: do not be an advocate for his interest. ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah…﴾ (al-Nisa' 106): if the matter of Islam and its image among non-Muslims occurs to you, for in the principle of reform Allah does not love every treacherous sinner.

If non-Muslims were alert to this matter, and knew that Allah, exalted is He, made the judgment just for the believers, and declared it to the Messenger of Allah, and established that the truth is the truth, and that all stand equal before it, the believer and the non-believer, they would know that Islam is the true religion, and they would turn to it. Therefore the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever antagonises a dhimmi, I will be his adversary on the Day of Resurrection."(2)

For if you antagonise him and persecute him, or threaten him in his life, his honour, or his property, it becomes a proof for him not to believe, and he may say: if this is the condition of the believers, what is the advantage of Islam that I should adopt it? Rather it is in my interest to keep away from it. But if you deal with him in truth, goodness and kindness, you will incline him toward Islam, and make him reproach himself for not being a Muslim.

Therefore we have said before: when Sayyidna Ibrahim, upon our Prophet and upon him be the most excellent prayers and peace, was visited by a man, he sensed from him that he was not a Muslim. When he asked him, the man said: I am a Magian, so he closed the door in his face, and the man departed. Then Ibrahim, peace be upon him, received revelation from Allah: O Ibrahim, you refused to host him because he is upon a religion other than yours, yet I have sustained him throughout his life in My dominion while he disbelieves in Me.

Ibrahim hastened after the man until he caught up with him and appeased him. The man said: What has happened? You drove me away and rebuked me a little while ago. He said: My Lord rebuked me concerning you. The man said: A Lord who rebukes His prophets about His enemies is truly worthy of being worshipped. There is no god but Allah, and Ibrahim is the Messenger of Allah.

So we understand from this that righteous deed is the object sought by faith. If you believe in a god so that you take the judgment from Him while you are assured that He is the true God, then it does not matter after that whether you believe or do not believe; what matters is the principle of goodness in the cosmos and in the movement of life. Therefore He did not say "and whoever believes, for him is his belief," as if the meaning of faith is deed: ﴿and whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare [the way]﴾ (al-Rum 44), because one does not do righteousness except when one is a believer.

We note here that the verse speaks in the singular form: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, on him is his disbelief, and whoever does righteousness…﴾ (al-Rum 44), then it shifts to the plural form: ﴿…for themselves they prepare [the way]﴾ (al-Rum 44). He did not say: "he prepares for himself." Why?

They said: because the one who does righteousness does not do it for his own self alone, but for himself and for his descendants after him, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join them with their descendants…﴾ (al-Tur 21). So when He speaks of faith He uses the singular, and when He speaks of recompense He uses the plural.

Also, righteous deed comes from the person's own self, and he receives its return from others; and the word man (whoever) here is suitable for the singular, the dual, and the plural of both kinds, and it stands in place of all the relative pronouns. You say: man jaʾa fa-akramhu (whoever came, honour him); man jaʾatka fa-akramha (whoever, feminine, came to you, honour her); man jaʾaka fa-akramhuma (whoever two came to you, honour them two); man jaʾuka fa-akramhum (whoever came to you in the plural, honour them).

(1) Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man ibn Zayd al-Ansari al-Awsi, a Companion who fought at Badr, one of their brave warriors, a famous archer. He attended all the battles with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; he carried the banner of the Banu Zafar on the day of the Conquest. He died in Medina in the year 23 AH at the age of 65, and he was the maternal half-brother of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. (al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 5/189).

(2) Abu Dawud related in his Sunan (3052), from a number of the sons of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from their fathers, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Beware, whoever wrongs a treaty-bound non-Muslim, or diminishes him, or burdens him beyond his capacity, or takes from him anything without his good pleasure, I will be his adversary on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Sakhawi said in al-Maqasid al-Hasanah: its chain is acceptable, and the unknown identity of those sons of Companions who were not named does not harm it, for they are a number which compensates for their unknown status.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 45:

Then the Exalted explains why they prepare for themselves (in this way):

﴿That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds, out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.﴾ (30:45)

Here He mentioned faith first, saying ﴿those who believe﴾, then ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, so that no one thinks that righteous deeds might suffice in place of faith. This is a matter that has preoccupied many philosophers, who say: how is it that the disbelieving man who performs righteous deeds is not rewarded for them?

We say to him: he is rewarded for his righteous deed, but in this world; because he did not act for God, but acted for fame and renown. He has taken from it honour, celebrity, and perpetuation of his memory, and statues were erected for them... etc. As for the reward of the Hereafter, it is for the one who performs the deed purely for the Face of God.

The Qur'an alerts us to this matter, saying: Beware of being deceived by those who perform deeds for the sake of this world.

﴿And We shall turn to whatever deeds they did, and make them scattered dust.﴾ (25:23)

And it has come in the hadith: "I did it so that it would be said, and it has been said." Yes, you built a mosque, but you wrote upon it: "Built by so-and-so, and its opening was honoured by so-and-so..." etc. So what do you expect after that? Your Lord desires deeds performed purely for His Face, the Exalted, as the hadith says: "And a man who gave charity and concealed it, so that his left hand does not know what his right hand has given."

So His saying ﴿That He may reward those who believe...﴾ (30:45) indicates that a righteous deed, if it is truly righteous, benefits its doer in this world, but does not benefit him in the Hereafter unless it proceeds from faith in God. Then He links faith with righteous deeds, such that neither can substitute for the other.

And His saying ﴿out of His bounty﴾ (30:45) means: by way of grace from God, so that no one is deceived by his deed and thinks he has been saved by it. This matter is a point of discussion among the scholars. They say: at one time the Qur'an says ﴿out of His bounty﴾ (30:45), and at another it says ﴿Enter the Garden for what you used to do﴾ (16:32), meaning that it is a right owed to you on account of the deeds you sent forth. So is Paradise a right for the believers, or a bounty from God?

We say: the deed that God requires as an obligation from the believers in Him returns to whom? It returns to the human being, and God gains nothing from it, because He, the Exalted, has the absolute attributes of perfection before He created the creation.

Therefore, in the sacred hadith He says: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most righteous heart of one man among you, that would not increase My dominion by the weight of a gnat's wing. And if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease My dominion by the weight of a gnat's wing. And if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, gathered in one open place and each asked of Me what he desired, and I gave each his request, that would not diminish what I have except as a needle diminishes the sea when one of you dips it in. That is because I am Generous, Glorious, Munificent; My giving is speech, My punishment is speech; My command, when I desire a thing, is only that I say to it, 'Be,' and it is."

And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿What you have will vanish, and what is with God is enduring.﴾ (16:96)

So then: the obligatory deeds are for the good of the human being himself. Even though outwardly they appear to restrict his freedom, for example, if he wants to steal in order to increase his wealth, we take him by the hand, prevent him, and say to him: Be aware that we have prevented you from stealing while you are one person, and we have prevented all people from stealing from you. So you are in fact the beneficiary of God's method. Do not look at what the obligation has taken from you, but look at what this obligation has given you from others.

And since the whole obligation is for your benefit and your good, if God rewards you for it afterwards, that is a bounty from God upon you, just as you say to your son, for example: If you excel, I will give you such and such, although he is the one who benefits from excelling, so the prize afterwards becomes a bounty.

Likewise, the Blessed and Exalted God loves that His servant perfect his work and strive in it; therefore He gives him a reward for it, although we are the ones who benefit from it.

And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿On that day God will pay them their full due, the truth﴾ (24:25), making it a truth incumbent upon Him, the Exalted, as He said: ﴿And it was a truth upon Us to help the believers﴾ (30:47).

If we examine the word "haqq" (truth/right) philosophically, we find that every right you have corresponds to an obligation upon another, so it is not a right for you unless it is an obligation on someone else. Your right here is therefore an obligation upon God, the Exalted. But an obligation requires something that imposes it: who imposed it upon God? No one, for He, the Exalted, imposed it upon Himself.

So: the right which He made for you as a grace from Him, the Exalted, and the rightness of His having made it a right for you, is like one who has no right to an inheritance, and then one of the heirs bestows upon him a bequest that is written for him, so it becomes an obligatory right, which he may claim from the heirs by law, because the testator bestowed it and made it a right for him.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.﴾ (30:45) We notice in the verse that it speaks of the reward of the believers, so what is the connection of mentioning the disbelievers here? They said: because God wishes to draw the attention of His disbelieving servant to faith and its privileges, as if He were saying to him: Come to faith so that you may attain this reward.

An example of that, and to God belongs the highest likeness: a man has three children and promised them a gift, but to whoever succeeds in his studies. Then the last one came, the world came, and two succeeded; each of them took his gift, and the father grieved for the third who failed, and wished that he were like his two brothers.

Likewise the Exalted God does not love the disbelievers, because He loves that all creation be believers so they may attain the reward of faith; for all are His servants, and He, the Exalted, is more merciful to them than a mother to her child. They are His creation and His handiwork. Have you ever seen a craftsman who smashes and breaks his own handiwork? So God, the Exalted, is eager for His servants, even the disbelievers among them.

And it has come in the sacred hadith: "The heaven said: O Lord, permit me to drop a fragment upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks. The earth said: O Lord, permit me to swallow up the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks. The mountains said: O Lord, permit me to fall upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks. The seas said: O Lord, permit me to drown the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks. Then what did the Lord, the Creator, say to all of them? He said: 'Leave Me and whom I have created. Had you created them, you would have shown them mercy. If they repent to Me, I am their beloved; and if they do not repent, I am their physician.'"

Therefore God, the Exalted, rejoices in the repentance of His servant when he returns to Him after turning away. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) gives us an example to clarify this matter, saying: "God rejoices more at the repentance of His believing servant than one of you who had his camel, which had strayed from him in a barren wilderness."

So God does not love the disbelievers because they were not fit to receive this bounty; and that is only because He, the Exalted, loves them and is eager that His goodness and His giving reach them.

1. From Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first of people to be judged on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who was martyred. He will be brought forward, and God will make him recognise His blessings, and he will recognise them. God will say: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I fought for You until I was martyred.' God will say: 'You lie; rather you fought so that it would be said, "He is brave," and it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is thrown into the Fire. And a man who learned knowledge and taught it, and recited the Qur'an, will be brought forward, and God will make him recognise His blessings, and he will recognise them. God will say: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I learned knowledge and taught it, and I recited the Qur'an for Your sake.' God will say: 'You lie; rather you learned knowledge so that it would be said, "He is a scholar," and you recited the Qur'an so that it would be said, "He is a reciter." It has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is thrown into the Fire..." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1905) and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/23), Dar al-Kutub al-Ilmiyya edition, Beirut.
2. Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1031) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), within the hadith: "Seven whom God will shade in His shade on a day when there is no shade but His shade..." the hadith.
3. Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/77, 154) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2495) from the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him). al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan hadith; in its chain is Shahr ibn Hawshab, whom some considered weak, but al-Bukhari graded his narration as good and strengthened his standing.
4. Cited by Abu Hamid al-Ghazali in Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din (4/52) as a saying of some of the early generations, its wording: "No servant disobeys except that the place of the earth asks permission to swallow him up, and his roof from the sky asks permission to drop a fragment upon him. God, the Exalted, says to the earth and the sky: 'Hold back from My servant, and give him respite, for you did not create him; had you created him you would have shown him mercy. Perhaps he will repent to Me and I will forgive him; perhaps he will replace it with righteousness, and I will replace it for him with good deeds.'"
5. A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh), narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6309) and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (2747), from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him); the wording is al-Bukhari's. "Waqa'a 'ala ba'irihi" means: he came upon it and found it by chance, without intent, after it had strayed from him, so he secured it. The "fala" (wilderness) is the destructive desert.

Then the Exalted says:

﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news, and that He may let you taste of His mercy, and that the ships may run by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾

These are five of Allah's blessings upon His servants.

The sending of the winds is itself a blessing; their bringing of good news of rain is a blessing; the running of the ships is a blessing; seeking from Allah's bounty is a blessing; and then gratitude for all of this is another blessing.

"Ayat" (signs) is the plural of "ayah," which, as we have said, is the wondrous thing that should draw attention and that a person must not neglect even for the blink of an eye. From this is our saying:

"So-and-so is an ayah in eloquence," or "an ayah in beauty," etc.

The word "ayat" is used with three meanings: cosmic signs that direct attention to the Creator, glorified is He, and establish the power of the Creator:

﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon...﴾ (Fussilat 37)

Signs in the sense of the miracles that accompany the messengers, to establish their truthfulness in conveying from Allah; and then the signs that carry the Law and the rulings, which are the verses of the Noble Qur'an that bring us the method of Allah.

Here the Exalted speaks of the cosmic signs: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news...﴾ (al-Rum 46). The word "al-riyah" is the plural of "rih," and "al-riyah" here in the general sense means air, which comes in varieties: still air, as in ﴿If He wills, He calms the wind...﴾ (al-Shura 33).

Still air oppresses a person, as it makes the process of breathing difficult for him, so he brings air to himself either with his hand or with a fan. Why? To renew the oxygen in the air surrounding him so that he can breathe. The air sometimes comes hot, scorching the faces, sometimes as a moist, refreshing, gentle breeze, and sometimes as a violent, destructive storm, etc.

And the Exalted, as we have previously explained, arranged the necessities of the life of the vicegerent on earth in this order: air, then water, then food, according to the importance of these necessities. Air is the most essential necessity in the life of a living being, for a person cannot endure without it for more than a moment, the length of an inhalation and exhalation; if it were withheld from him, he would die. Then water, which a person can endure for up to ten days. Then food, which a person can endure for up to a month.

Therefore, it is from the wisdom of the Creator, glorified is He, that no one owns the air. If someone owned it and became angry with you, you would die before he became pleased with you. As for water, it is rare for people to own it; as for food, it is often owned, because a person can endure without it for a long period, which allows him to earn it and devise ways to obtain it, or perhaps the owner of the food will be moved in heart and give it to you.

Therefore, we hear phrases of threat such as: "By God, I will choke his breath," as if this process were the harshest thing that can be done, because you may withhold water or food from someone and he will not die, but if you withhold air from him, that is his end. It is the swiftest and easiest means of destroying a person, and the least traceable: it leaves no blood and no wounds, just a damp handkerchief. So: air is an essential necessity for both life and death.

We have said: if the air is confined or still, and the oxygen in it is not renewed, a person becomes distressed because his breaths are suffocated. But if a foul smell occurs in a place, you will see everyone crying out: "Open the windows!" Why? So that the air may be renewed.

So: the sending of the winds in itself is a blessing. If there is coolness in them and you feel their freshness, they are announcing rain to you. Therefore the Arab used to know the rain before it fell and estimate the distance of the cloud that would rain upon him. So: the announcement of rain is another blessing.

These two blessings, the sending of the winds and the sending down of rain, are not within human power: ﴿and that He may let you taste of His mercy...﴾ (al-Rum 46), that is, through the rain. As for the verse about ships, ﴿and that the ships may run by His command...﴾ (al-Rum 46), the running is attributed to the ships because humans have a hand and effort in them: he is their maker and the one who steers them by the command of Allah. ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ (al-Rum 46), that is, you travel on the sea for hunting and seeking sustenance, or even for leisure and tourism.

So: the sign in which a person has no part is attributed to Allah alone, and where a person has a part in the action, He attributes it to him, as in His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Have you considered what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators? We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone, to replace your likeness and produce you in what you do not know.﴾ (al-Waqi'ah 58–61)

He gave us the blessing of life, then mentioned what nullifies it, so that we do not receive life with arrogance. And since the sign of life and the sign of death are not within human power, He sufficed with this interrogation: ﴿Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ (al-Waqi'ah 59). No one can say, "I created it."

As for the verse about tilling, the tilling is attributed to the human being, because his work is great in this verse, as he plows, sows, and waters... etc. Therefore, in nullifying this blessing, He said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it into debris...﴾ (al-Waqi'ah 65), and He emphasized the verb with the lam so that you are not deceived by your work in planting.

As for water, this emphasis was not mentioned, because water is a blessing in which humans have no hand; therefore, in nullifying it He said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it salty...﴾ (al-Waqi'ah 70), without emphasis.

The fifth blessing: ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ (al-Rum 46). This blessing is the treasure of all blessings and their binding cord: if you give thanks to Allah for His blessing upon you, He will increase you from it: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you...﴾ (Ibrahim 7).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 47:

After this, God, glory be to Him, consoles His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿And We certainly sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime. And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers.﴾

Meaning: O Muhammad, if you have grown weary in calling to the faith, and have encountered from the chieftains of Quraysh harshness, obstinacy, harm, deceit and plotting against you, nevertheless We have given you victory. Take as an example, in your brothers among the earlier messengers, that they were exposed to the same as what you have been exposed to. Did We ever hand over Our messenger to his enemies? So be at peace; none of these people will inflict anything upon you.

As for the meaning of ﴿they came to them with clear proofs﴾: that is, the manifest signs which establish their truthfulness in conveying from God. Yet they did not believe and denied them. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾: here there is brevity (ījāz) regarding a matter understood from the context. The Qur'an did not state that they denied, but rather mentioned the outcome of denial: ﴿Then We took vengeance﴾.

This brevity is evident in the story of Solomon's hoopoe, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them and see what they return.﴾ (27:28) Then immediately after it: ﴿She said, "O chiefs, indeed a noble letter has been delivered to me."﴾ (27:29) The events that lie between the two statements, which are understood from the context, have been omitted, and this is one of the manifestations of the eloquence of the Noble Qur'an.

The denial of earlier nations of the signs that came to them through the messengers is evidence that they were people of corruption who wished to benefit from that corruption. It is natural that they oppose the messengers who came to eliminate this corruption and that they persecute them. So God, exalted is He, becomes jealous for His messengers: ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime.﴾

Then He establishes this matter: ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers.﴾ God, exalted is He, would not send a messenger and then hand him over to his enemies or abandon him. Therefore He said, glory be to Him, in another place: ﴿And My word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that indeed they would be the ones given victory, and indeed Our soldiers will be the predominant.﴾ (37:171–173)

We have said before: one should not investigate this soldiership by asking, "Is this soldier sincere in defending Islam or not?" Rather, look at the results. If victory is his, know that the power of faith in him was sincere; if the other outcome occurs, then it is incumbent upon him to examine himself and seek the meaning of the defeat that was against Islam within himself, for if he were truly among God's soldiers, there would have been realized in him: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers will be the predominant.﴾ (37:173) The soldiers of God are not defeated except when the attributes of soldiership are dissolved from them.

Consider, for example, what happened at the Battle of Uhud, where the Muslims were routed. (The word "defeat" here is not used in its strict sense, because the battle was a back-and-forth affair, and they had won at its beginning; but the end was not in their favour, because the archers disobeyed the command of the Messenger of God.)(1) Defeat after this disobedience is a natural matter.

Would you, O Muslim, be pleased that the Muslims win after disobeying the command of their Messenger? By God, if they had won while disobeying the command of their Messenger, every command of the Messenger of God would have become trivial thereafter, and they would have said: "We disobeyed his command and yet we won." Thus, the meaning of that is that the Muslims were not defeated; rather, the defeatism within them was defeated, and Islam triumphed through the truthfulness of its principles.

Likewise on the day of Hunayn, about which God says: ﴿And [recall] the day of Hunayn, when your large numbers pleased you...﴾ (9:25). Even al-Ṣiddīq himself said: "We will not be overcome today for lack of numbers." So the matter began with defeat, but the matter was as you say (they had troubled our Lord), so He sent down His tranquillity upon them, and God willed to pardon them for this lapse out of consideration for Abū Bakr's feelings.

As for His saying, ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us(2) to aid the believers⁠﴾: yes, the aid of the believers is a right upon God, which He made obligatory upon Himself. It is thus a bounty from Him, glory be to Him, just as a testator bestows his property upon the legatee.

(1) Al-Bayhaqī in Dalā'il al-Nubuwwa (3/209) narrated from Mūsā ibn ʿUqba in a lengthy ḥadīth: "That the Messenger of God (ﷺ) appointed fifty men from the archers and placed them near the enemy's cavalry, and appointed over them ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr, and said to them: 'O archers, when we take our positions in the fighting, and if you see the enemy's cavalry move and the enemies of God are routed, do not leave your positions. I advance to you that not one man among you should leave his place, and repel the cavalry for me.' He admonished them and conveyed it. And from their direction came what befell the Prophet (ﷺ) that day and what afflicted him...
