When the fifty archers saw that God, mighty and majestic, had granted victory to their brothers, they said: 'By God, we will not sit here for anything; God has destroyed the enemy and our brothers are in the camp of the polytheists.' And groups among them said: 'Why do we stay, when God has routed the enemy?' So they abandoned their positions which the Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined upon them not to leave, and they faltered and disobeyed the Messenger." The ḥadīth...

(2) Al-Qurṭubī said in his tafsīr (7/5300): "Abū Bakr used to pause at 'ḥaqqan' (truly), meaning: and Our punishment was true; then he said: 'ʿalaynā naṣr al-mu'minīn' (it is incumbent upon Us to aid the believers) as a new beginning and predicate, meaning: We inform you of it, and there is no breach in Our report."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 48:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, so they stir up clouds, then He spreads them across the sky however He wills, and makes them into fragments, and you see the rain coming out from within them. Then when He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice.﴾ [30:48]

Here the Truth, glorified is He, gives us a detailed reminder of the process of the movement of the winds, the driving of the clouds, and the sending down of rain. When the word "winds" (riyah) appears in the plural, it indicates good, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilising...﴾ [15:22]

That is, they fertilise the plants: they take from the male and place in the female, and thus fruiting occurs. Among the marvels of this process is that you see the male and female in one stalk, as in the case of the maize plant for example. In the tassel (al-shushah) at the top of the stalk are the grains of male pollen, and in the silks that emerge from the cob, connected to the grains, are the female reproductive organs. With the movement of the winds, the grains of pollen scatter from the top and descend onto these silks. The silk that has been fertilised grows the grain attached to it, while the other, which does not receive the pollen, dies.

For this reason we notice that the stalks that stand in the path of the wind, or on the northern side, yield less than those beside them. Why? Because the winds carry their pollen grains to the other stalks next to them, so their yield increases.

If some plants are such that we know the male from the female, like the palm and the sycamore fig for example, where then are the male and female in wheat, or in the guava, or in the banana?

When they studied these pollen grains, they found that every grain, however small, has fine hairs like velvet, which scatter with the winds, and the air carries them to distant places. Therefore you see the mountains and the desert turn green after the rain falls. Who sowed these seeds there? It is the fertilising winds, by the power of the Creator, mighty and majestic.

We pause at His words, exalted is He: ﴿If He wills, He calms the wind, so they remain motionless on its surface...﴾ [42:33]. That is, the ships that move by the force of the winds remain still on the surface of the water, nothing moving them. If you say: how do we understand this meaning now, with the advance of knowledge that propels ships by steam, diesel or electricity, and has dispensed with the winds?

We say: "riyah" among its meanings means air, and it also means strength in general, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength (rihkum) depart...﴾ [8:46]. That is, your strength. So "riyah" means strength in any state, whether ships move by the winds or by machinery. He, glorified is He, is able to still it.

Therefore you find that "riyah" in the sense of strength has an immediate strength and a future strength: "immediate" meaning now, and "future" meaning what comes later. Likewise every person and every thing in the universe has a scent (nafs), a "riyah," and a specific chemical signature that distinguishes it from others. This is the task of police dogs that smell the scent of accused persons and criminals in drug cases, for example. A person has a scent now while present, and a scent that remains in the place even after he has left it.

Therefore the Qur'an teaches us that the scent (rih) is the most enduring of traces in a human being. Read in this regard His words, exalted is He, about Joseph and Jacob, peace be upon them: ﴿Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face; he will regain his sight...﴾ [12:93]

Joseph was in Egypt, and Jacob in the land of Palestine. When the caravan departed with Joseph's shirt, and left the enclosure of the buildings that may have blocked the winds, Jacob said: ﴿Indeed, I find the scent of Joseph...﴾ [12:94], despite the distance between them.

When "riyah" appears in the singular, it indicates evil. The meaning of "riyah" is that a wind comes from here, a wind comes from there... and it brings you oxygen wherever you are, and carries to you the fragrance of perfumes in the universe. So it brings you benefit.

We have said that stationary things gained their stability from the presence of air on all their sides and directions. If you emptied the air from one side of a building, it would collapse immediately. Likewise the wind, if it comes singular, is destructive and brings ruin, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind [51:41]﴾

And He said: ﴿by a furious, violent wind [69:6]﴾

So His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds...﴾ [30:48]: the sending of the winds in itself is a blessing. ﴿...so they stir up clouds...﴾ [30:48]: stirring the clouds means agitating and moving them, and this is another blessing.

The cloud is the water evaporated from the earth, gathered together in layers of the atmosphere. The rainwater is water distilled by the power of Allah, just as we carry out the process of distillation in laboratories, for example. The rain thus brings us pure, sweet, clear water which the care of the Creator, glorified is He, has distilled for us without our knowing.

If distilling one cup requires all these processes and all this cost, what then of rainwater?

We have said earlier that among the wisdom of the Creator, glorified is He, is that He made three-quarters of the land water, so that the area of evaporation would be vast enough to suffice for the remaining quarter. To illustrate this we gave the example of a cup of water when you leave it on a table, for example, and when you pour it onto the floor of a room. In the first case the water remains a long time, because evaporation is slight; but in the second it evaporates quickly.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿...then He spreads them across the sky however He wills...﴾ [30:48]. Consider the freedom of His will: Allah directs the rain as He wills to the places that need rain. And it is remarkable that when Allah wills to provide for a person, He may provide him from a cloud that does not even pass over his town. Consider, for example, the Nile: from where does its water come, and where did the rain fall that waters the land of the Nile from its beginning to its end?

The meaning of ﴿...and makes them into fragments...﴾ [30:48]: "kisafan" is the plural of "kisfah," which is a piece. ﴿...you see the rain...﴾ [30:48]: the rain. ﴿...coming out from within them...﴾ [30:48]: that is, from among these clouds.

﴿Then when He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice﴾ [30:48]. Reaching may be direct, so the rain falls upon them directly; or it may be indirect, as when the land slopes, so the rain falls in one place and waters another, and even brings to it fertility and growth, just as the Nile in the past carried silt from Abyssinia to Sudan and Egypt.

This silt continued with the water along the whole course of the Nile as far as Damietta. Why did it not settle along all these distances? It was not settled because of the force of the water's thrust and the steepness of its descent, such that this silt does not come to rest and does not deposit.

As for His words: ﴿...behold, they rejoice﴾ [30:48]: because when the winds pass over them they bring them good news of rain, and when the rain falls it brings them good news of crops, growth, fertility and goodness, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs, swells and puts forth every lovely kind of growth [22:5]﴾

I remember, when I was young, our town was on the Nile, and the Nile stretched wide in front of it, with several islands in it that people cultivated. I remember that we used to plant maize, and the flood came and drowned it while it was still green and not yet ripe. The people would go out to it and gather it by boats, and I saw the women trilling with joy, and happiness on their faces. I used to ask my father, may Allah have mercy on him: "The Nile has drowned the crop, so why are the women trilling?"

My father would laugh and say: "The women trill because the Nile has drowned the crop, and this is the source of goodness and the cause of the land's fertility." When I grew up and read the poem of Ahmad Shawqi, may Allah have mercy on him, about the Nile:

From what age does it pour forth through the villages, and by what hand does it lavish in the cities?
You send the water and it becomes gold, and the land drowns it and the drowned one lives.

When I read this poem I understood why the women trilled when the Nile drowned the crop.

The rejoicing at the coming of rain follows the circumstances: if it comes after despair, drought and dryness, the joy is greater, and the rejoicing is most intense when the rain comes suddenly, ﴿...behold, they rejoice﴾ [30:48]. But if the rain comes in ordinary circumstances, the rejoicing at it is less.

1 "Fassala 'an al-makan": passed beyond it. So the caravan departed and passed beyond the city. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/83)

2 The scholars differ in estimating this distance. From Ibn 'Abbas there are several opinions: a journey of eight days; ten days; a journey of eighty farsakh; a journey of six. From al-Hasan al-Basri, that it is a month's journey. From Muhammad ibn Ka'b, that it is a journey of seven days. (al-Suyuti mentioned these opinions in "al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi-al-Ma'thur" (4/581)). According to Ibn 'Abbas's view that it is a journey of eighty farsakh, this means the distance is more than 400 kilometres, on the basis that a farsakh is at least three miles, and a mile is 1760 metres. And Allah knows best.

3 He is Ahmad Shawqi ibn 'Ali ibn Ahmad Shawqi, the most famous poet of the recent age, known by the title "Prince of Poets." Born 1868 CE in Cairo, died 1932 CE aged 64. He grew up in the shadow of the ruling household, studied law, and was acquainted with French literature. His whole life was devoted to poetry, drawing its inspiration from observations and events. His wealth grew and he lived in luxury and wide comfort. (al-A'lam by al-Zirikli 1/137)

4 "Al-'asjad": gold. It is also said to be a collective term for all jewels, including pearls and rubies. (Lisan al-'Arab, root: 'sjd)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 30, verse 49:

Then He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And indeed they were, before it was sent down upon them, utterly despairing.﴾

The meaning of ﴿mublisin﴾ (utterly despairing) is: despairing of the descent of rain. If the rain came to them after this despair, their joy at it would be doubled and multiplied.

The scholars (1) have paused over this verse, because the phrase ﴿min qabl﴾ (before) is repeated. On reflection, the meaning is: "before it was sent down upon them, and indeed they were, before this 'before', despairing." Here, then, there are two "befores."

We must understand that there is a sending of the winds that herald rain, and there is the sending down of the rain. When the rain is sent down, there is a prior stage to it, which is the sending of the winds. So before the sending of the winds they were in despair, and after the sending they said, "Perhaps it will not rain."

So here, how many "befores" are there? There is "before the sending down" and "before the sending." The meaning is: they were, before it (i.e., before the rain was sent down), and before this, despairing.

(1) Here there are opinions mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5301).
According to al-Akhfash, this is a repetition whose meaning is emphasis, and most grammarians hold this view, as reported by al-Nahhas.
Qutrub said: the first "qabl" refers to the sending down and the second to the rain, i.e., "and indeed they were, before the sending down, before the rain."
It was also said: the meaning is "before the clouds, before seeing them." Al-Nahhas chose this opinion.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 50:

God, glorified and exalted be He, wished to draw inference from the perceptible things visible in the cosmos to what He wishes to inform us of from the unseen, concerning matters of resurrection (ba'th) and the Hereafter. Therefore He gives the reason in His saying: ﴿Indeed, He who gives life to the dead is the One who is able to do all things.﴾ (Surah al-Rum). So with the earth He mentioned the verb in the present tense, yuhyi (He gives life), and the present tense indicates renewal and continuity, and this is a process perceptible to us.

As for the giving of life to the dead, He used the noun muhyi (the Giver of life), and the noun indicates the establishment of the attribute, in order to affirm the giving of life to the dead. It is well known that no one doubts death, because it is witnessed by us; but resurrection is a matter of doubt for some, because it is unseen.

Nevertheless, the Exalted says about death: ﴿Then indeed, after that, you will surely die﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun 15), so He affirms this matter once with inna (indeed) and once with the lam (emphatic particle). Death is an event that befalls us, which we do not deny, so why all this emphasis?

They said: Yes, it is an event we do not doubt, but it is an event that is neglected. So heedlessness of it is like denial, and if you were certain of it, you would not have been heedless of it.

Then why, when He mentioned resurrection, did He say: ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection you will be brought forth﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun 16), affirming it with a single emphasis, although it is a matter of doubt? It is as if, since the proofs for it have been established, it should not be doubted; therefore He did not emphasize it as He emphasized death. And since we are heedless of the proofs, it was necessary to emphasize death, and He did not emphasize resurrection.

As for the meaning of ﴿So look...﴾ (Surah al-Rum 50): the command to look here is not (fanzuriya) nor (lil-furja) or for entertainment, because we say: this matter has naẓar (a point for examination), meaning a place for investigation and scrutiny so that we may reach the face of truth in it, by preferring some proofs over others.

Therefore: ﴿So look﴾ means a look of reflection (i'tibar) and contemplation, because we want to measure the absent from us, which we wish to inform of matters of the Hereafter, by what is visible to us of the giving of life to the earth after its death.

So in the verse there is a new proof of the power and oneness of the Truth, and it is a cosmic proof that we all see. God, glorified be He, varies the proofs to draw the created being's attention to the greatness of the Creator, so that he may believe in Him as the one God, the Dominant, the Self-Subsisting, the Powerful. These proofs are an argument that illuminates the intellect, signs in the cosmos that demonstrate truthfulness, parables that He strikes for people in the cosmos and in themselves, a promise for whoever believes, and a warning for whoever opposes.

Here too is a cosmic proof witnessed in the cosmos: the One who gave life to the dead earth, as you see, is the One who will give life to the dead (in the Hereafter), as He informs you. And He came with the form of the active participle, which indicates the establishment of the attribute of giving life before He gives life, just as we say: So-and-so is a poet, and he did not acquire this attribute because he composed poetry; rather he is a poet before he speaks. Likewise the Creator, glorified be He, is "Giver of life" before the act occurs from Him, and "Able" before He creates something capable for Him, and "Creator" before He creates a creation; so by the attribute in Him, glorified be He, creation occurs.

To bring closer the resemblance between the giving of life to the earth through plants and the giving of life to the dead on the Day of Resurrection, we say: If we look at the human being, we find this vast frame, weighing about a hundred kilos or more, whose origin is a microbe not seen by the naked eye. It has been said that the offspring of the whole world from the sperm cell could be placed in the size of a sewing-machine bobbin, if half of it were filled with semen. Then this sperm cell takes nourishment, sustenance, and grows and enlarges in size only, while the personality remains as it is.

When a person dies, this body decays and dissolves into the coccyx bone ('ajb al-dhanab), which remains; it does not dissolve and the earth does not consume it, so that it becomes the seed from which the human being is made to grow by God's power on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore there came in the hadith about the giving of life to the dead on the Day of Resurrection: "Then they will sprout as the herb sprouts" (1).

In this tiny bone are all the attributes and characteristics of the human being, and from it he returns as he was before death. As we see the sesame seed, for example: despite its smallness, it carries all the characteristics of this plant entirely. So: smallness of size is a proof of power. When this small seed is placed in a suitable environment, it takes nourishment from the soil and from the air, grows and enlarges, and this growth and enlargement does not give a new personality; the personality remains fixed, and it merely gives enlargement to it.

Therefore, when they dissected the rabbit, they found it an exact copy of human anatomy, meaning that it has all the members and all the systems of the human being. Even the mosquito, in its small size, has all the organs, but where are its digestive system, its circulatory system, its nervous system, its sympathetic and urinary systems... etc.? So the precision of these creatures is a proof of power.

In our present civilization we find that among the signs of practical progress is that we reduce the big to the smallest possible degree. Look, for example, at the radio: when first invented it was the size of a threshing floor (?), but now it is the size of a matchbox.

So: greatness is that you place all the apparatus in this small size, or make it large beyond custom and beyond capacity, as in the clock of "Bij Bin", for example.

Therefore we see that the Creator, glorified be He, created the minute thing, extremely small, so that it cannot be perceived by the naked eye, yet it contains all the characteristics of the large thing; and He created from creatures the huge which you cannot encompass.

So: when a thing grows, it does not gain new characteristics; rather the same characteristics and the same original features within it become larger.

We have said before: if a person weighing, for example, a hundred kilos is afflicted with an illness, God forbid, that causes him to lose half his weight, we say: where did this loss go? It went into excretions that came out of him; because a person grows when what enters him of food is more than what leaves him of waste, and if they are equal, he stops at a certain limit, neither increasing nor decreasing.

If God subjects a doctor to treat this patient, he regains his health until he returns to his natural weight of a hundred kilos as it was. Did what he lost in weight return to him, or did there return to him its like from the elements of nourishment and formation? What returned to him was like what he had lost. So: the personality is the same, remaining unchanged with loss or gain.

Likewise, the personality or characteristics exist in this minute microbe or in this small seed, until it is placed in its suitable environment, and then it gives the same personality or the same characteristics of its kind. They even said that the ancient Egyptians placed some grains with the dead and preserved them for thousands of years, so that when a grain of them is placed in suitable soil, it sprouts.

So if a human being can make a grain grow after several thousand years, would it be difficult for God to make the seed of the human being grow, and to give life to the remaining trace of him in the earth when the rain descends by His command, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection?

Moreover, the single grain that a person grows yields him thousands of its kind, but the seed of the human being and the remaining trace of him yield one single person and no more. Would this be difficult for divine power?

Therefore the Exalted urges us to reflect on His saying ﴿So look...﴾ (Surah al-Rum 50): not a look of the eye, but a look of reflection, understanding and deduction. Our Lord censures us for heedlessness in reflection, so He says, glorified be He: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it?﴾ (Surah Yusuf 105).

And we call debate for the manifestation of truths (munazara); each of us debates the other, not a look of the eye, but a look of intellect and deduction.

﴿So look at the effects of the mercy of God, how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the Giver of life to the dead...﴾ (Surah al-Rum 50): that is, the One who gave it life is the Giver of life to the dead. And since the attribute of giving life has been established for Him, if He informs you that He gives life to the dead, then believe it and take from what you have witnessed a proof of what is hidden from you.

Then the Exalted concludes this verse with another attribute that affirms the attribute of creating and giving life: ﴿and He is over all things Powerful﴾ (Surah al-Rum 50). Besides His being the Living and the Giver of life, He, glorified be He, possesses the attributes of perfection, and power over all things: knowledge, power, wisdom, extending and withholding, benefit and harm, etc.

So, after He mentioned the event in the present-tense verb indicating continuity, ﴿yuhyi... (He gives life)﴾ (Surah al-Rum 50), He mentioned the noun indicating the establishment of the attribute ﴿muhyi... (the Giver of life)﴾ (Surah al-Rum 50), then He came with all attributes of perfection in ﴿and He is over all things Powerful﴾ (Surah al-Rum 50).

God wishes to show that man is ungrateful (kanud) (2), that he was created anxious: if evil touches him he is distressed, and if good touches him he withholds. So when he was despairing of the wind that blows upon him, God sent the winds to him; and after he had despaired of a drop of water, God sent down upon him abundant rain. Has this bounty entered his mind, so that when despair strikes him about something, he seeks relief from God, removes despair from himself, and says: I have a Lord to whom I turn, and I should not despair while He exists?

He who relieved you of the despair of the winds and the despair of the rain is able to relieve you of every distress. Therefore the motto of every believer should be: no distress while you have a Lord. As long as you have a Lord, do not worry and do not despair, for with God there is no problem; the problem is that you have no Lord to turn to.

This is the difference between the believer and the disbeliever. The believer has a Lord to turn to if the means become difficult for him; but the disbeliever, how wretched he is: if the means straiten him, he finds no compassionate breast to embrace him, and so in many cases he resorts to suicide.

Therefore, when a matter distressed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would stand up to prayer, and he used to say: "Give us rest by it, O Bilal" (3). In prayer you are alone with your Lord and Creator, you present your need to Him, and you seek from Him help and strength.

Likewise, the prophet of God Musa, peace be upon him, teaches us this lesson. When he set out with the Children of Israel and Pharaoh and his people overtook him, and they found themselves besieged, the sea before them and the enemy behind them, they said to Musa: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara 61). This is the logic of humans and the reality of things; but Musa had another logic, proceeding from the existence of a capable Lord to whom he turns in time of hardship, so that He relieves it from him.

Musa said with full mouth: "No!" (kalla). He said it as a matter of certainty, the word of one confident that his Lord would not abandon him. He did not say it from a store of his own, but from the store of his faith in God: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara 62). And this is the refuge of every believer.

Why not? If you have a case, you feel at ease if you appoint a lawyer to defend you; how much more so if you appoint the Lord of the earth and the heavens, so that He is the advocate, the judge, the witness, and the executor of the judgment?

And you see that in this world a judge rules on evidence which may be falsified, and rules on a confession he cannot extract from its owner, or on the testimony of witnesses, who may be false witnesses; and then he does not possess the power to execute his judgment. There is a judicial authority that judges and an executive authority that executes, and even the executive authority a criminal may escape from.

But in the court of divine justice, its judge is the Truth, glorified and exalted be He; He needs no evidence, confession, or witnesses, and no one can deceive Him, or escape His judgment. Therefore He said of Himself: ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾ (Surah al-A'raf 87).

(1) Al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4935), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2955), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "What is between the two blasts is forty." He said: "Forty days?" He said: "Forty years." He said: "I refuse." He said: "Forty years?" He said: "I refuse." He said: "Then God will send down water from the sky, and they will sprout as the herb sprouts. Nothing of the human being will remain that does not decay, except one bone, which is the coccyx, and from it the creation will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection."
(2) Kanad (kanud) from kanada al-ni'mah yakndaha: he denied it and did not thank for it, so he is kanud; the intensive form kanud means: very ingrate, deeply denying (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/175).
(3) From Hudhayfa, who said: "When a matter distressed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would pray." Recorded by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (5/388) and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (1319).

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And if﴾ you notice the difference between the style of this verse, ﴿And if We send a wind... 51﴾ (al-Rum), and the preceding verse, ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds... 48﴾ (al-Rum). Here "yursil" (He sends) is a present-tense verb indicating continuity, and winds, as we have said, are only used for good, so sending the winds is something abundant, which often happens as a bounty and generosity from Allah.

As for here, in the discussion of the wind, and we have previously said that it is used only for evil, He did not say "yursil." Rather, He chose "in" (if), which indicates doubt, and the past tense verb, which indicates completion. Why? Because the wind of evil rarely occurs, and Allah rarely sends it upon His servants. For example, the "samum" wind comes once a year; likewise the "barren" wind (al-rih al-'aqim) came once in the past, and likewise the "screaming, violent" wind (al-rih al-sarsar al-'atiyah).

So it is rare and infrequent. Nevertheless, if it strikes them, they despair and lose hope, and this should not be from them. Do they not have a precedent of not despairing? They despaired of the sending of winds, and Allah sent them, and of the sending down of rain, and Allah sent it down to them. So why despair when the Lord exists?

The meaning of ﴿they saw it... 51﴾ (al-Rum) is: they saw the crop that had been green and fresh, ﴿turned yellow... 51﴾ (al-Rum), meaning changed and withered. ﴿Then they would certainly disbelieve after it... 51﴾ (al-Rum): they would disbelieve through the despair which removes the Almighty from events, even though they have a precedent, for they had despaired and Allah relieved them.

That is because man has no patience with affliction. If it strikes him, he quickly becomes distressed. Had he said, "I have a Lord to whom I turn for refuge, and He will lift this affliction from me, and He has a wisdom which I will come to know," he would have found rest, and the matter would have been easy for him.

And you may ask: why did the Qur'an say ﴿And if We send... 51﴾ (al-Rum) and not "wa-in" (and if)? They said: this superfluous lam is what they call the "lam al-muwatti'ah lil-qasam" (the lam preparing for an oath). The sense of the sentence is: "By Allah, if We send..." So the waw here is the waw of oath, and the lam prepares for it. The Almighty may swear by whatever He wills concerning whatever He wills, and every oath requires an answer. You say: "By Allah, I will surely strike you."

Likewise, the condition with "in" (if) requires an answer to the condition. Here the Almighty has combined the oath and the condition in a single sentence. If you ask, "Is the answer here for the oath or for the condition?"

They said: the acuity of the Arabs refuses that two answers exist in one sentence, so the context brings a single answer which we dispense with the other answer. The answer belongs to what comes first: if the oath comes first, the answer is for the oath, and if the condition comes first, the answer is for the condition. Here, ﴿And if We send a wind... 51﴾ (al-Rum), the oath came first, because the sense is: "By Allah, if We send a wind..."

The word ﴿they would remain... 51﴾ (al-Rum) is derived from "shadow" (zill). "Zalla" is a defective past verb like "bata" (to spend the night), meaning to be in the night, and "adha" (to become) in the forenoon, and "amsa" in the evening. Likewise "zalla" means to continue at the time in which the shadow is present, that is, throughout the day. So we take the time from the word from which it is derived.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 52:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs in retreat.﴾

Almighty Allah wishes to console His Messenger (ﷺ), so that he does not grieve over what he encounters from his people. He says to him: "O Muhammad, do not wear yourself out, for these people will not believe. Your only duty is to convey (the message), so do not despair at the aversion of these people, and do not retreat from conveying your call, from striving (jihad) in its cause, and from proclaiming it openly, for I have sent you on a mission, and I will not abandon you. It is not (befitting) for Allah to send a messenger and then forsake him or leave him to his fate."

Almighty Allah said to His Prophet: ﴿Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps, if they do not believe in this discourse.﴾ (Al-Kahf) And if I wished, I would have made them believers by compulsion, unable to disbelieve: ﴿If We willed, We could send down to them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks would remain bowed before it.﴾ (Al-Shu'ara)

And here the Exalted says to His Prophet: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear...﴾ (Al-Rum). He has placed them in the category of the dead, though they are alive and sustained. Why? Because one who does not benefit from what he hears and is not affected by it is equal to the dead.

Or we may say: a human being has two lives: the life of the spirit, in which believer and unbeliever, obedient and disobedient, are equal; and the life of the method (manhaj) and values, which belongs to the believer in particular, and of which Allah says: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life...﴾ (Al-Anfal)

So He addresses them with this address while they are alive, but what is meant here is the life of the method and values, which is the life that bequeaths to you a lasting, enduring bliss that does not cease, an eternity that neither leaves you nor you leave it.

Therefore He, glorified is He, says of this life: ﴿And indeed the Last Abode, that is the (true) life, if they only knew.﴾ (Al-Ankabut)

Therefore Allah named the method that He sent down upon His Messenger a "spirit": ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit (rūḥ) of Our command...﴾ (Al-Shura), because the method gives you a lasting life that does not shrink or vanish.

And He named the angel who descended with it a "spirit": ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit (rūḥ) descended with it﴾ (Al-Shu'ara). So the method is a spirit from Allah, and with it descended a spirit of the angels, namely Jibril (peace be upon him), upon the heart of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that the chosen Messenger might carry it and disseminate it among all people, and they would live the life of the Hereafter.

Thus the disbelievers, in this sense, live the life of the body-spirit (rūḥ al-qālab), in which all human beings are equal, but they are dead with respect to the second spirit, the spirit of values and method.

Therefore, if there is a wretched person or a thug who corrupts society more than he reforms it, we say to him: "Your existence is like your non-existence." Why? Because life, if it is not employed in what is lasting and beneficial, has no meaning.

And here the Exalted says to His Prophet: Do not grieve, and do not let your soul waste away in regret over these people. They are dead; they have not accepted the spirit of the method and the spirit of values. As long as this spirit has not entered them, there is no hope of reforming them, and they will not respond to you. Response comes from one who lends his hearing and employs his mind upon the universe around him, to reach the reality of life and the riddle of existence.

We have previously said: If, for example, an aeroplane crashed you in a desert and you were cut off from people, with no companion and nothing around you, and then suddenly you saw before you a table laden with the finest food and drink, it is natural that before your hand extends to it you must ask yourself: "Who brought it?"

Likewise, you, O human being, have arrived in a universe prepared for your reception, filled with all this goodness. By God, does this not demand that you ask: "Who prepared this universe for me?"

Then no one claims this universe for himself. Then a messenger came to you from Allah, informing you of the realities of the universe and resolving for you the riddle of life and existence. But these people, when the Messenger of Allah came to them, refused to listen to him and did not accept the spirit with which he came.

The Truth presents this matter to us in another verse: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they go out from your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?"﴾ (Muhammad). This means that the spirit of the method has not touched their hearts.

The Truth answers them: ﴿Say: "For those who believe, it is guidance and healing. And as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place."﴾ (Fussilat)

So the Qur'an is one, but its reception differs: one hears it with an attentive ear and a conscious heart and benefits, and reaches the solution of the riddle of the universe and of creation, because he responded to the new spirit that Allah sent to him; and another turns away.

And those who turn away from the Qur'an fear only for their status and their dominion, for they are people of corruption and tyranny, and they know that this method came to restrict their freedoms and to put an end to their corruption and tyranny; therefore they rejected it.

Thus you find that those who confronted the calls of the messengers and opposed them were the lords and the great ones. Do you not read the words of the Truth, glorified is He, about their saying: ﴿Indeed, we obeyed our lords and our great ones, and they led us astray from the way﴾? (Al-Ahzab)

So do not be surprised that when the Qur'an is heard by a person, he says with delight: "God, repeat it!" and another turns away from it and does not know what he is saying. The one who turns away from the Qur'an is of two kinds: either he turns away out of arrogance, meaning he understands the Qur'an and comprehends it, but is too proud to submit to its commands; or another hears it but does not understand it, because Allah has sealed his heart.

The duty of the caller is to look after the one he calls, not to despair over his non-response, and to repeat the call to him, perhaps it will coincide with a moment of clarity in him, a natural disposition and an empty soul, so that the call bears fruit in him and he responds.

Otherwise, we have seen from the people of ignorance (jahiliyya) those who embraced Islam after a long period of the call's duration, such as Khalid ibn al-Walid, 'Amr ibn al-'As, 'Ikrima, and others.

We know how much 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was averse to Islam and hostile to its people, and the story of his beating his sister after she had embraced Islam is a well-known account, for it was the cause of his own conversion. When he beat her and wounded her until blood flowed from her, his heart softened toward his sister. When she recited the Qur'an to him, he found in him a pure heart and a sound disposition, which shook off from him the false tribal zeal of the Jahiliyya, and he was moved by the verses, and their gladness reached his heart, and he embraced Islam.(1)

Therefore Almighty Allah commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to proclaim the call openly, and to declare what he was commanded, perhaps the listener will coincide with a moment that awakens his nature, as happened with 'Umar.

When we observe the fa' (then/so) at the beginning of this verse, ﹛So indeed you cannot make the dead hear...﹜ (Al-Rum), we find that the implied meaning is: "Do not grieve, and let not their aversion alarm you, for you have not fallen short in conveying; rather, the shortcoming lies with the addressees, because they did not accept the sublime spirit that came to them, but recoiled from listening and forbade (others) from it, as the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it, that perhaps you may overcome."﴾ (Fussilat)

Their forbidding one another from listening to the Qur'an is evidence that they know that whoever hears the Qur'an with a receptive ear will inevitably believe in it and be convinced.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs in retreat.﴾ (Al-Rum). And in another place: ﴿And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness...﴾ (Fussilat). And He also said: ﴿Deaf, dumb...﴾ (Al-Baqara).

We know from the physiology of the organs that dumbness results from deafness, because the tongue reproduces what the ear has heard; so if the ear is deaf, the tongue must be mute, having nothing to reproduce.

Thus, for example, we find the Arab child who grows up in an English environment speaks English, because he heard it and learned it. Indeed, we find that the owner of the language himself is presented with strange words of his language and does not know them. Why? Because he never heard them. When an Arab says of an old woman: "She is al-ḥaizabūn and al-dardabīs (2)..." etc., you say: "What is this talk?" although it is Arabic, but your ear has not heard it.

The ear is the first instrument for receiving the message, and since Almighty Allah has judged them to be in the category of the dead, perception is impossible for them: the ear does not hear the verses of the Qur'an, and the eye does not see the signs of the universe nor contemplate them.

Therefore He, the Exalted, said of them: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blind.﴾ (Al-Hajj)

And the word "blind" we say of one who sees, with sound eyes, when he errs in something: you say to him, "Are you blind?" Why? Because although his eyes are sound, he has not used them for their purpose, so he is like the blind man.

These people, Allah described them first as being in the category of the dead, then they are afflicted with deafness, so they do not hear the message; and the picture is completed by their being blind, not seeing the signs of inimitability in the universe. Would that they were merely deaf! For the deaf may be communicated with by signs, and he benefits through his eyes if he faces you. But what is the situation when he is turned away, as the Exalted said: ﴿when they turn their backs in retreat﴾ (Al-Rum)? That is, they have presented you their backs. Thus no channel remains for them for reception or perception; they are deaf and dumb, and with turning away, sight too is disabled. So there is no hope in such people, and no way to guide them.

(1) On the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: "'Umar went out wearing his sword, and a man met him and said: 'Where are you heading, O 'Umar?' He said: 'I intend to kill Muhammad.' He said: 'And how will you be safe from the Banu Hashim and the Banu Zuhra, having killed Muhammad?' 'Umar said to him: 'I see you have also turned away and abandoned your religion which you hold.' He said: 'Shall I not direct you to a wonder: your brother-in-law and your sister have both turned away and abandoned your religion which you hold.' So 'Umar walked, furious, until he came to them, and with them was a man of the Muhajirun called Khabbab. When Khabbab heard the sound of 'Umar, he hid in the house, and 'Umar entered upon them and said: 'What is this murmuring I heard from you? Perhaps you have turned away?' His brother-in-law said to him: 'O 'Umar, what if the truth is in other than your religion?' 'Umar leapt upon his brother-in-law and trampled him severely. His sister came to push him away from her husband, and he struck her with a blow of his hand so that her face bled. She said, angry: 'Even if the truth is in other than your religion, I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'" This situation led 'Umar to go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the house of Ibn Abi al-Arqam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out until he reached 'Umar, seized the edges of his garment and the strap of his sword, and said: "You will not desist, O 'Umar, until Allah sends down upon you the disgrace and punishment He sent down upon al-Walid ibn al-Mughira." So 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah, and that you are His servant and Messenger," and he embraced Islam. Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (2/219-220).

(2) Al-ḥaizabūn: the old woman; the nun is extra, as it is added in al-zaytūn. (Lisan al-'Arab, root ḥ-z-b.)
al-dardabīs: the old man, great of care (worn out), decrepit; an old woman is also called dardabīs. (Lisan al-'Arab, roots d-r-d-b, d-r-b-s.)

Guidance upon the path and leading to it cannot be achieved with blindness, especially when the blind person insists on his blindness. We say of one who is stubborn about blindness: "So-and-so gives blindness its due" (meaning: he disdains to seek help from the one who can see). Had he sought help from the people around him, he would have found them serving him, and he would have become one who sees through their sight.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Surely you cannot make the deaf to hear... 53﴾ (al-Rum). That is: you cannot make [them] hear, ﴿except those who believe in Our signs, so they are Muslims 53﴾. These are the pure of heart and of natural disposition (fitrah), who turn their attention to the existence of God, and so they infer the Creator from creation and the Maker from the cosmos, glorified is He. And why not? We know the one who invented the simplest things in our lives, and we record his history and commemorate him: do we not know Edison, who invented the electric lamp? Then the God who created the sun is more deserving of being known.

So when a messenger from God comes to you, informing you of His existence, and resolving for you the riddle of this existence about which you are perplexed, it is incumbent upon you to believe him and to affirm what he has brought you. Therefore, glorified is He, instructs the messengers to say to people in the wake of delivering the message: ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it... 109﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

In this is an indication that the work which the messengers perform for their peoples is work for which they deserve a wage by the judgment of reason, but they rise above taking your wages, because their work is precious and none can estimate it except the One who sent them, and He alone is able to give them their rewards.

The meaning of ﴿believe in Our signs... 53﴾ (al-Rum) is: they look into them and contemplate them, and they stand upon the wonders of creation in the cosmos that point to the power of the Creator. So when a messenger from God comes to them, they turn to him and believe in him. Therefore He said after it: ﴿so they are Muslims 53﴾ (al-Rum).

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.﴾ [30:54]

The Truth, blessed and exalted, after having set before us some of the proofs in the universe around us, says to us: Why should we go far if the signs in the universe around you are not sufficient? Then look into the signs within yourselves, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And within yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾ [51:21] and He combined the two kinds in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth...﴾ [41:53]

Here He says: Reflect upon yourself: ﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness...﴾ [30:54]. If the accountable person now says: I did not witness the stage of weakness from which I was created.

We say: Yes, you did not witness it in yourself, for you had no observation of it at that time, but you witnessed it in others. You witnessed it in the despised fluid from which the fetus is formed, in the pregnant mother, and in the woman when she gives birth to her child, small and weak, with no foot to walk, no hand to strike, no tooth to cut. Yet with Allah's care your Lord raised you until you reached the stage of strength in which you are now.

So the evidence of weakness is witnessed by every human being, not in himself, but in others, and in what he observes every day. Each of us has seen hundreds of children at the various stages of growth. The child is born without power or strength, then he begins to grow and mature, so he is able to sit, then to crawl, then to walk, until his organs are complete and he reaches the stage of maturity and vigor.

At that point the Truth, glorified and exalted, holds him accountable, and we too should hold him accountable, and we should exploit this period of youth in productive work. We see that when a ripe fruit is not picked by its owner, it falls into his hands, as if it wants to fulfill the task for which Allah created it.

Therefore, our affliction, and one of the causes of the backwardness of our societies, is that we prolong the childhood of our children. We treat the young man until the age of twenty-five as a child: we must fulfill all his desires, and nothing is lacking except that we nurse him.

Our affliction is that we have a tenderness (mirq) that has no meaning. As for outside our countries, once the young man reaches maturity, he no longer has a right over his father; rather, the right passes to the father over him, and he bears the responsibility himself.

The Truth, glorified is He, teaches us in raising children to make them accustomed to bearing responsibility at this age: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission as those before them did...﴾ [24:59]

So look, O human being, you for whom Allah has made all the species stronger than you in your service. Look into yourself and the signs within it, and the manifestations of Allah's power within your two sides. For you were raised weak, unable to do anything; others served you.

Among His wisdom, exalted is He, regarding the child: his teeth do not appear throughout the nursing period, so that he does not harm his mother. Then temporary teeth emerge for him, which they call milk teeth, because he is still small and cannot clean them. Allah made them temporary until he grows and becomes able to clean them; they fall out and permanent teeth replace them. And if you reflected upon yourself, you would find signs beyond counting.

﴿Then made after weakness strength...﴾ [30:54], i.e., the strength of youth and vigor. ﴿Then made after strength weakness and gray hair...﴾ [30:54], i.e., the weakness of old age. This weakness spreads through all the organs, even knowledge and memory: ﴿so that after knowledge he knows nothing...﴾ [22:5]

This weakness persists in you until you become like a child in everything, needing someone to carry and serve you. So do not take this matter as a matter of your own constitution, but by the will of the One who constitutes you, glorified is He. After you were weak, He strengthens you; and He, glorified is He, is able to return you to weakness such that the drugs of this world cannot return you to strength. Therefore one of the wise mocks those who take vitamins in old age, saying: Woe to him whose vitamins are not from his back.

Thus you notice the precision of expression in the words of our master Zakariyya: ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened within me...﴾ [19:4], because the bone is the last storehouse of a person's sustenance, where what exceeds the body's need of energy is stored. When the body is not nourished with food, it draws from this store of fats and grease, then from the muscle, then from the bone marrow, which is the last storehouse of sustenance in your body.

So the meaning of our master Zakariyya's words, ﴿indeed my bones have weakened within me...﴾ [19:4], is: I have reached the stage of ḥaraḍ(1), in which there is no hope of strength. He confirms this meaning with His words: ﴿and the head has glistened with gray hair...﴾ [19:4]

We have said that whiteness of hair is not a color; rather, whiteness is the absence of color. Therefore white is not among the colors of the spectrum. With old age the body's systems weaken, and the glands responsible for hair color weaken in secreting black pigment, so the hair appears colorless.

We notice that most people who go gray go gray at the sideburns, from here and from here. Why? They say: because the hair is a fine tube; when it is cut during shaving, this tube opens, and certain chemical substances such as soap and cologne enter it, affecting the pigmented follicles and destroying them. Therefore we notice this phenomenon frequently among the affluent in particular; that is why you find some young men with gray in these areas of the head.

Our master Zakariyya arranged the manifestations of weakness according to their importance: he said first ﴿my bones have weakened within me...﴾ [19:4], then ﴿and the head has glistened with gray hair...﴾ [19:4]. Despite Zakariyya's old age and weakness, and although his wife was barren, Allah, exalted is He, responded to his request for a child who would inherit prophethood from him. He gave him the good news of a son and named him Yahya. It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted, says to us: Beware, can I not create with gray hair, old age, and weakness? Therefore after it He said: ﴿He creates what He wills...﴾ [30:54]

And concerning Zakariyya, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿He said: So (it will be). Your Lord says: It is easy for Me, and I created you before when you were nothing.﴾ [19:9]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He is the Knowing, the Competent﴾ [30:54], i.e., this creation arises from knowledge: ﴿Does He not know who created, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?﴾ [67:14] But knowledge alone is not enough, for you may be knowledgeable yet unable to implement what you know, like the electrical engineer who has extensive knowledge of electricity but cannot build the network of a power plant, so he goes to one of the financiers to help him implement it. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, described Himself with knowledge and power.

So this is the psychological proof of the true Originator, the Active, the Chooser, who does things with knowledge and power, and for whom action costs nothing and takes no time, because He, glorified is He, says to a thing: "Be," and it is. Do not be surprised that your Lord says to a thing "Be" and it is, for you, O weak creature, do this with your limbs and members.

Otherwise, tell me: what do you do if you want to stand, for example, or carry something? Merely by wanting movement, you find your limbs obeying your will, without your knowing what happens within you of emotions and movements. And if you say: "I am big and I can perform these movements as I wish," then what about the small child?

We had earlier given an example to clarify this matter with the bulldozer: each of its movements has a lever specifically for it, operated by the driver, and buttons he presses; perhaps the driver needs more than one tool to move this machine in one movement.

As for you, merely wishing to move a limb, you find it moving with you as you wish, without knowing the muscles and nerves that participated in its movement. If you are in this condition, should I be surprised that Allah, exalted is He, says to a thing "Be" and it is?

(1) Ḥaraḍ: the fallen one who cannot rise. (Lisan al-'Arab, root ḥ-r-ḍ.)

Then the Almighty, glory be to Him, says:

﴿On the day the Hour comes, the criminals will swear that they tarried but an hour. Thus were they ever deluded.﴾ (55)

After the Almighty, may He be exalted, has presented the proof so that whoever wills may be guided by it, and whoever is not guided is warned by this threat: ﴿On the day the Hour comes, the criminals will swear that they tarried but an hour...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55). The word ﴿comes [taqum]...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55) indicates that the Hour already exists, but is sleeping, awaiting permission to act. It rises, awaiting the Word: "Be," and it is.

The word "rising" (qiyam) here carries its own meaning, because the Hour is not something that can be brought about by someone rising. Only the Almighty establishes it. His saying ﴿comes [taqum]...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55) is as if it were regulated, the way an alarm clock is regulated, and it has a time it awaits. When its time comes, it rises of its own accord.

When you reflect on the word ﴿comes [taqum]...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55), you find that rising (qiyam) is the last stage of a person in order to carry out his task. Its opposite precedes it: before rising comes sitting, then reclining, then sleep. So the meaning of "the rising of the Hour" is that it has come to carry out its task completely.

The Hour is named so because it indicates the time at which God permits the world to end. Yet for us the "hour" is a unit for measuring time. We say: "morning" or "evening," according to the reckoning of the government or the people, "such-and-such a time" or "such-and-such."

This machine in our hands, with what it regulates for us of time, is a simple matter. It is no problem if it runs fast or slow by a few seconds or a few minutes, whether it works automatically or by batteries, whether it was made in Switzerland or in China. This clock does not matter. What matters is the other clock, the hour after which there is no hour. Know that it is regulated by the Almighty, and you have only to regulate yourself by it and make a thousand calculations for it.

It is strange that the disbelievers will swear on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿that they tarried but an hour...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55). If they lied in this world, do they also lie in the Hereafter? It has been said: rather, they say it according to their own assumption. Otherwise, their speech at that time is not a matter of choice, for the time of choice has passed, and they are no longer able to lie.

Therefore the Almighty says at the end of the verse: ﴿Thus were they ever deluded﴾ (Al-Rum, 55). They used to turn realities upside down in this world, but in the Hereafter they will not turn realities upside down. Rather, they will speak according to their own view.

"The criminals" (al-mujrimun): the criminal (al-mujrim) is one who has departed from what is required of him through a sin that opposes it. We say: "So-and-so committed a crime (ajrama)," and the law calls the act a crime (jarimah).

The meaning of ﴿they tarried...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55): "tarrying" (al-labth) is remaining for a long time, that is, in the world. Or it means: they tarried in their graves after death until the Hour of rising, when the dead are brought to life.

So there are three periods of their tarrying in the graves. The longest belongs to those who died since Adam, peace be upon him. The middle belongs to those who came after them, like us. The shortest tarrying belongs to those who die between the two blasts of the Trumpet. In all these periods there are disbelievers. In the time of Adam there were disbelievers, and throughout the ages after him there are disbelievers, and even between the two blasts there are disbelievers. Therefore the word "tarried" here is general: some tarried a long time, some a long time, and some a short time, and some a shorter time.

These people will say on the Day of Resurrection: "We tarried but an hour," although there is no lying in the Hereafter. But they say it according to their assumption, because one who is absent from time does not know it. Time is the container for the occurrence of events, just as place is the container for their location. The sleeper, for example, does not perceive time, because time is measured by the succession of events within it. If you do not perceive an event, you consequently do not perceive the time, whether by sleep, like the People of the Cave, or by death, like the one whom God caused to die for a hundred years and then raised up.(1)

When they rose from sleep or death, they estimated time only according to the custom of people in sleep. They said: ﴿We have remained a day or part of a day...﴾ (Al-Kahf, 19), because in this state one does not perceive time, but only the time that follows events. As long as a person is in this state and does not grasp time, he is truthful in what he reports according to his assumption.

Therefore the Almighty says in another verse: ﴿He said, "How long did you remain on earth, counting years?" They said, "We remained a day or part of a day, so ask those who count."﴾ (Al-Mu'minun, 112–113)

That is, ask those who count time and keep account of it for us. The intended ones are the angels,(2) for they are the ones who know events and record them from the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, until now, and until the Hour rises.

So no one is asked about a number except one who has actually counted, or one who is able to count. As for a thing that is not an object of counting and enumeration, it is not counted. Has anyone in the world counted the sands of the desert, for example? Therefore we hear in jokes that one man asked another: "Do you know how many stars there are in the sky?" He said: "Nine thousand million, five hundred thousand, and ninety-three stars." The first said: "You are a liar." The other said: "Go up and count them."

But why do the disbelievers belittle time, so that they swear on the day the Hour rises that they tarried but an hour? In another place He says about them: ﴿As if, on the day they see it, they had not remained but an evening or a morning.﴾ (An-Nazi'at, 46)

It has been said: because time differs according to people's conditions within it. One wishes that time had lengthened for him, and another wishes that it had shortened. The moments that gather you and those you love pass swiftly, and you wish they would last longer, unlike the time you spend reluctantly with someone you dislike, which passes slowly and heavily.

As the poet says:

The events of joy are weighed by the measure,
while calamities are measured by the bushel.(3)

Another says:

Leave patience, O lover, for your farewell is public;
whoever keeps his secret, you have kept his trust.

He grinds his teeth that the journey did not add
provision on those steps when he bade you farewell.

Until he says:

If your night is prolonged after you,
how often I complained that the night was short with you.

So in times of joy, time is short, and in times of grief, time is long and heavy. Have you not heard the one who said, when the night gathered his shattered self with one he loved:

O night, lengthen! O sleep, be gone! O dawn, stand still and do not rise!

Likewise, one who awaits joy finds time slow, and wishes it would pass quickly so that he may see the joy he awaits. But one who expects evil or awaits it wishes that time would lengthen, to keep him away from the evil he fears.

Therefore we find the believers wishing that time were shorter, because they are certain of the good that awaits them and the bliss they were promised. But the criminals are the opposite: they wish that time would lengthen, to keep them away from the punishment that awaits them. Therefore they say: ﴿We tarried in the world only a little,﴾ and: ﴿Would that it had been prolonged for us!﴾ Either because they do not know time, so they speak according to their assumption, or because they want something that will keep the punishment away from them.

So: they swore that they tarried but an hour, either by way of assumption, or because one who is heedless of events does not know time and cannot count it, like 'Uzayr, whom God caused to die for a hundred years and then raised up. ﴿He said, "How long have you remained?" He said, "I remained a day or part of a day..."﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 259). Then his Lord informed him that he had remained a hundred years. ﴿He said, "Rather, you remained a hundred years..."﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 259)

There is no doubt that God, the Exalted, is truthful in what He reports. Likewise 'Uzayr was truthful in his judgment about time. Therefore the Almighty, glory be to Him and exalted, established the proof of the truth of both statements. He said: ﴿Look at your food and your drink, which have not spoiled...﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 259). Food does not change in a day or part of a day, so the food and drink stood as proof of the man's truthfulness.

Then He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And look at your donkey, and that We may make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones, how We raise them and then clothe them with flesh...﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 259)

So the decayed bones stood as proof of His truthfulness regarding the hundred years. Do not say: "How can both statements be reconciled?" For the one who ordered this matter is the Lord, glory be to Him, the Restrainer and the Expander. He contracts time for some people and expands it for others.

This verse, ﴿On the day the Hour comes...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55), came after God's establishing the excuse of the disbelievers through His messengers. The meaning of "establishing the excuse" is removing their excuse, in that He, glory be to Him, did not make clear to them the proofs of faith, in its foundation in belief in one God, and the proofs of faith in the Messenger through miracles, so that they would believe in the verses of rulings concerning "do" and "do not do."

As we have said, the verses are of three kinds: verses that establish the foundation of belief, which is faith in the existence of the Capable, Wise God; verses that establish the truthfulness of the communication from God through His messengers, which are the miracles; and verses that carry the rulings.

The Almighty does not require those who believe in Him to believe in His rulings concerning "do" and "do not do" unless they are first convinced of the Messenger who conveys from God through a miracle. They cannot believe in the Messenger who conveys from God unless the existence of God is established for them, and the existence of God is established in the signs of the cosmos.

Therefore the Almighty always presents to us His signs in the cosmos, but He presents them separately. He does not pour them upon us all at once. He brings a sign and then follows it with their denial and refusal, so that He brings the sign and its result from them. This is to repeat the establishing of the excuse against them, that there is no longer any excuse for them not to believe.

We notice this repetition in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news, and that He may let you taste of His mercy, and that the ships may run by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ (46)

Then He mentions that these signs did not benefit them: ﴿We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs, so We took vengeance upon those who committed crimes, and it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers.﴾ (47) (Al-Rum)

Then He brings another sign: ﴿It is God who sends the winds, so they stir up clouds, and He spreads them across the sky however He wills, and makes them fragments, so you see the rain coming out from within them. Then when He sends it upon whomever He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice. And even though they were, before it was sent down upon them, in despair. So look at the traces of God's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the one who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.﴾ (48–50) (Al-Rum)

Then He, glory be to Him, mentions what they did after all these signs: ﴿And if We send a wind and they see it turn yellow, they would certainly continue to disbelieve after it.﴾ (51) (Al-Rum)

Thus the Almighty mentions the sign, and follows it with their denial, and repeats it so that no argument remains for them to use in disbelief. Then this verse comes: ﴿On the day the Hour comes, the criminals will swear that they tarried but an hour...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55), to say to them: If you have denied all these signs, there will come to you a sign you cannot deny, which is the Resurrection.

It is strange that they swear by God in the Hereafter that they tarried but an hour, when they disbelieved in Him, glory be to Him, in the world.

In the verse there is a paronomasia (jinas) between the first word "the Hour" (al-sa'ah) and the second "hour" (sa'ah). The word is one, but the meaning differs. ﴿On the day the Hour comes...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55) means the Resurrection. ﴿...the criminals will swear that they tarried but an hour...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55) means a period of time. Among this is the poet's saying:

I departed from the abodes, and I am a captive for you,
and my heart, in your love, is a captive.

That is, "captive" (ma'sur) [in the sense of "taken captive"].

Between me and my colleague Dr. Muhammad 'Abd al-Mun'im Khafajah, may God prolong his life, there is a story concerning paronomasia. In one of the rhetoric classes, the teacher said: "There is no complete paronomasia (jinas tam) in the Qur'an except in this verse, between sa'ah and sa'ah. But there is in it an incomplete paronomasia (jinas naqis)." Dr. Muhammad raised his finger and said: "Sir, I do not like it said that there is something incomplete in the Qur'an."

The Shaykh laughed at him and said to him: "Then what shall we say?" The rhetoricians divided paronomasia into complete (tam) and incomplete (naqis). The first is when the two words agree in the number of letters, their order, and their vowel patterns. If anything differs among them, the paronomasia between them is incomplete, as in His saying: ﴿Woe to every slanderer, defamer﴾ (Al-Humazah, 1). Between humazah and lumazah there is an incomplete paronomasia, because they differ in the first letter.

I recall that the Shaykh gestured toward me and said: "What is your opinion of what your companion says?" I said: "We call it paronomasia of the whole (jinas kull) and paronomasia of the part (jinas ba'd), meaning that the two words agree in all the letters or in some of them. In that way we do not say in the Qur'an: incomplete paronomasia."

So their saying ﴿they tarried but an hour...﴾ (Al-Rum, 55) refers to the temporal hour that we know. Time has measures: second, minute, hour, day, week, month, year, century, and eon. They mean the temporal hour known to us.

Therefore they belittle the duration of their stay in the world, or in the graves, when the Resurrection suddenly overtakes them. We had informed them, while they were in the ease of the world, that...

(1) He is 'Uzayr. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related this from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi. This is the well-known view. Salman ibn Buraydah said: he is Hizqil ibn Bawar. Ibn Kathir said: "As for the town, the well-known view is that it is Bayt al-Maqdis, which he passed after Bakhtnasr had destroyed it and killed its people." (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/314).

(2) Said by Mujahid. Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/122), attributed to Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

(3) Al-qafzan is the plural of qafiz, a measure that people have agreed upon. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-'Arab (root q-f-z): "It is eight makakik according to the people of Iraq, and the makuk is three kilas," meaning that a single qafiz is 24 kila, about 288 kilograms.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: "You have indeed remained, by the Decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection. This is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not aware."﴾

Here He says: ﴿knowledge and faith...﴾ (al-Rum). So does knowledge contradict faith? No. But there is a difference between them: knowledge is acquired, while faith means you believe in Allah though you have not seen Him. So there is something you see and know yourself, and there is something another person tells you that he has seen, and you believe in his truthfulness and so you accept it as true. Thus there is affirmation of knowledge and affirmation of faith. Therefore it is always said: faith concerns what is unseen to you. But when your faith grows strong and your certainty increases, the unseen becomes, for you, like the seen.

We have clarified this matter in our discussion of His words, addressing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ):﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (al-Fil, 1)

He said: Have you not seen? The Prophet (ﷺ) was born in the Year of the Elephant, and it was not possible for him to have witnessed this event. They said: because Allah's report to him is more truthful than seeing it with one's own eyes.

So His words ﴿given knowledge and faith...﴾ (al-Rum) mean: you acquire knowledge either through deduction and evidences... etc., or you take it from one who informs you, and you accept what he reports. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) asked a Companion(¹): "How have you woken up?" he said: "I have woken up a true believer." He said: "Every truth has a reality; what is the reality of your faith?"

That is: what is the meaning of this word you have said?

The Companion said: "My soul has turned away from this world, so its gold and its clay(²) are alike to me, and it is as though I look upon the people of Paradise enjoying its bounties, and the people of the Fire being tormented in it." He meant to say to the Messenger of Allah: "I have woken up as though I see what you have told us." So the Messenger of Allah said to him: "You have known, so hold fast to it."(³)

But who are those who were given knowledge? They are the angels, who were present at everything, since they do not die; or the Prophets, because He who sent them informed them; or the believers, because they affirmed the Messenger in what he reported.

He said ﴿were given knowledge...﴾ (al-Rum) and did not say "they knew," as if knowledge is not acquired but is a bestowal from a Knowing One greater than you who gives it to you. If you say: Do scholars not play a role in reasoning and considering the evidences? We say: Yes, but who established these evidences for them? So knowledge is a gift from Allah.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿You have indeed remained, by the Decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection...﴾ (al-Rum), meaning: a matter inscribed and fixed in the Preserved Tablet until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿This is the Day of Resurrection...﴾ (al-Rum), the one you used to deny. Now you must affirm it, for something has come to you that you cannot deny, since it has become a reality; and it would be in your interest that your excuse be accepted, but it will not be accepted from you, and We will not listen to any words from you, because We had already presented the excuse.

As for His words ﴿but you were not aware﴾ (al-Rum): at the beginning of the verse He said ﴿were given knowledge...﴾ (al-Rum), attributing knowledge to Allah, whereas here He attributes ignorance to them, because Allah set up the evidences for them and they took nothing from them; He set up for them proofs, arguments and signs, and they were heedless of them. So they did not take from the indications and proofs what would lead them to knowledge.

(¹) He is al-Harith ibn Malik al-Ansari. Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani mentioned him in *al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah* (1/343) and attributed the hadith to Ibn al-Mubarak in *al-Zuhd*.
(²) Al-Madar: pieces of dried clay. It is also said: sticky clay without sand. (*Lisan al-Arab*, root m-d-r).
(³) Cited by al-Haythami in *Majma' al-Zawa'id* (1/57), who attributed it to al-Tabarani in *al-Kabir* from the hadith of al-Harith ibn Malik al-Ansari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 57:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿On that Day, those who did wrong will not benefit from their excuses, nor will they be given the chance to make amends.﴾

His saying ﴿On that Day...﴾ (al-Rum) means: the Day the Hour is established. ﴿Their excuses will not benefit those who did wrong...﴾ (al-Rum) means: no excuse of theirs will be accepted. And the meaning of ﴿who did wrong...﴾ (al-Rum) is: they wronged themselves. The wrongdoer resorts to wrongdoing because he wants to take from others what his own effort has failed to attain.

Wrongdoing is that you take the fruit of another's sweat and turn it into blood within you. But your blood, if it does not come from your own sweat, is corrupt blood against you, and no movement of obedience will ever come forth from it in existence; its outcome must be movements of evil, because it is unlawful blood. How, then, could it move in the way of what is lawful?

For this reason, the noble hadith has been related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, Allah is Good and accepts only what is good, and Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers. So He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds; indeed, I am Knowing of what you do.﴾ (al-Mu'minun 51) And He said: ﴿O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah, if it is Him that you worship.﴾ (al-Baqarah 172)" Then he mentioned a man who travels far, disheveled and dusty, who raises his hands to the sky and says: "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, and his clothing is unlawful, and he is nourished with the unlawful; so how could he be answered?"(1)

So then: how could we be answered, when all our parts are unfit to address Allah in supplication?

The matter does not stop at the non-acceptance of excuses; rather, ﴿nor will they be given the chance to make amends (yastaʿtabun)﴾ (al-Rum 57). Al-'Atab (reproach) is a gentle and affectionate dialogue between two people about a matter that has angered one of them, a matter that was not expected to happen, and it must be presented to him so that he may clear his heart of it. For example, a friend passes by you and does not greet you, so you become angry with him. If you are keen on his affection, you meet him and say: "By God, I have something in my heart against you, because you passed me on such-and-such day and did not greet me." He then says: "By God, I was busy with such-and-such and did not see you." This excuse removes from your heart what was in it against your friend.

We say: "So-and-so reproached so-and-so, and he made him content (a'taba-hu)," meaning: he removed his reproach. For this reason they say: "Affection remains as long as reproach remains." And the poet says:

"As for reproach, it wears down the beloved, yet love is set right by reproach and made true."

The hamza in a'taba is called the hamza of removal (hamzat al-izalah), and from it is the saying of the poet:

"I wish to forsake you — that is, by my reason — while the heart refuses; and I make you content, though my soul is full of reproach."

And from it is what came in the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ) to his Lord on the day of Ta'if, after what he suffered from them, until he took refuge at a wall and began to address his Lord: "O Lord, to whom do You entrust me? To a distant one who frowns upon me, or to an enemy You have given power over my affair? If there is no anger from You against me, I do not mind; but Your well-being is more spacious for me... until he says: 'To You is the making of amends until You are pleased.'"(3)

That is: O Lord, if You are angry at something that came from me, then I want to remove Your reproach against me.

From the hamza of removal is our saying a'jamtu al-kalimah, meaning: I removed its obscurity and concealment, and clarified its meaning. From this we call a dictionary (mu'jam) because it removes the obscurity of words and makes them clear.

In this regard, you may read His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; I am almost concealing it...﴾ (Ta-Ha 15), meaning: I am nearly about to remove its concealment through signs and indications.

This word ﴿yastaʿtabun﴾ (al-Rum 57) occurs in the Qur'an three times(4), and it occurs once in the active form (yastaʿtibun)(5), because they sought the removal of their reproach, and God did not remove it and did not permit them to remove it. As for the passive form (yustaʿtabun), it is because they did not seek to be reconciled by themselves; rather they appointed intercessors to plead for them, but their expectation was disappointed in this and in that.
