So the meaning of ﴿nor will they be given the chance to make amends﴾ (al-Rum 57) is: no intercessor will dare to say to them, "Seek the reconciliation of your Lord, and ask Him to be content with you," that is, to remove the reproach from you.

1. Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/328), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1015), and al-Darimi in his Sunan (2/300), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).
2. Jahamahu: he met him with a disagreeable face, i.e., he confronts me with harshness and a repulsive face. A man is jahm al-wajh, meaning: of a scowling face. (Lisan al-'Arab, root j-h-m)
3. This supplication was recorded by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (2/420). The people of Ta'if had incited their foolish ones and slaves against the Prophet (ﷺ), who cursed him and shouted at him, until the people gathered around him and drove him to a wall belonging to 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah and Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reassured, he made this supplication.
4. Yustaʿtabun in the passive form occurs in three places: ﴿Then they will not be permitted, nor will they be given the chance to make amends﴾ (al-Nahl 84); ﴿On that Day, those who did wrong will not benefit from their excuses, nor will they be given the chance to make amends﴾ (al-Rum 57); ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it, nor will they be given the chance to make amends﴾ (al-Jathiyah 35).
5. This is in His saying: ﴿And if they seek to make amends, they will not be among those granted amends﴾ (Fussilat 24).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 58:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example. But if you brought them a sign, those who disbelieve would surely say, "You are nothing but falsifiers."﴾

This verse means that We have left no excuse for anyone among those who disbelieved their messengers, because We have brought them many examples and various kinds of evidence that can be seen, so that they might infer from them what is unseen, and take from their own eyes and senses a proof of what is hidden from them.

When He, glory be to Him, wants to convince them to believe in one God with no partner, He strikes for them this example from the reality of their own lives: ﴿Allah presents an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging entirely to one man. Are they equal in comparison?...﴾ [Az-Zumar: 29]

Is a slave belonging to one master equal to a slave belonging to several masters who pull him in different directions? If one of them is pleased, he angers the others?

Then He brings the matter closer through an example from the self, and nothing is closer to a human being than his own self. So the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿He presents to you an example from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal therein, fearing them as you fear one another? Thus do We detail the verses for a people who reason.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 28]

The meaning: if you do not accept that your slaves be partners with you in what Allah has provided you, so that you are equal in that provision, then how do you accept partnership in the right of Allah, exalted is He?

And when the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to nullify their associating partners with Him and their worship of deities, He strikes for them this example: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gather together for it. And if the fly should steal from them something, they could not retrieve it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ [Al-Hajj: 73]

The word "mathal" (example) means that you liken one thing to another and attach the hidden to the manifest, in order to clarify it and to settle it in the mind of the hearer, as when you liken an unknown person to a known person. This is called mathal or mithl; we say: "So-and-so is like so-and-so."

As for the proverb (mathal), it is a saying from a wise person that spread on people's tongues, and people repeat it whenever its occasion arises. We have previously given an example of this: the king who sent a woman to propose marriage on his behalf, Umm Iyas bint Awf ibn Mihlam al-Shaybani, whose name was ʿIsam. When she returned from her mission, he hastened to her saying: "What is behind you, O ʿIsam?" It then became a proverb said on such an occasion, although it was said about a specific incident.

The proverb is said as it is; we do not change anything in it. We say: "Ma waraʾaki, yā ʿIsām" to the masculine and the feminine, to the singular, the dual and the plural.

From this, we liken the generous to Hatim, and the brave to ʿAntara, etc., because Hatim al-Ta'i became the proverbial example of generosity, and ʿAntara of bravery. In proverbs, we say to one who confronts someone stronger than himself: "If you are a wind, you have met a whirlwind," and to one who has not prepared for a matter: "Before shooting, fill the quivers" (Qabl al-rama' tamla' al-kana'in).

So: the proverb is a saying that likens its present target to its former source, because the original source was strong and concise, therefore it was memorized and passed on by tongues.

The Qur'an follows the style of the Arabs and their manner of expression and clarifying meaning through proverbs, to the point that the gnat is used as an example. Some people are too proud to have the Qur'an, in its majesty and greatness, strike an example with a gnat, and they do not know that Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example of a mosquito or what is above it...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 26]

And the phrase ﴿or what is above it﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 26] does not mean greater in size, as some suppose, who say: "Why does He say 'or what is above it' when it would be a fortiori?" Rather, the intended meaning is what is above it in smallness and in what you find contemptible in its insignificance, such as microorganisms, viruses, etc.

But why does Allah strike examples for people? They said: because the human being has multiple senses: he sees, hears, smells, tastes, touches, etc. If you reflect on all these senses, you will find that the thing most closely attached to sensation is to be struck. Therefore, when you want to wake a person from sleep, he may not hear your call, so you go to him and shake him as if you were striking him, and he gets up.

So: striking is the effect whose significance never fails. Among this is His saying: ﴿And others travel through the land seeking of the bounty of Allah...﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 20], meaning they make a clear impact upon it, like tilling, which is most akin to striking.

A striking does not perform its task and have an effect unless it is such that it pains the one struck and does not hurt the striker; otherwise you might strike something forcefully and your hand would be pained, as though you had struck yourself. This meaning was perceived by the poet, who said to those who do not believe in the decree of Allah:

O you who mock the varieties of destiny, you blame yourself, not the decree.
And O you who strike a rock with a staff: the staff was struck, but did the rock feel it?

So the Truth, glory be to Him, strikes the example so that you may feel it, and you sense it with the sensation of pain from a blow. If a person does not feel the striking of the example, he is like one who does not feel an actual physical blow, and this, God forbid, is one lacking sensation or with paralyzed sense.

Thus the meaning of ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example...﴾ [Ar-Rum: 58] is: We have brought them examples and proofs that no one can fail to receive, just as one receives a blow, because striking is the last stage of perception.

We have previously said that the Truth, glory be to Him, gave an example for Himself in His saying: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp...﴾ [An-Nur: 35]

The example here is not for His light, exalted is He, as some suppose; rather it is an example of His illuminating the vast universe. He illuminates you sensorily through the sun, the moon and the stars, and He illuminates you spiritually through the method and the values.

The benefit of sensory light is that it removes darkness, so that you walk upon guidance and insight, and your steps and direction are safe from destroying what is less than you, or being destroyed by what is stronger than you. The outcome is that you do not harm the weaker than you, and the stronger than you does not harm you.

Likewise is spiritual light, the light of values and method, which prevents you from harming others and prevents others from harming you. Just as sensory light saves you from sensory dangers, so light of values saves you from spiritual dangers.

Therefore, after giving us this example, He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ [An-Nur: 35]

We have also mentioned what Abu Tammam(1) said in praising one of the caliphs:

The boldness of ʿAmr, the generosity of Hatim, the forbearance of al-Ahnaf, the intelligence of Iyas.

One of his envious rivals said, regarding his position with the caliph: "Do you liken the caliph to the uncouth Arabs?" He lowered his head for a moment, then completed in the same meter and rhyme:

Do not deny my striking for him an example, unusual in generosity and valor,
For Allah has struck for the lesser light an example from the niche and the lamp.(2)(3)

What is even more remarkable is that they took the paper he had with him and did not find these two verses in it, which means that he improvised them on the spot. I said: By God, if they had found these verses prepared with him, it would not have diminished his standing; rather it would indicate his intelligence, his foresight for his affair, and his anticipation of what the envious and the spiteful might say against him.

But these examples do not benefit them, and it would be well if the matter ended at this point. Rather: ﴿And if you brought them a sign...﴾ [Ar-Rum: 58], that is, a new one, ﴿those who disbelieve would surely say, "You are nothing but falsifiers."﴾ [Ar-Rum: 58], so they accuse the messengers in their conveying from Allah of being people of falsehood and lies.

The Truth, glory be to Him, argues against the people that He did not grant them the signs they proposed, because the precedents with the nations that denied the messengers confirm this. They used to ask for signs, Allah would give them what they asked for, and they would only increase in denial.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We did not withhold from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them...﴾ [Al-Isra': 59]

So the matter does not go beyond their wish to prolong the procedures and extend the time in fruitless disputation. Furthermore, granting them what they asked for despite their denial of previous signs was out of consideration for their unbelief, and as proof that the earlier signs were insufficient. Evidence of this is that He brought them another sign. Therefore, the absence of further signs means that the earlier signs were sufficient for belief, but they did not believe; thus We shall not answer their request for new signs.

This matter is clear in the debate of Abraham, peace be upon him, with Nimrod, in His saying: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death..."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 258]

At that point Abraham, peace be upon him, sensed that his opponent was inclined to dispute and sophistry, and that he wanted to prolong the debate and waste time in back-and-forth. Therefore he turned away from this argument, although his opponent truly neither gives life nor causes death, and drove him to another argument from which he could not escape, and in which he found no way to evasion. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 258] So what did this obstinate one say? ﴿So the one who disbelieved was overwhelmed, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 258]

Likewise Pharaoh used to resort to this method in his dialogue with Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them. In every situation he would say: ﴿"Who then is your Lord, O Moses?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 49] It is barren argument, resorted to by one who has gone bankrupt and finds no proof to rely upon.

We notice in the style of the verse the singular form in ﴿But if you brought them a sign...﴾ [Ar-Rum: 58], then it shifts to the plural in ﴿...those who disbelieve would surely say, "You are nothing but falsifiers."﴾ [Ar-Rum: 58]. They did not say to their messenger, for example, "You are a falsifier." Why? They said: because when a messenger is denied by his people, they say, "You are a falsifier," and perhaps among his followers who believe in him there are those who defend him and testify to his truthfulness. So the plural form came to indicate comprehensiveness, as if they were saying: "You are a falsifier, and everyone who ... clings to you."

Or the meaning is: ﴿You are...﴾ [Ar-Rum: 58], that is, all the messengers, ﴿falsifiers﴾ [Ar-Rum: 58], that is, liars who fabricate from themselves and say: "It is from Allah." It is strange of these people that they believe in Allah yet deny His messengers, like the Meccan disbelievers who gloated over the Messenger of Allah when revelation paused, saying: "Muhammad's Lord has forsaken him" (4).

They did not realize that revelation was exhausting the Messenger of Allah, and that it was difficult for him at the beginning, to the point that he came to his wife Khadijah saying: "Wrap me up, wrap me up, cover me, cover me," and his forehead was dripping with sweat. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said about the angel: "He embraced me until the strain reached me" (5).

This was only due to the meeting of the angelic with the human: for this reason Gabriel, peace be upon him, would appear to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in human form, without the dust of travel on him and unknown to anyone, as he came to the Messenger of Allah while he was in a gathering of the Companions, asking him about Islam, faith and excellence (6).

So: the matter of the pause and interruption of revelation for a period from the Messenger of Allah was intended by Allah so that the Messenger of Allah might rest from the hardship of revelation until the pain and fatigue left him, and then he would long for revelation anew, it would become easier for him to bear, and he would become accustomed to receiving it from the angel. A person's longing for a thing makes him bear hardships in its pursuit and makes difficulties easy for him, like one who walks toward his beloved and does not mind even if he walks on thorns, or if fears and dangers confront him.

Revelation is a meeting of the human with the angelic: either the Messenger rises to the rank of the angel, or the angel descends to the rank of the human. This closeness had not yet occurred at the beginning of the revelation, so it exhausted the Messenger of Allah, and he needed this rest through the cessation of revelation.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We relieved you of your burden, which had weighed upon your back﴾ [Ash-Sharh: 2-3], that is, We made it light so that it would not exhaust you. And in response to them He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it covers, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]﴾ [Ad-Duha: 1-3].

It is strange that they said, "Muhammad's Lord has forsaken him," thereby acknowledging the Lord of Muhammad at the moment of hardship and distress that befell him; they gloated over him until they said, "Muhammad's Lord has abandoned him." Then, when his Lord reached him with revelation and called them to faith, they disbelieved and denied.

1 He is Habib ibn Aws al-Ta'i, born in a village of al-Sham (180 AH), raised in modest circumstances, working as a boy for a weaver. He died in 231 AH at the age of 51.
2 Al-mathal al-shurud: that which departs from what is familiar and customary. Al-nada: generosity and bounty. Al-bas: strength and war.
3 Al-nibras: lamp and lantern. Al-mishkat: a niche in a wall of the house that is not a window; in our villages it is known as "al-taqa," with the qaf pronounced as a hamza.
4 From Jundab ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Bajali, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) became ill and did not get up for a night or two. A woman came and said: "O Muhammad, I do not see your devil except that he has forsaken you." So Allah revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it covers, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]﴾ [Ad-Duha]. Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim. In another narration Jundab said: Gabriel was delayed coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the polytheists said: "Muhammad's Lord has forsaken him." Related by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4/522).
5 ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "I saw him (ﷺ) when revelation descended upon him on an extremely cold day, and it would leave him, and his forehead would be dripping with sweat." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, Book of the Beginning of Revelation. Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (1/21): "He likened his forehead to a vein that has been bled, as an exaggeration of the abundance of sweat." Al-fasd is cutting a vein to let blood flow.
6 From ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one day, a man appeared before us with extremely white clothing and extremely black hair, with no trace of travel visible on him, and none of us knew him. He sat before the Prophet (ﷺ), leaned his knees against his knees, placed his palms on his thighs, and said: 'O Muhammad, tell me about Islam' (he answered), 'tell me about faith' (he answered), 'tell me about excellence' (he answered), 'tell me about the Hour' (he answered)." ʿUmar said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you know who the questioner is?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It was Gabriel; he came to teach you your religion." Related by Muslim in his Sahih, Book of Faith, and similarly al-Bukhari in his Sahih (50), but from the hadith of Abu Hurayra.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 30, verse 59:

His saying, glorified be He: ﴿Thus...﴾ (59) [al-Rum], meaning: like their denial of every sign that comes to them. ﴿Allah sets a seal upon the hearts of those who do not know﴾ (59) [al-Rum], meaning He sealed them and closed them.

If you say: is it not in the interest that their hearts remain open, so that they might receive some guidance and light? We say: sealing the hearts of these people does not happen except after all the means of da'wah (calling to the faith) have been exhausted. When they did not respond, there is no hope in their guidance and no benefit in their hearing.

The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, is the Lord who helps His servant to what he loves and grants him his desire, even if it is disbelief. These people wanted disbelief and loved it, so Allah helped them to what they wanted and sealed their hearts so that no faith enters them and no disbelief departs from them.

For this reason we have previously warned those afflicted with calamities, or those who lose a beloved one, warning them not to perpetuate grief and not to become accustomed to it, lest God agree with you in your desire for grief and your passion for it, so that sorrows follow one another and calamities succeed one another. Beware of leaving the door of grief ajar; rather, close it with the nail of contentment (ridha), for if grief remains with you, it will leave you no beloved.

And likewise we say: if a person turns away from you, do not remember him yourself; rather, help him to abandon you, and assist him by not remembering him.

If you say: if the Truth, glorified be He, has described them as those who do not know, why then does He seal their hearts, and why does He call them to account? We say: because lack of knowledge is the result of their own negligence. The Truth, glorified be He, established for them the proofs and the cosmic signs indicating His existence, exalted be He, but they did not reflect upon these signs, nor did they reason from the proofs to the existence of the Creator, the Capable, glorified be He, and the necessity of conveying (the message) from Allah. Therefore, their lack of knowledge is the result of their heedlessness and negligence.

But then, after they denied the messengers and rejected the signs, does the course of the da'wah stop because they plugged their ears against it? Allah created the universe and scattered in it signs that point to the existence of the One, the Unique God, and placed in it miracles that establish the truthfulness of the messengers in conveying from Allah. The Truth, glorified be He, does not benefit from these signs, because His dominion does not increase by our obedience nor decrease by our disobedience; the matter returns to us first and last. Therefore, the resolution of this matter: leave these deniers, O Muhammad, and remain steadfast in what you are upon.

Then Allah, Glorified and Exalted, says: ﴿So be patient. Surely the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you light-hearted.﴾ (30:60)

Be patient in the face of their aversion, be patient in the face of their obstinacy and enmity, and be patient in the face of their harm to you and to those who believe in you. Be patient in all of this, for the outcome is in your favour. ﴿Surely the promise of Allah is true...﴾ (30:60) Allah has promised His messengers victory and triumph, and the promise of Allah is true, so be assured that victory is coming.

But if victory is coming, why this conflict between the believers and the disbelievers? And why all this hardship and toil in the way of the call (da'wah)? They say: because Allah wishes to test (yumahhis) the followers of Muhammad and to train them to bear the trust of the call and the torch of light after the Messenger of Allah, not only for the people of the Arabian Peninsula, but for the whole universe.

So they must be among those of firmness upon the principle, whom hardships do not shake. The proof of this is that they are harmed and persecuted, yet they remain patient, and this is the most important quality of those who prepare to bear the trust.

For this reason we say: if you see a method or a principle that showers its adherents with benefits first, know that it is a false principle, for the true principle is one for whose sake its people sacrifice their lives and their wealth; they give before they receive. Why? Because the adherent of a false principle will find no one to support his falsehood unless he first entices them with money and buys their consciences; otherwise, what would compel him to a false principle and drive him to follow it? Therefore, the price must be collected first.

As for the true principle, its adherent knows that the reward is deferred to the Hereafter; he is promised things beyond this world, which he believes in and works for, so his soul becomes light to him and his wealth becomes light to him in the cause of this principle.

In the journey of the call, we saw many fall away into apostasy when a sign or a shock struck the Messenger of Allah and shook the people, as if hardship were a sieve that distinguishes these from those, so that none remains under the banner of there is no god but Allah except the brave and strong, capable of carrying this banner to the whole world.

So Allah says to His Prophet: be patient in the face of their denial, their rejection, and their plotting against you, for We are your supporters and will never abandon you. This support was made clear to you when they opposed you openly and you prevailed over their openness, and when they plotted against you in secret and you prevailed over their plotting; they even sought the help of the jinn to corrupt your affair, but Allah exposed their scheme and saved you from them.

So be reassured: We are watching them, and We will never hand you over. Indeed, We will show you what they deserve of punishment in this world, which you will see with your own eyes, or in the Hereafter after your death: ﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you back, to Us they will be returned.﴾ (40:77)

Among this punishment that came down upon them in this world and that our master, the Messenger of Allah, saw, is what befell them on the Day of Badr of killing, capture and dispersal. We have said that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and what could make you know what ʿUmar is, since the Qur'an would descend in accordance with his opinion. Nevertheless, when there was revealed: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs.﴾ (54:45), he was astonished and said: What multitude is this that will be routed, when we are unable even to protect ourselves? Then when Badr came and he saw what he saw, he said: Allah has spoken truly: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs.﴾ (54:45).

As for Allah's saying: ﴿Surely the promise of Allah is true...﴾ (30:60), al-wa'd (promise) is the announcement of a good not yet arrived in its time. There is a difference between a promise of good from a human being and a promise from Allah, Exalted. Your promise may fail, because you are a son of changing circumstances, and you do not possess all the elements of fulfilling a promise; perhaps when the time of fulfilment comes you will not be able to do it, or your soul will change toward it and you will become stingy with it, or you will see that it does not deserve it, and so on.

So: the changes that befall you, or befall him, or befall the value of the good you render, exist, and they may come between you and the fulfilment of what you promised.

For this reason, Allah, Glorified, teaches us to take precaution in this matter, saying: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed I will do that tomorrow," (18:23) except [with the phrase] "If Allah wills."﴾ (18:24) So tie your action to the will of Allah, who makes the action possible for you, and you should not be certain of anything whose causes you do not possess in any way.

We say: suppose you said, "I will meet you tomorrow at such-and-such a place, and I will give you such-and-such," you have said this statement and made this promise while you cannot guarantee that you will live until tomorrow, nor guarantee that your companion will live. Even if you both live until tomorrow, your opinion may change, or something may befall you that prevents you from fulfilling it. So your saying "if Allah wills" protects you from being described as a liar in case of non-fulfilment, because you promised and Allah did not will it, so the matter is not in your hands.

Then from whom does the true promise come? From the One who possesses every means of fulfilment, and whom no obstacle prevents.

And Allah's saying: ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you light-hearted.﴾ (30:60) To make a thing khaffa means it no longer has weight; istakhaffa another means to ask him to be light-hearted. For example, when you are harsh with a person, another comes and says to you: "Ease off on him" (khuff ʿanhu). And istakhaffahu is like istafazzahu, meaning: he moved him and shook him from his steadfastness, so if he was sitting, for instance, he leapt up standing.

Therefore we say in such situations: "Be firm (khalīk thaqīl)... so-and-so is provoking you (yastafziz), meaning he wants to drive you out of your forbearance and steadfastness... don't become light (mutbaqash khafīf)... etc." and we say to a boy: "Fiz", meaning stand up, rise. And from it is Allah's saying: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, and attack them with your cavalry and your infantry.﴾ (17:64)¹

So the meaning of istakhaffahu is: to make him light, to cause him to move away from the steadfastness he is in.

The meaning then: beware, O Muhammad, lest the people provoke you or drive you out of your steadfastness, so that you clash with them; but remain steadfast in your call and do not worry, for Allah has promised you victory, and the promise of Allah is true. When Allah, Glorified, lets the reins go slack to those who disbelieve in Him, He only wants to bring out all that is in them, so that they have no excuse left; then He confronts them with some of what He has, of what they deserve in this world, and the rest they will see in the Hereafter.

And Allah says: ﴿And已 Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed they would be the ones given victory, and indeed Our soldiers would be the victorious.﴾ (37:171–173)

From the biography of Imam ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him and honour his face, we learn that he was tested by two groups: the Khawārij, who declared him a disbeliever, and the Shīʿa, who deified him and raised him to the rank of prophethood, so that the saying of the Messenger of Allah came true concerning him: "Two will perish because of you: one who loves excessively, and one who hates and speaks ill."² (3)

It is reported⁽⁴⁾ that one day he, may Allah be pleased with him, was leading the people in the dawn prayer, and when he recited "wa lā'l-ḍāllīn" (and not of those who are astray), one of the Khawārij drew near to him and recited: ﴿Indeed it has been revealed to you and to those before you: If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers.﴾ (39:65), wanting to say to him: you are a disbeliever and your deeds will not be accepted.

ʿAlī quickly perceived what the man intended, and immediately after it he recited: ﴿So be patient. Surely the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you light-hearted.﴾ (30:60), meaning: you will not move me from my steadfastness and forbearance, and you will not provoke me.

The greatness in this situation is that he responded at once with the healing word from the Book of Allah without prior preparation or arrangement, and why not, since he was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who was given a long reach in eloquence, rhetoric and argument.

The meaning of ﴿those who have no certainty﴾ (30:60) derives from yaqīn, which is firm faith that does not waver, so that it becomes a conviction in the heart that does not rise to the intellect to be debated anew.
